# BOOK II OF GUILLAUME POSTEL

...[he] has commanded the elements and demons, whose words and doctrine are clearly consistent with his deeds, tending entirely toward the benefit of one's neighbor, the improvement of man, and the knowledge of God, containing nothing contrary or repugnant to the laws that have been received. Let us contrast this man with one educated in trade, accustomed to fraud (which a greedy merchant must altogether commit) in buying and selling, laboring in both mind and body even unto madness and the loss of his senses; one who, for the entire course of his life—at least twenty-three years—seized the property of others by the law of an enemy, and from a very poor man became a powerful tyrant. If he gave anything away, he stole it from another’s property; he never performed a single noble or honest deed in his life; he was ruled by all pleasures and converted everything to his own utility. His law, finally, is very much like his life—namely, full of slaughter and lies, and stuffed with entirely contradictory opinions. By natural judgment, I ask you: to whose prescriptions would you rather subscribe? Should those two laws even be seen as equal? I accept both as men: both Christ and Muhammad. 

Now, if I grant to Christ those things which Muhammad willingly conceded to him—that he was conceived of the Holy Spirit, born of a virgin, spoke immediately from the womb, conversed in his cradle, and animated birds made of clay with only his breath after he had fashioned them with his fingers <note>original: *aues ex luto solo flatu animauisse*. This refers to a miracle of Jesus found in the Quran (3:49) and the apocryphal Infancy Gospel of Thomas, but not in the canonical Gospels.</note>; and if I add the innocence of his followers, who in their teacher’s name drank all poisons without harm, trod upon asps unhurt, and were not weakened by the bite of vipers, and who performed all kinds of miracles for the needs of men, all preferring to lose their lives rather than the truth—what will one think when comparing them with the followers of the other lawmaker? Those followers were seditiously killed, thirty in succession, because of greed and the lust for ruling; and their descendants not infrequently kill fifteen, twenty, or thirty of their own brothers out of a desire for the throne. Will one not judge their laws similarly, as being equally conducive to salvation? Let both the impious and the followers of Muhammad <note>original: *Muhamedici*</note> weigh these things carefully, and let them finally enter into the distinction between light and darkness, between salvation and perdition, and follow whichever they wish.

<margin>cc cc</margin>
Let us proceed. "And when we began your faith and certainty (O Jews), we elevated the mountain over you, in case you should be afraid." <note>A reference to Quran 2:63, which describes God raising Mount Sinai over the Israelites.</note> Where is that mountain in the Holy Scriptures? When the Law was given, and the children of Israel could not endure the divine lightning, they were ordered to withdraw to the side of the mountain so that they might not see, but could still hear. Thus, Muhammad—as if God were unable to place a cloud before their sight—placed a mountain hanging in the air over a hundred thousand people. He seems to satisfy the dispute of the Jews in this place. For they argue greatly about how it could happen that the people, placed near the mountain at its base, saw less when they were closer. Moses had done this at their request, because they said they could not endure the majesty of the portents. From this, certain <term>Rabbis</term> <note>Jewish scholars and teachers of the Law.</note> say that the mountain was necessarily hollowed out and suspended so that the people might withdraw into it. They are occupied with a very simple matter, for they do not know, or seem not to know, that the further you are from a very high mountain (provided you do not go beyond the power of sight), the more clearly the things happening on its summit appear; and the closer you come to the roots, the less the peak appears. Since the signs of divine majesty terrified those for whose sake they appeared—so much so that they could not even endure the sight of Moses—it was necessary to satisfy them, give the law, and also show how it was given. Therefore, if the people had moved further away from the place, they would neither have seen nor heard those wonders. But since Moses wanted them to be confirmed by at least one of the senses, he led the people to that place where, if they did not see, they would at least hear the thunders and the horrendous crash of the voice. For Moses, whom many have mimicked <note>original: *cuius simiæ multifacti sunt*, literally "of whom many have been made monkeys/apes."</note>, was not like other lawmakers. For all of them, by withdrawing from the common people, sought divine conversations in caves, in temples, in places in which...

### ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

...[lies] so that they could neither be heard nor seen. But last of all, Muhammad added the finale of the play <note>original: *catastrophen fabulæ*. Postel uses theatrical language to imply that Muhammad’s revelations were a staged performance.</note> with his cave and the angel Gabriel. Moses, it is true, withdrew alone, but he did so in such a way that hundreds of thousands of people could not help but be stirred by those wonders which appeared on that mountain while he remained there. These things were seen and heard not just by one or two impostors who might serve the plot, but by more than a million people—for six hundred thousand men capable of bearing arms had departed from Egypt—and those of the most stubborn sort <note>original: *ceruicossissimis*, literally "stiff-necked," a common Biblical epithet for the Israelites.</note>. Thus, Muhammad has acted as an interpreter for the Jewish doctors with his "aerial mountain" <note>Postel likely refers to the Quranic tradition (Sura 2:63) where Mount Sinai is said to have been lifted above the Israelites.</note>. I have chosen to hand down these matters at somewhat greater length for the sake of certain impious men, and to propose this distinction to those sitting on the **Machiavellian throne** <note>A reference to political pragmatists who viewed religion merely as a tool for statecraft rather than divine truth.</note>, so that they may weigh it carefully.

What shall I add concerning the **Cow**, whose title this Syrian <note>Postel often uses "Syrian" or "Arab" interchangeably for Islamic texts.</note> book bears? How many fables does he weave from a single passage in the sacrifice of Numbers 19? Everything is to be laughed at and hissed off the stage. The people make Moses ask God what the cow is. Moses fears he is being a fool; the people ask that God be consulted as to its nature and its color, and that a similar cow be provided—all of which are absent from the Sacred Scripture. Therefore, Muhammad, it is necessary that you be a liar, since you possess fables and manifest falsehoods that contravene the Old Testament. In this, we Christians agree with the Hebrews; do not say that their texts are corrupted and yours are intact. For it is the refuge of Muhammadan victory, when they are pressed, to claim that our texts have been corrupted. Greeks, Latins, Hebrews, Syrians, Armenians, Jacobites, and even Samaritans agree in their copies against you, O **Muslim** <note>original: *Mussulman*.</note>. Since there are as many errors and lies in the Quran as there are words (except in so far as you follow our own texts), it follows that this law is the invention of an abominable demon. I add nothing more of that same fable, for it is too long and refutes itself by its own absurdity.

When the follies of this law had been detected by **Abdallah Ben Salon** the Jew <note>Abdullah ibn Salam, a companion of Muhammad who converted from Judaism; Postel claims here that he manipulated the revelations for seven years.</note> (who, as I said above, inverted the things he received for seven whole years) and he had revealed this to the others, that "prophet" cried out, after saying many false things regarding the law of the Hebrews:

> Woe to those who write the book with their own hands, and then say, "This is from God," so that they may doubt it for a little while. He terrifies the one who had changed the text, and the others to whom he gave the pamphlets to be learned by heart. Because if they changed them, he did not notice it, since his dreams did not return to his mind; thus, being unable to restore the things they had forgotten, he was covered in great shame. Yet he would say: "Though you change it, God is not changed; and though you change this covenant of God, his covenant is not changed." Now, therefore, he rises up against the Jews and says:

These things were written in favor of Christ to provoke the envy of the Jews. Thus truth, whether envy likes it or not, comes forth even among lies. You see that Christ—against whom he nevertheless writes—is granted the wisdom of God, and conceived of the Holy Spirit, yet was called a liar and finally even killed. For so he seems to imply, even though elsewhere he contradicts this. He adds against the Jews:

### GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II.

...[revealed] openly, that is, made manifest by God against the ungodly; nevertheless, when that which they recognized came to them, they defected from him, and the curse of God is upon the ungodly. He <note>Muhammad</note> involves himself in divine imprecations, yet continues to claim his law was sent from heaven, against which they <note>the Jews</note> oppose their own; for this reason, he reproaches them even now for the slaughter of the prophets.

Shortly thereafter, he states that whoever is an adversary of Gabriel and Michael will be an enemy of God, and such a person will be ungodly. It is as if it were a confessed fact that angels had come to Muhammad, who was merely concealing his **falling sickness** <note>original: *morbum fonticū*. This term refers to epilepsy; historical critics of Muhammad often interpreted his prophetic trances as physical seizures.</note>. 

But it is worthwhile to hear the theology of this lawmaker: "Follow what you read," [he says], "concerning the demons under King Solomon, and how Solomon acted impiously." And for this reason, the demons are impious, for teaching men incantations. In this passage, he seems to turn Solomon’s impiety and incantations into a disgrace, even though Solomon was a Jew. Indeed, he says (to make this more clear) in the following sections that Solomon had the service of demons, by whose diligence he accomplished everything in the blink of an eye. He claims that they were unaware of Solomon's death; when his household had placed him, deceased, upon his throne and he had leaned upon his staff, the demons never realized he was dead until a worm gnawed through his staff and he collapsed; then, astonished and wailing, they departed. 

These are the man's marvelous dreams, which he claims are written among the Jews so that they might read them. Perhaps he is noting the opinion of **Josephus** <note>Titus Flavius Josephus, a 1st-century Romano-Jewish historian.</note>, who says in his *Antiquities* that Solomon possessed the art of compelling demons and left it to his descendants, so that some used it even to his own memory to force demons to depart from possessed bodies. Certainly, it was granted to the scribes by divine power to put to flight and cast out demons. You see how excellently this lawmaker understands the power of demons, whom he makes ignorant even of the past and of visible things. Yet, that Solomon was an enchanter is not found in the Sacred Scriptures, nor can it be read there. 

I proceed. "And what was sent from heaven concerning the angels **Harot and Marot** in Babylon." It is fitting to know what these things mean. The interpreters and the book *Hassiar* <note>Likely referring to the *Siyar*, or biographies of the Prophet.</note> explain it in this way: When the angels Harot and Marot were judges in Babylon, they were seized by love for a certain noble woman. She refused to yield to them except on this condition: that one of them should lead her into Paradise and the other bring her back. Captivated and drunk with wine, they promised; they enjoyed her, and they led her into Paradise. Upon seeing her, God turned her into the morning star <note>original: *stellam luciferum*</note>. To the drunken and deceitful angels, He gave a choice: whether they would prefer to suffer punishment in this present world or in the world to come. They chose this present life and were led to punishment at the place where they had committed the crime; they are suspended in a well in Babylon until the Day of Judgment. 

This is the story. Muhammad’s angels are corporeal, prone to vice, and capable of physical punishment. However, I have never read or seen elsewhere of angels serving as judges in cities. This story must certainly please the Arab women, as it teaches that one may earn Paradise and a position as a star through sexual intercourse. O, laws and stories worthy of their author! 

Shortly after, in order to draw everyone to himself, he says that all laws are good for one who lives well and observes those ceremonies he instituted. These tend toward the same purpose as before: so that having captured everyone, he may initiate them into his own following. Meanwhile, he does not notice that he is saying his own law is no better than the laws of the idolaters; thus he wastes his effort and lies, for it is not authored by God. From this it follows that it is the law of the devil, which suggests that the devil and God are equals. 

"Those who do not understand say: 'Unless God speaks to us and gives us a sign [we will not believe].'" Those who were before them said similar things; their speech was like their hearts. "But now we have declared miracles to an innocent people. We have sent the announcement and the warning to you in truth, and it was not sought by a damned people." When miracles were demanded of him, he eluded them in this way; for his followers said, "Unless we see..."

### ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

He <note>Muhammad</note> says, "We do not believe in the God who speaks with you, as it seemed when **Moses** ascended the mountain; you and your fathers have always demanded miracles in this way." I ask, when did the Jews demand miracles from **Moses**, since he had already begun to terrify both his own people and the Egyptians with wonders? He showed them, of his own accord, that divine power was present with him. When did they ask **Christ**, who was hated by the **Pharisees** for the very reason that he performed miracles everywhere? And when they could object to nothing else, they said that he ought not to heal on the Sabbath. You cannot give laws from any others except **Christ** and **Moses**. **Christ**, indeed, when asked twice for the sake of their curiosity—once by the **Pharisees** and once by **Herod**—did not perform one; for he knew they sought it with an evil heart, not for the sake of believing, but for the sake of pleasure. Before **Herod**, he remained silent, though he was already about to be sacrificed; he restrained the wickedness and curiosity of the **Pharisees** and scribes, who did not believe despite a hundred miracles and the thousands upon thousands of people who had seen them, yet they asked for more nonetheless. And he said to that evil and adulterous generation of scribes that no other sign would be given greater than his rising again after three days, just as **Jonah** was once cast out alive from the fish on the third day. But he who says that the announcement is not sought by a damned people brings this forward with a general and indefinite term, so that he might even attach his own persuasion, which no one was receiving, to sacred things; it is as if he were saying, "The damned did not want to receive those good laws, and therefore they are damned; so too, whoever does not receive mine shall be damned." An excellent inference! As if his law were already divine simply because it was called so by him. It follows:

> And the Jew or the Christian will not be pleased with you until you follow their prescription. Say: "The direction of God is the direction," and do not follow their desire in place of that which has come to you from the knowledge you have from God, etc.

From this it is clear how he had his first followers from among the Christians, **Nestorians**, and Jews, and in what way each group wanted to draw him into their own law. For he did not please the Jew if he were a Christian, and vice versa. Therefore, he attempts to elude both with an "excellent" syllogism familiar to him. "There is no direction of God," he says, "except the direction." What does this imply? A stone is nothing but a stone; a man is nothing but a man; there is no God except God, or besides God. It implies nothing at all, and yet he wanted the initiation of his sect to be confirmed by this phrase: "There is no god but God" <note>original: "la alla illa alla," a phonetic rendering of the Arabic Shahada, *La ilaha illa Allah*</note>. As if anyone would demonstrate a point in such a way, or affect a joined notion of things by saying the same thing twice! The Jew and the Christian believe these things: that the direction of God is nothing but the direction of God, and that God is nothing but God. But for the sake of enticing the common people, he used this indefinite phrasing; and when the great and the skilled assented to it, he later used the same word among the unlearned to stand for his own personal persuasion alone—placing that which is common to all in its stead—and he drew the <term>idiotas</term> <note>simple or unlearned people</note> to <term>hudan</term> <note>Arabic: *huda*, meaning guidance or direction</note>, which is the name the **Quran** obtained. A little later, when he says:

> O children of **Israel**, remember my benefit with which I benefited you; I gave you good things and ordained you over all peoples; fear the day when a soul shall not be repaid for a soul, and justice shall not be received from another, and redemption shall not follow it, nor shall they be liberated.

He again hunts for the Jews and rises up against **Christ** and our justification, which I have nonetheless shown, by necessary arguments in the first book, that **Christ** gave to his followers and saints. For it was made clear enough there that a human being, by himself, can never be justified. Since in all the ages from the creation of the world until **Christ** there were scarcely ten men to whom miracles were granted, how could it be that hundreds of thousands of millions of people—more than can be numbered—could have flourished with every kind of miracle in a short span of time, unless they had been endowed with a justice, power, and force other than human? If those things were from man, then **Muhammad** and other men ought to have had them; but since they do not have them, and those others had them...

...[they] had, so many and such great ones in a single century, especially during those 500 years, and up to our own times, even in many places, it follows that it is and was of the righteousness of others and of **Christ**. ...servant for servant, woman for woman, etc. All of these matters Christ wished us to refer back to the duty of judgment. Indeed, he even instituted a fast according to the custom of the ancestors, lest he should fail to **Judaize**; yet he permits it to be exchanged for alms, so that he might flatter everyone. He says:

> In the month of **Ramadan**, in which the **Quran** itself descended for the guidance of men, and the wisdom of the guidance of the **Furqan** <note>original: "Alphurcan." A term from the Quran meaning "the criterion" or "differentiation" between truth and falsehood.</note>; whoever among you is able during that month, let him fast; and whoever is sick or on a journey, he shall postpone the number of days, as God will advise.

In this place, it is clear that before **Muhammad**, there was no **Quran** or **Furqan**. From this it appears, as I noted above, that **Muhammad** spoke a manifest lie when he said it was given to **Moses**. Truly, we must look at the **Quranic** fast.

> And it is permitted to you during the fast to be with your wives. For God is merciful. Eat and drink, until the white line (that is, the dawn) appears to you amidst the shadows; then begin the fast again.

An "excellent" fast indeed, and one worthy of its author! In it, the night—which is given for rest and meditation—is turned entirely toward "crapula" <note>A Latin term for excessive drinking or the resulting hangover; here used to imply gluttony.</note> and a life worthy not of a man, but of brutes. As if the fast were given so that you might abstain during the day only to gorge yourself at night, rather than to mortify the flesh. The truth is that in this fast, two types of people had to be satisfied: he instituted the fast at the beginning of his persuasion so that he might seem to fast according to the custom of the **Hebrews** and **Christians**; but so that he might accommodate himself and those **Arabs** like him, who were corrupted by luxury and **Venus** <note>A common Renaissance metaphor for sexual desire or activity.</note> and accompanied by a multitude of wives, he wished the reins of gluttony and excess to be loosened all night long. This was so that their strength might satisfy **Venus**, lest this prophet—who boasted that he had from God the sexual vigor of forty strong men—should suffer from thinness and be forced to cease from such a "noble" gift. Who does not see that this impious, pagan **Epicurean**, under the feigned name of piety, foisted himself upon the simplicity of unrefined men?

A little later he speaks again of war, saying that those who die in it will be most happy, provided they believe in him; and that all who oppose them must be killed until they submit. What kind of "prophetic virtue" is this? What tyrant, robber, or murderer would not similarly encourage his followers? Such things are far removed from the gift of prophecy. But he was in <term>alhigera</term> <note>The Hijra, or Hegira: the migration of Muhammad and his followers from Mecca to Medina in 622 AD, marking the start of the Islamic calendar.</note>, that is, in exile. He had earned this through his factions, and for that reason, he was arming himself against the citizens of **Mecca**. From this, it is likely that this chapter, although it is not stated where it was written, was nevertheless written in **Medina**; for he arms himself with the favor of the citizens of the **Jews** (of whom there were many in **Yathrib** <note>original: "Iezrab." The ancient name for Medina.</note>), whose labor he easily utilized along with the rustics, because they were most ready for plunder. He says, therefore, that those adversaries in the temple of **Mecca** must be killed just as they previously killed his own people in the same temple. This is explained more at length elsewhere. However, so that the cause might seem more just, he tells the soldier that there is the <term>Elheg</term> <note>The Hajj: the annual Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca.</note>, that is, the pilgrimage, in which they fasted for three days, and seven upon their return—so that religion might cover his vice. > And they will ask about wine and the recreation of the hive <note>original: "aluei recreatione." Likely referring to *maysir*, or games of chance/gambling, which were often played by drawing lots or arrows.</note>. Say: in those things is a grave sin, and a help for men: but the sin is greater than the benefit.

He condemns gambling and wine: the former, lest the soldier become preoccupied and he be unable to rule him. Because he was personally troubled by wine, he prohibited this most excellent gift of nature so that others would not be different from himself. And even if many gluttons and drunkards ruin themselves with it, nevertheless, for recreating weary bodies and even afflicted minds, nothing greater was ever born. He acted thus so that a most excellent part of nature might be missing among his followers, and a most abundant harvest lost, all to conceal his own illness and to gratify his wife. What he adds concerning the laws of divorce, and concerning lawful oaths, and concerning bringing war upon his own citizens—since all those things are against public peace, opposed to equity, goodness, and honesty, and moreover fight against divine law—therefore they need no other refutation than...

...by themselves. But the **Muhammadan** <note>original: "Muhamedicus." A term used by Postel to refer to followers of Islam.</note> will say, "there are many good things in these precepts"; for who would have wanted to receive such a massive pile of apparent absurdities unless some truth and goodness were mixed in? There is indeed some good, though very little, in the **Quran** <note>original: "Alcorano"</note>; but in the **Gospel**, which he admits is from God, there is nothing that is not absolutely perfect and most worthy of its divine author. 

He takes a pretext for war from the children of Israel, when they pursued the lost **Canaanites**. And yet he persecutes the Jews, whose law he approves; he kills the Christians, whose **Gospel** he says is from God; he sheds the blood of citizens, even while he seems to do the same as the Israelite cohorts did with **Saul**. Indeed, he mentions Saul so that his followers might establish a leader—not Saul himself, but **Abu Bakr** and **Umar** <note>original: "Vbecharū & Ahmerum." The first two Caliphs and successors to Muhammad.</note>, most audacious and desperate men, from whom he might receive a pacified power. After he has spoken of **Talut** <note>original: "Talot." The Quranic name for King Saul.</note> (for so he calls Saul), he proceeds with absurdities regarding **Goliath**. But I almost passed over the fable attached to the history of Saul; he says:

> "When Saul had brought his cohorts into order, he said: 'If God makes you pass through a river, he who drinks from it is not of mine, or from me; and he who does not eat is from me, except for him who shall scoop a handful with his hand.' And they drank from it, except for a few. For he did not cross over, nor those who believed with him, because the enemies were in that place and fortune, so that victory could be had over them."

**Saul** had issued a curse <note>Postel is referencing the account in 1 Samuel 14:24.</note> that if anyone touched any food that day, he would be cursed—that is, he would die. Saul's son **Jonathan** was not present then, but was pursuing the enemies he had fiercely attacked. By chance, he touched a little dewy honey with the tip of his rod, which frequently tends to drip from the sky in **Syria**. For this reason, he was made subject to the **anathema** <note>term: anathema. A formal curse or person consigned to damnation; here, a death sentence for breaking a religious oath.</note> and was sought for death by his father because of the oath. However, the multitude resisted his attempts, saying it was unworthy for him to be dragged to death by whose labor and diligence they had obtained the victory. 

For **Jonathan** was not the cause of the calamities, but rather the imprudent father and leader who had foolishly bound the people by a religious oath in a time of great necessity. If the people had been allowed to drink and eat and regain their strength, they would have brought back an absolute victory, having completely finished off the enemies; nor would they have eaten meat with the blood in extreme hunger, contrary to the divine precept. 

Now let the lies this scoundrel <note>original: "nebulo." Postel frequently uses disparaging terms for Muhammad.</note> told be compared. "If you cross the river, he who drinks of it is not of mine, except as much as a hand can hold. All drank except a few." First, he turns food into drink; he introduces a river where honey is the subject; he says everyone failed except a few, when not even one person departed nor went against the commands, except for **Jonathan**, who (as I said) had not heard them. There are as many lies as there are words. 

Yet we do not know to what end these things lead: because he was embarking upon a religious pilgrimage—that is, the slaughter of all good men—he wanted his own people to be bound by similar laws so they would not desert him, and so that, devoted to death or vengeance, they would rush forward before taking food. In the meantime, he was abusing sacred examples to encourage and terrify them. He could have written this accurately among so many learned Jews, but he did not want his cunning to be open to anyone. Furthermore, he wanted his sacred things to be entirely like himself—that is, sprinkled with lies—lest, while they seemed true, they might be attributed to their original authors. 

Regarding **Jalut** <note>original: "Galot." The Quranic name for Goliath.</note>, that is, **Goliath**, he does exactly the same thing when he makes him a general in that war; whereas one does not read that he was a general, nor was he in that war, but after the forces of the **Palestinians** <note>Postel refers to the Philistines.</note> were restored a long time later, he challenged the Jews as a common soldier. Finally, he adds things worthy of himself: that wars ought to exist among men lest the world be corrupted. No greater plague can be compared to war among men, and yet he says war exists so that the world is not corrupted, and that this is God’s benefit upon the earth. If God said those things, I appeal to you, O **Nature**, who places the happiness of all things in rest and tranquility. Who taught you thus, if not that God, who is the highest and perfect rest? Yet this prophet makes Him the author of the "benefit" of war.

...since among all men, unless one is insane, not a single person can be found who would approve of war in word, even if he occasionally approves of it in deed. The envy of the demon, the wickedness of men, the stubbornness of matter, and corruption stir up war, with God permitting all things so that we might come to our senses; and meanwhile, with **Muhammad** <note>original: "Muhamede"</note> as the author, God gives us this same war as a supreme good, so that the prophet might grow rich and take possession of things. Who does not know that robbers and tyrants, and those who lie in wait for the lives of others, approve of such things? And that they banish peace from the world as much as they can? It is for this reason that he says so frequently that riches belong to God, and that He gives them to whom He wills, so that, evidently, he who has swooped down upon another’s wealth—acquired through great sweat—might have an equal right to those things as he who is their just possessor. This is the "good" prophecy of Muhammad, and meanwhile, he seriously affirms that this is a sign of his prophethood.

->These, he says, are truly the miracles of God read before you, because you are a prophet.<-

<margin>« (Postel uses these marks to highlight specific points of critique regarding the text's logic)</margin>
These things are connected to the preceding passages, which say that unless men attacked one another by a mutual impulse, the earth would be petrified. But I shall approach other matters. He says: "We have ordained certain such prophets over others; some of them God addressed, and some He raised up by certain degrees. And we gave wisdom to Christ, the son of Mary, and we created him from the Holy Spirit; and if God willed, those who came after them, after wisdom had come to them, would not have killed one another. And therefore they dispute, and among them are those who believe, and among them are those who believe poorly; and if God willed, they would not be killed. But God does what He wills." I do not know what I should examine first. What he has already granted to Christ, I do not think needs to be repeated. When he says, "if God willed, He would not kill those who are after them," he understands "those after the prophets." The God of the **Quran** <note>original: "Alcorani"</note> is a murderer who kills those whom He chooses as prophets. Man does no evil, nor does he have free will: therefore, God kills men through the tyrants of the world. O nefarious sentiment, worthy of a thousand punishments! Some people used to disagree; among our people there were **Nestorians**, **Jacobites**, and Christians <note>Postel refers to the diverse Christian sects in the East; Nestorians and Jacobites held different views on the nature of Christ</note>. A judge ignorant of both causes had to be appointed as an arbiter. And because he was helped by the favor and benefits of **Bahira** <note>original: "Baheira." A legendary monk said by Christian polemicists to have taught Muhammad</note>, therefore the Jacobites and Nestorians "believe best." This is his reasoning for agreement. Petty kings and robbers from among the Armenians, coming into the borders of Arabia—since dog does not eat dog—once a "prophetic peace" was settled, were said to "believe well," being most worthy of that judge. Because a tyrant and a robber lacked supporters, and could not carry out a profitable war with those like himself (for there is neither ample plunder from a robber, nor an easy victory), once peace was settled with them and the dogmas were firmed up, while "hand rubs hand," the plague crept into the whole world. Indeed, as to what he says in the last place—"if God willed, they would not be killed"—what else might the most monstrous murderer say, even mockingly, while he slaughters everyone without regard for humanity? If God wills those things, then He is no longer God. For if He is unjust, He is nothing. Therefore He does not will it, O destruction of men! He does not will what He permits to human **free will** <note>original: "liberum arbitrium"</note>. But He wants the actions themselves to be done by us sincerely and holily; yet even if we wish to commit evils, He permits it—He does not will it. Even if this permission seems like an evil, it would be far worse for all men to lack free will and be like a stone, rather than being unable to commit vices, since this is specifically the grounds for punishment and reward—a fact you confess in words and assert, but deny in your life. A little later he says that God gave the kingdom to **Abraham** <note>original: "Abrahæ"</note> himself, and that he possessed it. For he did not use the word *Vaada* <note>original: "Vaada." Translating from the Arabic root *wa'ada*, meaning "to promise"</note>, which means "to promise," but *attha* <note>original: "attha." Translating from the Arabic root *ata*, meaning "to give" or "bestow"</note>, which signifies "to give" and "to assign." And yet, this is truly false. For he held this kingdom only in promise and faith, which God delivered to his descendants four hundred years later under the leadership of **Moses** <note>original: "Mose"</note>. He does this so that his followers might hasten to snatch things from everywhere, and prepare wealth and a kingdom for him. A little later, when he speaks of the destroyed city, although the Sacred Scriptures have nothing of it, yet...

## BOOK II, PAGE 472

...by themselves. But a follower of Muhammad <note>original: "Muhamedicus"</note> will say: there are many good things in these precepts. For who would have been willing to accept such a mass of apparent absurdities unless some truth and goodness were mixed in? Indeed, there is something of good, though very little, in the Quran; but in the Gospel—which Muhammad himself admits is from God—there is nothing that is not absolutely perfect and most worthy of its divine Author. 

However, he takes the pretext for war from the children of Israel when they were pursuing the lost Canaanite people. Yet he persecutes the Jews, whose Law he approves, and kills the Christians, whose Gospel he says is from God. He sheds the blood of citizens, even though he seems to do the same as the Israelite cohorts did with **Saul**. He mentions Saul so that his followers might establish a leader for themselves—not Saul, but **Abu Bakr** <note>original: "Vbecharum"</note> and **Umar** <note>original: "Ahmerum"</note>, those most audacious and ruined men, from whom he might receive a pacified power. 

After this, almost passing over the fable attached to the history of Saul, he says:

> When Saul had set his ranks in order, he said: "If God makes you cross a river, he who drinks from it is not mine, or from me; and he who does not eat is from me, unless he takes a sip with his hand." And they drank from it, except for a few. For he did not cross over, nor did those who believed with him, because the enemies were in that place and state of fortune that victory could be had over them.

Saul had issued a decree with a curse: if anyone that day touched any food, he would be cursed—that is, he would die. Saul’s son **Jonathan** was not present then, but was sharply attacking and pursuing the enemies. By chance, he touched a little dewy honey with the tip of his rod, which frequently tends to drip from the sky in Syria. Because of this, he was made guilty of the curse and was sought by his father for death on account of the oath. However, the multitude resisted his attempts, saying it was unworthy for a man to be dragged to death by whose effort and diligence they had obtained victory. 

For Jonathan was not the cause of their calamities; rather, it was his imprudent father and leader who, in a moment of extreme necessity, had recklessly bound the people with a religious oath. If the people had been allowed to drink and eat and recover their strength, they would have brought back a total victory with the enemies completely destroyed; nor would they, through extreme hunger, have eaten meat with the blood against the divine precept.

Now, let the lies told by our scoundrel <note>original: "nebulo," referring to Muhammad</note> be compared. He says: "If you cross the river, he who drinks from it is not mine, except for as much as the hand can hold; everyone drank except for a few." First, he turns food into drink; he brings in a river where the matter concerns honey; he says everyone failed except a few, when not even one person withdrew or contravened the commands, except Jonathan, who (as I said) had not heard them. There are as many words here as there are lies. 

Yet we do not know to what purpose these things are told, unless it is because he was embarking on a "religious pilgrimage"—that is, the slaughter of all good men. He wanted his own people bound by similar laws so they would not desert him, and so that, devoted unto death or vengeance, they might rush forward before taking food. Meanwhile, he was abusing sacred examples to encourage and terrify them. He could have written this accurately among so many learned Jews, but he did not want his cunning to be open to anyone. Moreover, he wanted his own sacred rites—that is, those sprinkled with lies—to be like himself; lest, if they seemed true, they might be attributed to their [original] authors.

Regarding **Galot** <note>original: "Galot," the Arabic name Jalut for Goliath</note>, he does exactly the same thing when he makes him a general in that war; whereas one does not read that he was a leader, nor was he even in that war. Rather, after the forces of the Palestinians were restored a long time later, he challenged the Jews as a common soldier. 

Finally, he adds words worthy of himself: that it is necessary for there to be wars among men, lest the world be corrupted. No greater plague can be compared to war among men; and yet he says war exists lest the world be corrupted, and that this is God’s benefit on earth. If God said those things, I appeal to you, O **Nature**, who places the happiness of all things in rest and tranquility. Who taught you thus, if not that God who is supreme and perfect rest, whom this "prophet" posits as the author of the benefit of war?

...reason <note>The text begins mid-word, likely completing "necessaria" or a similar term from the previous page</note>, since among all men, unless one is insane, not a single one can be found who would approve of it in word, even if they occasionally approve of it in deed. I do not know what to examine first. I do not think what he has already granted to Christ needs to be repeated. As for his saying, "if God willed, He would not kill those who are after them," he means those after the prophets. The God of the Quran is a murderer <note>original: "homicida"</note>, who kills those whom He chooses as prophets. Man does no evil, nor does he have <term>liberum arbitrium: free will, or the capacity to choose one's own actions</term>; therefore, in Postel's view, God is the one who kills men through the tyrants of the world. O, what a wicked sentiment, worthy of a thousand punishments! Certain groups disagreed; among our own people there were the **Nestorians**, **Jacobites**, and Christians <note>Postel refers to various Eastern Christian sects that the West often viewed as heretical</note>. The judge [Muhammad], ignorant of the cause of either side, had to be appointed as arbiter; and because he was helped by the favors and benefits of **Baheira** <note>A monk who, according to medieval Christian polemics, was a mentor to Muhammad and influenced the Quran with heretical ideas</note>, he claims the Jacobites and Nestorians "believe best." This is his reasoning for agreement. Petty kings and robbers from among the Armenians, coming into the borders of Arabia—because "dog does not eat dog"—once a "prophetic peace" was settled, they were said to "believe well," being most worthy of that judge. Because a tyrant and robber needed supporters, and could not carry on a lucrative war with people like himself (for there is neither ample spoil from a robber, nor easy victory), once peace was settled with them and his dogmas were strengthened, while "one hand rubs the other," the plague crept through the whole world.

As for what he says in the final place, "if God willed, they would not be killed": what else could this most monstrous murderer say, even with a laugh, while he slaughters everyone without any regard for humanity? If God wills those things, then He is not God. For if He is unjust, He is nothing. Therefore, He does not will it—O destruction of men—He does not will what He permits to human will. But He wants the deeds themselves to be done by us sincerely and holily; as for evil deeds, even if we wish to commit them, He permits them, but He does not *will* them. Even if this seems like an evil, it would be far worse for all men to lack free will and be like a stone, than for them to be unable to commit vices, since this life is primarily a place for punishment and reward. You confess this very thing in words and assert it, yet in life you deny it.

His goal was this: that Yathrib—which he called *Medinat alnebi* <note>original: "Medinat alnebi"</note>, that is, the "City of the Prophet"—could be restored by his own people and, after the Jewish inhabitants were driven out, be claimed for the Prophet. For shortly before, it had been overturned by robbers and men similar to that prophet. And so, so that no crime might seem to lack a precedent, he ascribes wicked examples to the Patriarchs. All these deeds are unknown to the wretched Muslims <note>original: "Muhametanis"</note> today, because their successors and the Caliphs <note>The leaders of the Islamic community following Muhammad</note>, detesting and shuddering at such things, took care to erase them from human memory, and chose to cover them with other interpretations so that the crimes from which their power and remaining traces sprang would not be open to posterity. Those books—numbering 60,000 and more volumes—which were sunk near Damascus, intended this very thing, though the unlearned are ignorant of those mysteries. But when he sensed that his lie might one day betray itself, he took care at the end of the chapter to ensure that no one would doubt or dispute what he says was sent to him. For he says:

<margin>»</margin>
<margin>»</margin>
<margin>»</margin>
<margin>»</margin>
> The prophet believed in that which was sent to him by his Lord and by the faithful; he believed it all, along with God, His angel, His scripture, and His prophecy. Let us not doubt any of his prophecy. And they said: we have heard and we have submitted, etc. <note>This is a paraphrase of the Quran, Surah Al-Baqarah (2:285).</note>

He established a law among his people that nothing should be doubted; from this, it is clear that it is a lie and a falsehood. For just as gold does not fear the fire by which it is purified, so the nature of truth naturally seeks out the disputes and altercations of all men so that it may show its own light. Falsehood flees from being tested at all, such that there is no greater proof of falsehood in the entire Quran <note>original: "Alcorano"</note> than in this passage. If he had forbidden public dispute or doubt among adversaries because of "mysteries" that should not be revealed to the common people, he might perhaps have seemed to do so with merit. But to allow no doubt among his own followers, where he could have provided satisfaction, is the surest sign of a lie, of fear, and of a guilty conscience. Christ, by contrast, voluntarily asked his disciples to question him if they doubted anything (even though in the presence of such great power there was no room for doubt). If anyone today wishes to propose something against Christ or his decrees out of a desire to seek the truth, he is heard, and satisfaction is given even publicly. For the Muslims, reason is placed in the sword and in power; hence it happened that he used the word for "reason" and "power" as the same and equivocal term. For <term>Sultanet</term> <note>The term "Sultanate" or "Sultan," derived from the Arabic *sultan*, meaning authority or strength.</note> signifies both, according to that saying of the tyrant: "Right is found in arms." These are a few points from *Bacara* <note>Surah Al-Baqarah, "The Cow."</note>. If I had wished to pursue everything—since no word or sentence (unless taken from us) lacks a lie, blasphemy, or vice—the work would have grown to an immense size, causing only weariness and nausea.

### THE CHAPTER OF IMRAN, WRITTEN IN MEDINA, CHAPTER II. 200 Verses.
<note>Postel refers to Surah Al-Imran, which is the 3rd Surah of the Quran, though he labels it Chapter II here, likely following a specific manuscript division.</note>

Just as the preceding chapter was compiled partly to win over or argue against the Jews, so this second one acts partly against us <note>Postel refers to Christians here.</note>, beginning with Joachim, whom they call <term>Humran</term> <note>Postel equates the Quranic "Imran" with Joachim, the traditional father of the Virgin Mary.</note>. Therefore, everything in this chapter must be observed more diligently. It begins thus:

<margin>»</margin>
<margin>»</margin>
<margin>»</margin>
> God is; there is no God but He, the living, the self-subsisting, who sent down upon you the book in truth, confirming that which is in your hands; and He also sent down the Law and the Gospel from heaven, already before this, for the guidance of men. <note>Quran, Surah Al-Imran (3:2-3).</note>

Just as he tried to commend his own teachings in the first chapter by associating them with sacred things, so he does now. For there he had said, "that which was sent before you"; now he specifically says that the Law and the Gospel, sent from heaven, preceded him, so that the Quran might also be believed in the same way. One must take what is conceded by an adversary, and it must be admitted that the Law and the Gospel are to be accepted by the Muslims. For as I said, either the Quran must be a work of lies, or our scriptures must be approved. With the same cleverness, he grants us this just as he did above, so that we might swear by his laws. If the Quran contains a lie, it is not the law of God. If our scriptures are true and from God, the Quran—contradicting them in innumerable places—lies. Therefore, etc. A little later, speaking of paradise, he amplifies what was said above.

In instilling religion into souls, it seems to me he used that art of any rising tyrant, armed to acquire an empire. For in order to draw all types of men to his opinion, if he finds slaves, he asserts nothing is more excellent than slavery, saying their power is to come; he soothes nobles with the same words, deals with peasants with the same art, and praises defectors, outlaws, and every kind of criminal, provided they obey him, promising that everything will turn out successfully for them. He suggests that a single power will be established in which all may live freely according to their own character; and so, shoeing everyone’s feet with a single boot-tree <note>The "boot-tree" (*calopodio*) is a metaphor for a "one-size-fits-all" solution or a deceptive way of forcing everyone into the same mold.</note> until he reaches his goal, he exercises tyranny over all. This is what Muhammad <note>original: "Muhamedes"</note> actually did. For once he joined everyone to himself, he immediately oppressed them. And yet, this blind nation does not blush to attribute this law of a most cruel tyrant to God. A little later, he says that all the religions of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, the tribes, and Christ are good, and are included in his own. Thus, he says he delivers now only the law of Abraham, now of others, now of nature, so that you will find nothing more changeable than this Proteus <note>Proteus was a Greek sea-god capable of changing his shape at will; Postel uses this to call Muhammad's doctrine "shifty."</note>. This entire chapter, in short, busies itself with nothing other than gathering a multitude from everywhere and from all nations. When he says that Christ is not God, according to His humanity this is true; otherwise it is false. But I have already sufficiently shown that we do not understand God to have a partner because of this. For the one and same God is powerful, wise, and benevolent—three and one. His wisdom is the Son, not needing a physical location, begotten from eternity; He joined our humanity to Himself and so inspired His own people that almost everyone appeared as a god, which could not have happened without the Divinity transforming men. There remain innumerable things in this chapter to be refuted, where nothing is sound; but I proceed to the rest.

-> Surah An-Nisa <note>The Women</note>, that is "The Women," written in Medina. 175 Verses. <note>original: "Sora elnasæ... 175 Aiet."</note> <-

In this Surah, he treats primarily the rights of women and the goods of orphans, saying by what law they should be preserved and administered:
» Take as many wives as please you, two, three, or four; and unless you fear that «
» you cannot rule them peacefully together, take as many as your power can subdue. «
This is the opinion of the legislator, which, even if the interpreters moderate it, is still arbitrary up to the number of four <note>Postel is discussing the Quranic limit of four legal wives.</note>, and so it is in use among the great men. How unjust this is, and contrary to public peace, I leave to be judged by either the Greeks or the Romans, even though they, in the greatest natural liberty and without any fear of God, experimented with every pleasure. What peace can there be where you nourish four or five wives with their children at home like a flock, when you can scarcely satisfy the needs and desires of one? How much happier was the ancient law of the Arabs? Which gave even one sister twelve brothers as husbands (it being permitted for those lacking law to neglect kinship). How much greater was the rest and happiness anywhere among nations, whether at home or abroad? Since they ought to enjoy equally both the body and the goods of the husband, who could maintain such equity for even one hour that many complaints would not arise, when [subservient] to the lust of one...

# GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II.

...could one man ever be enough? Nor is this only a domestic evil; judges everywhere hear nothing but the disputes of women, daily divorces, daily weddings, the reclaiming of dowries, legal assignments, injuries suffered by husbands, and the miseries and oppressions of all the children. To put it in one word: nothing more turbulent or unhappy can be imagined. Consequently, the unhappy woman—though the partner of man, endowed with a rational soul like a man, and born for freedom—occupies the position of the lowest slave. She is scorched with lashes and led by commands like a beast rather than by reason, according to the husband's whim. Added to this is that countless orphans perish of hunger or are killed by their brothers so that the inheritance may remain intact. Thus, they are not treated as brothers but (unless kept for the sake of honor) are slaughtered like cattle. Nothing is more common than for a Muhammadan prince to remove his brothers from the scene, and for the beginnings of a reign to be taken from brotherly blood; some do not even spare their children. I know of one Muhammadan king who, upon ascending to power, killed or arranged for the killing of seventeen brothers; he also dispatched as many kinsmen, not by the law of war, but by poison, treachery, and private violence. I also know one who killed his own children. These are the *effects* of your law: that man—for whose sake the lower world exists, whose soul no price can compensate, who was born for the sake of cultivating the world through virtue and benefits, to whom life was given by the most high God as a distinguished gift—is held in lower esteem than lice, for whom there is a four-month truce every year according to Muhammad. <note>Postel likely refers to the "Sacred Months" in the Islamic calendar, during which violence was forbidden, but he absurdly extends this protection to vermin to mock the law's priorities.</note> O wretched men, who has bewitched your eyes? God made and joined male and female so that man should seek no others; He joined them such that it is permitted for no one to separate them, so that Christ allowed no room even for divorce (except on account of fornication). Muhammad, the author of a new nature, wishes that men, like bulls in herds, may enter into various unions; he ordained that a husband driven by an oath may divorce, and not just call her back once, but three or four times. Where there is no place for taking her back, he decreed she could be taken again as if new after being subdued by another <note>This refers to the practice of *Nikah Halala*, where a woman who has been divorced three times must marry and divorce another man before she can remarry her first husband.</note>, so that in that state, the most certain thing is that nothing is certain. Lest this "illustrious" law have too little scope, he willed that the number [of unions] be placed within the discretion of money and possessions; meanwhile, he mixes miserable catamites <term>catamites: (cynaedos) young men kept for sexual purposes</term> among the wives, converted to his law. Although interpreters veil these things with explanations, the true understanding concerns unnatural lust. So that this does not seem strange, much greater things are permitted with beasts. From this, as I have already noted, there are among the Muhammadans "most holy" men who copulate with beasts. If anyone denies this, I will produce testimony from the *Sorat Sori* <note>Referring to Surah Ash-Shura (The Consultation), verse 42:11.</note>. Lest they say I am inventing anything in such an absurd matter, I subjoin the Arabic:

> *Phatiru, flamauati uelardhi geala lechum, min anphussicumu azuagian, uemín elanhamí ezuagian, iedreuchum phihí,*
> that is, word for word: The Creator of heaven and earth gave to you spouses from yourselves, and He permits to you spouses from the beasts in this. <note>Postel is intentionally misinterpreting the verse, which states that God created "pairs" (azwajan) for humans and "pairs" for livestock. He reads "pairs from the beasts" as "spouses from the beasts" to accuse Muslims of sanctioned bestiality.</note>

<margin>ee</margin>
What do "spouses from the beasts" mean? Is this not the work of your "holiness"? Otherwise, how could it be that what heaven and earth shudder at, what even the most ferocious and barbarian nations cannot bear to hear, and what all other laws punish with the most bitter penalties, is considered a form of holiness—and no common one—among Muhammadans, unless it had authority from your "divine" legislator? Interpret it as you will, but certainly it would not be laughed off and even approved by men of the highest authority unless the law granted its assent. There is no doubt that catamites are understood in this chapter, for he joined them to the management of women and wants "Mussulmans" to be made for the sake of concubinage (which is written elsewhere, lest it be doubted here). You have all kinds of men among you in a state of slavery, yet it is not customary for a "Mussulman" to be a slave to another "Mussulman." Therefore, they ought not to be converted if they were intended for uses other than as bed-wrestlers <term>clinopales: a Greek-derived term meaning "bed-wrestlers," used here to imply sexual partners</term>. But listen, I ask, you most blind men...

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

...we also call the whole God the Son; and the love and will, we call the whole God and Holy Spirit. We also call the Father Almighty God, His Word the Son Almighty God, and the Holy Spirit His effect, which is present everywhere. It is impossible for God to act without these properties; and yet it is clear that He acts in all things. By a similar analogy, we ourselves must be able, must know, and must will before we do anything. In all arts there must be <term>fecundity</term> <note>original: "fœcunditatem," referring to the generative or creative potential</note>, a process, love, and delight. For example, take a potter: he must possess the fecundity of his art and such a power that it cannot be exhausted by use; and that power must not remain hidden, but must proceed into an effect, which cannot happen without will and love. When fire heats or breaks things apart, there must be an inexhaustible power of acting, an unceasing process of its action, and a certain natural delight, so that it naturally loves to act and cannot help but love it. Therefore, those three things are one single power distinguished by certain properties. The fecundity of the fire is the whole fire; the process of action from the fire is the one and same fire; and that ardor and love of acting is the same fire. The first is not the second, nor the second the third, or vice versa. Thus, there are not three gods, but one God. Therefore, God could not fail to generate the Son from eternity in this way, by knowing future things as present through wisdom and by creating them. In this manner we say God has a Son, a Wisdom, a Word. Whoever wishes for more on this should return to the first book. Muhammad therefore spoke wrongly when he said God does not have a son, nor is He three and one. He wished to overturn all the tenets of our religion so that he might introduce his own new religion with a new
<margin>,, ,,</margin>
God—the author of evil, as we have already seen. He adds: *Christ will not deny that he is a servant of God, nor will the angels who are near to God.* <note>Postel is paraphrasing Surah 4:172.</note> He never wished to deny that he was a servant of God insofar as he is a man, whose form he took so that he might make servants free. Therefore, insofar as he is God, he is entirely equal to the Father, differing in property and person. Insofar as he was man, he wished to undergo the most humble and dejected rank of dignity; though he was the highest in divinity, he was the lowest in the human condition. Yet he took flesh from a virgin so that he would not receive into himself any stain of the kind he was intended to remove, even though, had he been born in our [normal] way, he could have equally washed us clean by the benefit of his present divinity. For in one composite being (if indeed divine power could be confined to a place) he united the whole divinity to a soul—or a mind—and a body. Once joined, he made this a ladder to heaven for believers. But enough regarding this prophecy.

### SURAH AL-MA'IDAH, THAT IS, THE CHAPTER OF THE TABLE,
### written in Medina.

<margin>,, ,, ,, » » »</margin>
Here he speaks of choices, washings, and so many other things that this part of the Quran holds the privilege of being unable to be summarized. He said previously that four things were prohibited; now there are far more. It is prohibited for you to use <term>carrion</term> <note>original: "morticinio," meat from an animal that died of natural causes</note>, blood, the flesh of swine, and the flesh of an animal killed without invoking God, or one that was strangled, burned, crushed, killed by any fall, or whatever wild beasts have touched. I have set this down to point out the inconsistency and contradictions of the man. I do not wish to touch upon the superstitions of their washings, nor recount the practice of <term>smearing dust on the face</term> <note>Postel refers to "Tayammum," the Islamic ritual of dry purification using sand or soil when water is unavailable</note> instead of water. Let them keep those for themselves. He has this against us: *And from those who said, "We are Christians," We [God] approved their faith, but they forgot that which they were reminded of, and We spread enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Judgment, and God is by no means among them in what they do.* <note>A paraphrase of Surah 5:14.</note> Our faith is good through you and confirmed by God, just as you wrote a little earlier regarding the children of Israel. Therefore, whoever lived under those holy laws by keeping the commandments are approved by God by reason of their goodness and the law they observed.

# GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II

Therefore, both laws <note>The Old Testament/Jewish law and the New Testament/Christian law</note> are holy and good, having no fault in themselves. Thus, if men who live under that law argue and contend, because the law is good, it cannot be obscured or diminished on that account. Just as if someone were to say that gold is <term>brass</term> <note>original: "aurichalchum," a golden-colored ore or alloy</note>, another that it is Cypriot copper, some that it is iron or lead, while a few others call it gold; it does not, therefore, cease to be gold. For as is commonly said, nothing in the substance of things is changed because of affirmations or negations. Therefore, because of our disputes, or those of anyone else, our law cannot be evil, even if many forget it. For it is written and preserved in so many literary monuments that it could never fall into oblivion unless the whole world were overturned. By making God the author of sects, heresies, and evil, are you not altogether impious, you who make God the author of evil? For if what He once gave is good, it is evil to overturn it.

As for your claim that God is not among us (for you do not reveal whom you mean by "us"), if you say this of the Nestorians, Jacobites, Arians, and other impious heretics, we also admit it: and we say they are so far from having God among them that they are driven by the devil, the author of perfidy. But if you say this concerning that constant belief in Christ and the Gospel which the Catholic Church received through the hands of the Apostles and their successors, it is clear that you speak impiously. The seal of God's power was and always will be in the Church, which the saints have testified to through miracles and most famous divine works, and which has been proven by the two most famous empires <note>Likely referring to the Roman and Carolingian or Holy Roman Empires</note> and infinite kingdoms of the whole world. Whereas among the impious heretics (unless perhaps someone was a <term>sorcerer</term> <note>original: "gœticus," referring to goetic magic</note> and a conjurer), no one has ever possessed power through miracles, purity of life, or any public peace. 

Therefore, since the devil could not force any fellowship of perfidy into the convictions of the faithful, he armed Muhammad against piety and religion, and he was equipped with a sword for the ruin of nature. Hence it is no wonder that among his followers there are at least 70 sects, from which only one will be saved. For Muhammad alone received into himself the poisons of all heretics. He denies the Holy Trinity with Sabellius <note>A heretic who taught that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit were not distinct persons</note>; he says there is God and the soul of God, placing a binary in divine matters, where he seems to agree with Arius <note>A priest who taught that Christ was a created being and not fully God</note> so that he might remove Christ from the midst. Certainly, with Arius, he thinks Christ is a creature—Arius, whose guts were spilled out in a latrine because of his blasphemies, a surely divine vengeance. That Christ was only a holy man is a view he shares with Cerdo and Marcion. With the Nicolaitans, he approves of multitudes and flocks of wives; he places paradise in luxury with Cerinthus. In short, no plague of any heretic is absent from the <term>Quran</term> <note>original: "Alcorano"</note>, just as no vice was absent from its author. 

Truly, to return to the matter, our law or that of the Jews could not become evil through ambiguity, forgetfulness, or neglect; rather, the fault was in those who ought to have drummed it into the people. Just as it is not the fault of a gem or gold that it lies hidden—for it is always gold—but it must be ascribed to the negligence and ignorance of men (assuming that is the case). Therefore, there was no need to find other laws, but it was necessary to reinforce those good laws that had been neglected. But let us proceed.

> Ho there, you who use the laws of nature <note>Postel notes: "for so he understands those 'having the book,' which the interpreters call 'men of laws'"</note>, our prophet has come to you to explain many things from the book that are hidden from you, and he will hide some things from you. Now light has come to you from God, and an explained book, with which God directs him who follows His will and the way of peace, and leads him out of darkness into light by His precept, and directs them to the <term>straight path</term> <note>original: "Tzirat mustechim," likely a transliteration of the Arabic *al-Sirat al-Mustaqim*</note>, that is, to the right point of the Quran.

You see, most kind reader, to whom he says he was sent: to the gentiles themselves, so that he might bring natural light to them. Does not every single person carry around natural judgment, so that by acting badly he is inexcusable? Therefore, the Quran gives precepts in vain. For what it teaches and says is either according to nature or against it. If the first, it is fruit...

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD
### BOOK II

...is ours, since in every man there is a judgment of good and evil and **free will**, wherefore there is no place for ignorance or excuse, for God has naturally opened this to all. If he <note>Muhammad</note> speaks against nature, he is no longer to be heard; therefore, on both sides, he has written in vain. There is certainly something loftier than human judgment: **true religion**. For all pleasures are according to nature, and yet they destroy it, unless man, warned from heaven, desists from them. If, therefore, only the law of nature is to be followed, we would rush headlong into pleasures and vices and neglect the prescriptions against the plagues of soul and body. For all kinds of pleasures are according to nature. Indeed, man is prone to evil from his youth: as each person judges within himself, while often committing that which he later retracts with repentance. If nature in us had not been weakened from its origin <note>original: "ex propagine labefactata," referring to the inherited stain of Original Sin</note>, and so depraved that it drove us off course, its prescription would rightly be said to be enough, and there would never have been a need for other laws. But since, by the testimony of conscience, man daily commits those things which he judges to be evil, he knows the evil and yet cannot amend it by himself. Therefore nature, as it is now, without the **grace of God** restoring it through Christ, can never achieve salvation. 

But after trying to win over the Jews and Christians, there was a need also to flatter and worm his way into the favor of the pagans <note>original: "ethnicis"</note>: which Muhammad does more familiarly because he had been raised among them. For his speech tends toward drawing them into war, or so he says. 

<margin>»</margin> And therefore they err who say that Christ is the son of Mary <note>meaning *only* the son of Mary, denying his divinity</note>. I have already demonstrated enough, both in the first book and this one, that it was impossible for Christ to do what he did, and to bestow those powers upon his disciples, unless he had been both man and God. Look at the Gospel. He raised the dead in his own name, he put demons to flight in his own name, he healed diseases in his own name: he performed all miracles without invoking the name of God <note>i.e., he did not need to pray for the power to be granted, as he possessed it inherently</note>, although he was subject to the Father. This, unless he were God, he could not do. His disciples did the same things in his name, and greater ones, as he had promised. The prophets performed miracles only by invoking the name of God. Thus no one, however holy, could accomplish anything unusual without the invocation of God. Therefore, Jesus Christ was God; he is from eternity, and shall be. But having been made man in time, he changed the nature in true believers, so that they might dread vices worse than death, and might even seek death itself for the sake of the truth, living for other men and not for themselves—contrary to all things which those led by nature do. Therefore, those who call Christ God are not blasphemers, but rather all who dare to deny it are impious and damned.

<margin>»</margin> It follows: *Say, and what would prohibit God if he wished to kill Christ, and Mary*
<margin>»</margin> *his mother, and as many as are on the earth? For God is king of heaven and earth, etc.*
He could indeed reduce the humanity of Christ and Mary to nothing, but he could not reduce the divinity. For nothing simple can rise up against itself, much less God. But Mary and the most holy humanity of Christ yielded to fate <note>meaning they experienced physical death</note>, for God did not consider death unworthy, which he willed to have a place among all men, even the most holy. Let us proceed.

<margin>»</margin> The Jews and Christians say, *We are the children of God and his friends.* Say: *But he would*
<margin>»</margin> *not at all afflict you in your sins. Therefore you are men. For from these whom he* 
<margin>»</margin> *created, he has mercy on whom he wills, and punishes whom he wills.* 
What do you infer, hey there, "prophet"? We are the friends of God (suppose the Jews were equals to good men after the killing of Christ); therefore we ought not to suffer anything evil in this life on account of our sins, or even without evils, we should not be pressed by afflictions? Do you not often say that these riches are nothing, that this life is nothing but a game? How then do you wish the best men to be gifted with good things in this life? Since virtue itself, which in this life is the goal of a good man, is placed upon a steep path, and since the present goal of life consists in perpetual action and labor. If to follow virtue is to be a good man—which you will admit, whether you like it or not—how can it be that the better someone is, as a son and friend of God, the more he is weighed down by labors, troubles, and punishments? # THE SECOND BOOK OF GUILLAUME POSTEL
### q 3
<meta>catchword: speaking</meta>

God punishes. Philosophers never considered a man unhappy in his body if he seeks, grasps, and practices virtue itself with all his effort. Therefore, Christians are not unhappy because they are afflicted by physical punishments or the plundering of their fortunes; rather, they are far happier because they would rather suffer those things than defect from God in any way or break the prescriptions of His law. If virtue consisted of having riches and lacking troubles, what would a tyrant or a stone be? Would not the tyrant be the happiest of all because he will have scraped together everyone’s wealth, and stones because they enjoy a total absence of pain? You betray yourself, O prophet <note>Postel is addressing Muhammad directly</note>. You approve of the "highest good" of **Epicurus** <note>Epicurus was an ancient Greek philosopher often associated—sometimes unfairly—with the pursuit of physical pleasure as the ultimate goal</note>, and you prefer the life of a beast to a human one when you think those who overflow with all the delights of the body are the friends of God. Virtue has nothing in this life worthy of itself. God, and the future and eternal life, is its reward. Tyrants snatch away the property of others while pious men suffer it, and men will be nothing other than men in this life: some good, others evil.

God punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills. You call "mercy" the splendors of fortune, riches, pleasures, and fame; but you call "punishments" humility, patience, endurance, justice, and similar things—which we nevertheless prefer to have over riches. You have had your happiness in this life, you and those like you, and you will lack the reward in the future. What shall I add regarding the fable of the two men, whom Moses supposedly sent ahead, when in the Sacred Scriptures mention is made of the whole army? I do not refute what is foreign to the Sacred Scriptures. What of the raven, who went out to seek a companion? Are these things not against the Scriptures? Someone went out to a corpse a second time, but there was no other raven outside the ark with which it might meet. Furthermore, Noah sent it, not God. When Muhammad says that he who does not judge according to the prescriptions of Moses is unjust, does he not speak against himself, since he hands down and follows different things almost everywhere? Concerning **Christ**, however, he says:

> And we ordained in their footsteps (the prophets, of whom he spoke above) Jesus the son of Mary, the most certain confirmer of the Law, and we gave him the **Gospel**, in which there is light and certain direction for those things held in the Law, and for a firm direction for those who fear, so that the people of the Gospel may judge concerning that which God sent down in it. And those who do not judge according to what God sent in that Gospel are unjust.

This is the praise of the Gospel which we receive even as if from an adversary. He gave this to the **Jacobites** <note>A name for the Syrian Orthodox Church</note> and the people of **Bahira** <note>Refers to a legendary monk who, in Islamic tradition, recognized Muhammad's prophetic potential</note> who had joined him, so that they might finally grant that he was a prophet sent to the nations using the **natural law**. To what end did God, after the Law of Terror <note>the Old Testament</note> and the Law of Grace <note>the New Testament</note>, preserve that which was first and make it last? Any unrefined and unskilled pagan could clearly profess the same: that a natural light had been given to him from heaven, by which he might follow things to be sought and avoid things to be fled. Anyone relying on the sword was just as much a prophet as Muhammad. 

Moreover, although there are two good laws, and according to Muhammad there is salvation in all of them, nevertheless a little while after gaining power he allows it to Christians or forbids it to Jews. He hunts for nothing other than power and tyranny, whereas Christ commands that all magistrates and princes be obeyed. He later encourages attackers to fear nothing so that they may seize whatever non-believers possess. For he asserts that goods belong to God, and He gives them to whom He wills. Finally, he wishes to attack by any path and draw the pagans of **Mecca** to his opinion. And if, he says,

> you would receive the Law and the Gospel, and that which is ordained for you by your Lord, you would have so much food that it would be above you and beneath your feet.

Thus, to force everyone into one law—an impossible one indeed—he grants the "happiness of the belly," in which even the beasts themselves surpass us. Then he says:

> O pagans, you can do nothing until you receive the Law and the Gospel, and that which was sent to you by your Lord.

I wonder, O followers of Muhammad, since you have so many and such great testimonies of the Law and the Gospel, why do you not believe in the Gospel and in Christ? Why do you persecute Christians, the best kind of men? Either those things are false, or they are true. If false, your law is evil. If true, our things are to be believed. But when he introduces Christ...
