### WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK II ###

the beginning, that Christ is the Son, I have proved by many reasons in the first book. For whatever notable miracles Christ performed, he did so (as I have often said) in his own name, which belongs to God alone. All those miracles performed by the disciples and saints were done in that same name; all who subscribed to it and used his precepts were entirely transformed and made unlike other men. This is a transformation that only God can perform. Yet in the name of Christ, all those things were done. It is as if by the power of the word, <note>original: "in ui uerbi," referring to the Logos or the creative power of speech.</note> through which the concept of my mind is opened to me, I were to approach, perform, and complete all the highest things—I would be doing them both in the name of thought and in the name of the work. For the thing is the same in its conception or thought, the same in the explanation of the word, and the same in the execution of the work. The Devil could not otherwise draw the human race back to himself except under the pretext of the glory of God, as if the glory ascribed to the Son of God were contrary to the divine glory; whereas, in truth, the glory of God never appeared until Christ joined it to a human body. I shall not speak in this chapter of that "happy" and usual paradise in which there are rivers of wine, milk, honey, fruits, silk garments, golden necklaces, gems, food, drink, sexual intercourse, and the other instruments of bodily pleasure. For Muhammad was made a prophet for no other reason than that he might pursue, in this life, that paradise born of plunder and blood. But I have often wondered why God did not fear drunkenness in paradise more than in this world. The reason is ready at hand: Muhammad's head will not ache, because they shall drink from it abundantly and not become intoxicated; they will be busy enough, and the virgins will always remain "unconquered." <note>Postel is mockingly describing the Islamic concept of the *Houris* and the lack of hangovers or exhaustion mentioned in the Quran.</note> O great joys! O happy pigs, <note>original: "ô fœlices porcos." A common Renaissance polemic comparing those who seek carnal pleasure to Epicurean swine.</note> who shall live again! O happy rewards! This is the goal of a law received from a man. And are you not ashamed, O <term>Muslims</term> <note>original: "Mußulmani."</note>? Are you so lacking in common sense that you are more senseless than many brute animals? For by the silent sense of nature, the beasts cry out against your law. The faith and marital love of the turtle-dove, the modesty of the camel, the cleanliness of the elephant, the kisses of the wood-pigeons, and six hundred other things condemn you before God.

35. From here to the end of the book, he swears most frequently, so that those who saw his claims were false—overcome and bound by the oaths of the prophet—might finally believe that which they had previously begun to believe through fears, torments, spoils, and impostures. Indeed, how much he valued faith is indicated by his breaking of the marital bond with all his wives. The oath shown to <note>Postel likely refers to Hafsa and Aisha, wives of Muhammad.</note> Hafsa and Hafiza was immediately neglected and broken for the sake of a concubine; the covenant struck with the Jews was afterwards made so void that he destroyed almost all of them; even as he broke those laws which nature gave to the conscience and by which we make peace with it, while he commanded and saw to it that brothers, parents, citizens, and friends were slaughtered. Therefore, they were quite captured in mind who, after God was neglected, after human nature was stripped away, and after slaughter was brought to all, thought he would have any regard for an oath. He swears, therefore, in this place by the "wise and holy <term>Quran</term>," <note>original: "Alcoranum prudens."</note> as if wisdom were outside the soul. He wishes, however, to be supported by the example of the Apostles (for by joining all prophets, both false and true, together, he had previously crammed them in to the point of disgust) whom they rejected in Antioch when they were sent by God. It says:

> And he set forth for them a parable. The citizens of the city, when the messengers came to it; when we sent to them two, they called them liars, and we increased the number with a third, and they said: "We are messengers to you." They said: "What are you but men like us? God has granted you nothing from heaven, and you do nothing but lie." They said: "Our Lord knows that we are destined for you, and nothing pertains to us except clear preaching." etc. <note>This is a translation of Surah Ya-Sin (36:13-17) from the Quran.</note>

The interpreters of this passage say that these were Peter and Matthew, or some other of the Apostles, whom the people of Antioch <note>The text cuts off at "An-tiocheni."</note> would not...

### ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD ###

the people of Antioch <note>original: "Antiocheni"</note> refused to listen, until they healed a rich man named Abibaiarum <note>Habib al-Najjar, often called "Habib the Carpenter," a figure in Islamic tradition associated with the disciples of Jesus in Antioch.</note>, after he had believed in Christ. He immediately began to cry out in the whole city: "Listen to those who ask no reward from you and are rightly guided!" Whereupon the king, being moved to anger, killed the man and thrust two Apostles into prison. Then came Paul, who—acting as if he were unknown to them—asked the king to see them and learn what law they were teaching. When they had come out, a girl blind from birth was presented to them, whom Peter immediately healed, as he did a boy. Furthermore, the girl was the daughter of that prince. Then the people of Antioch were converted to Christ. This is the account given by the interpreters Buhatias and Hamahsseri <note>Postel is referring to the famous Quranic commentators Al-Baydawi and Al-Zamakhshari.</note> on this passage. Because the people had rejected them and wanted to stone them, Muhammad attempts to make his own followers act similarly, so that they might not wish to hear or receive a prophet of God—since they rejected those and all other prophets—as if he himself were now an Apostle or prophet. With these lures, he began to capture the miserable peasants and force himself upon them.

In the following chapters, he intersperses the same sacred rites, the same paradises with chaste women (that is, virgins), with whom they will spend fifty years in the ecstasy of Venus <note>original: "ecstasi Veneris," a classical reference to sexual pleasure.</note>. He describes a hell with poison and the tree of Zaqqum <note>original: "zacomiij," the bitter, thorny tree of Islamic hell.</note>, and so on. He repeats the stories of the winds and demons obeying the nods of Solomon, and six hundred other fables. Indeed, the chapters become shorter as they approach the end, so that the last ones are merely a few lines. Therefore, one should not linger on them as much as on the first ones, since we have touched upon the principal headings of these matters in the previous sections. I have done this to reveal to our curious people those things which it is right to know when speaking of these absurdities. I will pluck out certain things here and there <note>original: "Vellicatim," meaning piecemeal or selectively.</note> from here to the end, if any seem relevant to the matter. I shall be more diligent in the Arabic edition.

In chapter 41, which the Westerners call *Sura* <note>original: "Sori"</note> and the Easterners call *eschec*, there are certain things to be noted, one of which I have already noted above: namely, that God created mates for us from the brutes <note>animals</note>, the use of which He permits. It was not enough for this "prophet," having violated his faith, to have brought other women in over his first marriage—the woman through whom he had been raised to power—and to have made fourteen other concubines lawful. Nor was it enough for him to have either divorced or married any woman he pleased, without a dowry contract, at his own whim, or to have used all women in every possible way. Nor was it enough to have abused catamites <note>original: "catamittis," referring to pederasty or male youths.</note> with burning lust—unless he had also granted to his "saints" sexual intercourse with brutes. All these things are worthy of the author, the prophet of the Arabs. If the commentators cloak these things with honorable interpretations, as I have said, the most "holy" Muslims nevertheless demonstrate that they are to be understood in this way, by mounting she-asses and camels or any living creatures in the middle of the market. Because we have seen it, we can assert it. Among the Turks <note>original: "Tuniciij," likely referring to Tunisians or Ottomans generally.</note> nothing is more common; the same is proven in Syria. Whence would such a powerful reputation for "holiness" have come, such that you admire such men <margin>,,</margin>, if not from the prescription of your law? I know you explain the phrase *uemin elanhami ezuagian* <note>Arabic: "wa-min al-an'ami azwajan," meaning "and of the cattle, pairs."</note> as "and from the animals, mates," meaning females for the propagation of the species. But why did the prophet join females from the brutes with human females when he is speaking there of carnal union? If you deny the writing, I shall appeal to the fact. Finally, he concedes our scriptures and those of the Jews to be holy and to have proceeded from God, so that he might seem to profess all those things—which he has already done quite often to capture our people. I take this from a crafty adversary and infer the following: Since our scriptures are from God, and are prior, and holy, and of such a kind that if we kept them we would be most happy in this present life (as Muhammad says), then they must be the best and must be kept. And whatever contravenes them must necessarily be false. But since the Quran contradicts them more than a thousand times, it cannot be from God. For since it is written entirely against the Gospel, let no one doubt that it was made with the Devil as its author.

<margin>,,</margin> He also contravenes the precept of Christ here when he says that one who is provoked ought to take revenge, otherwise he is impious. This is the reason for which you write: when anyone had offended this prophet even by suspicion alone, unless he had immediately taken revenge or killed him, he would have been among the damned, as he says.

<meta>This page continues William Postel’s polemic against Muhammad and the Quran, focusing on the moral contrast between Christ and Muhammad, and pointing out perceived logical inconsistencies regarding the revelation of the Quran and the status of the Prophet.</meta>

# WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK II. #

O, how far those things are from that holy patience of Christ and his followers. Christ suffered all things; Muhammad undermined all things, even when provoked by no injury. Christ and his followers gave all, if they had anything; that man [Muhammad] plunders all. Christ heals all; Muhammad harms all. Christ grants all to his enemies; Muhammad does not even spare his brothers. Thus darkness differs from light.

<margin>“</margin>He says in the following chapter that he plundered the goods of those among whom he lived so that he might divide them among them [his followers], and promote certain ones to ranks of dignity. What else <margin>“</margin>would a robber do for his companions? He seizes what belongs to others so that he may bestow others' property, and finally, for the sake of strengthening a power—however unjust—it is necessary to establish certain ranks of dignities and offices. What can this be, except the highest iniquity? For what purpose are laws, if such things are permitted? What do republics and the assembly of men offer if whatever is pleasing is permitted? So that when one is stronger, he is immediately more just. These things are indeed permitted to princes against enemies, because enemies are to be coerced by such civil punishment. But to attribute these things to God—which he [Muhammad] committed against citizens, against friends, against brothers, against the weak and afflicted, against the undeserving—who would not shudder? "That is the law of God," he says. God said it, that is: "let the will stand for reason" <note>original: "sit pro ratione voluntas"; a classical legal maxim implying that a ruler's whim is sufficient justification for law.</note>.

### 34. Dochan, that is, Smoke. ###

<note>Referring to Surah ad-Dukhan (The Smoke) in the Quran.</note>

<margin>“</margin>"Through the clear book," he says, "we sent it on a blessed night." Rightly he says "in the night," because no one saw it. Before the eyes of all, with everyone seeing wonders <margin>“</margin>on the mountain peak, and hearing thunder and voices scarcely tolerable to the ear, the law was given to Moses; but to you, by night and in a cave. This is the ancient fiction of crafty men, which hates the light and seeks double darkness: of the night and of the cave. But tell me, in what place, and which book was received? If at Mecca, as I have already said, the chapters from Medina are not sacred; if at Medina, the Meccan ones are false. If you received the whole book at once, why could it not be completed for twenty-three entire years? If it was whole, why did you not publish it? If only a part, why does it not stand out and get marked as a summary of the whole, like the tablets of Moses? It is entirely contradictory that the book was given in one night, and yet was given piecemeal to followers every day, and was composed according to the occasions of events. Furthermore, when you frequently say that you have placed in that book things concerning all matters: those things which you placed, you did not have from God. These are old wives' delusions <note>original: "anilia deliramenta"</note>, worthy of both the author and the believers.

### Chapter 46. ###

<note>Referring to Surah Al-Ahqaf.</note>

Many things must be noted by us here; he betrays himself in almost every verse. When he is accused of it being a fiction, he denies it with an oath: <margin>“</margin>"If I devised it," he says, "let nothing of God be mine." As if that scoundrel <note>original: "nebulo"</note> believed God existed—he who abused His name throughout the entire book and made Him the author of idolatry, homicide, fratricide, lying, theft, adultery, and whatever vices there are or ever were. Which I know not to be anything other than denying God Himself. <margin>“</margin>"Say," he says, "I am not the first of the prophets, nor do I know what will become of me, or of you." <margin>“</margin>Certainly you are not the first, nor the last: because among them you are nothing. For what is false is a privation of the true. But it is most marvelous how it can be that the "universal redeemer," the "seal of the prophets" <term>Seal of the Prophets (Khatam an-Nabiyyin): The Islamic title for Muhammad as the final prophet.</term>, who saw God in the ninth heaven, who is the most perfect of creatures, who is on familiar terms with angels, who fulfills all laws—now is ignorant of what will be in the future for him, even though God, loving him so much, has not made him secure regarding his salvation. It must surely be believed that he did not have such familiarity with God as was said, if he does not know whether he is on the path of salvation or damnation. Our Paul knew that neither death, nor life, nor things high, nor things low could separate him from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus. Never did any of the prophets doubt what would become of him.

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD #

Therefore, Muhammad, who wavers on this point, is no prophet. Indeed, he was so hard-pressed by the failing multitude that he did not know which way to turn. Some objected that the law of Moses was better; others said, "Your work is a fiction"; others said they were merely the writings of the ancients; still others said he was a raving madman and out of his mind. Certainly, such things would never have been raised so often or so frequently if there had been no cause for them. For it is impossible that what everyone frequently objects to is not true, or at least plausible. Such things were never objected to any of the true prophets, because there was not even a suspicion of similar behavior in them. The leaders of the Jews did object three or four times to Jesus Christ—the God-man—claiming he was a sorcerer <note>original: "incantator"</note> when he cast out demons; but that accusation proceeded from a fact they maliciously misinterpreted. For this reason, Muhammad frequently used this perceived injury as a pretext for himself, as if he shared a common cause with Christ—though he would have actually wanted to be considered and be a sorcerer. 

But I have already noted those things above. It remains to speak about the demons as listeners. Since Muhammad could hardly obtain faith for his trifles among men, he borrowed it from demons so that he might thrust it upon men. He says:

> And when we directed a multitude of demons to you so they might hear the Quran, and when they read it, they said: "Be silent." And when it was finished, they returned to their people as messengers, and said: "O our people, we have heard a book sent after Moses, confirming what is in hands, directing to the truth and to the right way. O our people, strive to call upon the Lord and believe in Him; He will remit your sins and save you from a heavy punishment." <note>This is a Latin translation of Quran 46:29–31, where a group of Jinn (spirits/demons) are said to have listened to Muhammad and converted.</note>

This is the true confirmation of this law: a law that no man could prove, but the devil was able to confirm. A vote truly worthy of the work and its author! The demon—that nefarious plague of mankind—adds his seal of approval to the law, to the ruin of nature and the contempt and disgrace of the written Word of God. No philosopher would deny that all works of the demon are evil and sinful. But since the demons heard the Quran, preached it to their own people, and believed in it so as to become Muslims <note>original: "Mussulmani"</note>, it follows that whoever does the same must be a companion of demons. Truly, the spirit compelled Muhammad to babble these things prophetically in this passage to hint that all who would give their name to this persuasion would also be joined to the company of demons in eternal punishment. O Muslims, at least recognize the author of your law from this passage, and unless you wish to perish, repent. 

I will pass over how sinful it is to believe that there is a certain "people" of demons, and that they perform preaching for one another and repent; for those <term>separate substances</term> <note>Postel uses the scholastic term "substantiis separatis" to refer to angels and demons—beings that exist without physical bodies.</note> are so confirmed in evil that they are unable to repent by any means. But I understand his logic: God wanted to be just and an avenger of crimes, using the works of evil demons to punish the impious; Muhammad, however, brought salvation to the demons and freed them from hell and the dark places, thereby doing away with the place of divine justice. For this is what follows: if indeed they can be saved from that same class of being, then all can be; if all can be saved, the wicked will not suffer punishment; if the wicked are not punished, then God is not God. For he who acts unjustly is no God at all. This is the logical conclusion of the opinion of Muhammad, the "redeemer of demons." 

Truly, a demon presided over you when you babbled these things. His goal was that while you persuade the unlearned that a demon can be good, they might not be on guard against his tricks and fraud—which he is truly incapable of abandoning. For once the sign of the cross and its Author are removed, the devil takes possession of all things. This was made clear enough in my previous book, where we dealt with separate substances and their kinds. It has now been most evident that this man raged violently in two instances (though in the whole book nothing else is urged but the shedding of blood): first, after the Jews had defected from him, and second, after the women returning to their parents' houses had exposed his fables and impostures. Now indeed, especially in the chapter of the author...

# GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II #

...carrying the name of slaughter, he commands the sword to be drawn against the faces of all, and for them to be forced into the faith by death or captivity. The Africans and Arabs call this chapter <term>elcatal</term> <note>original: "elcatal"; referring to *Al-Qital*, an alternative name for Surah 47 of the Quran, meaning "The Fighting" or "The Slaughter"</note>, that is, "the slaughter." Others call it "Muhammad," so that these terms are clearly synonyms: slaughter, plague, destruction, and Muhammad. Hear the edict:

> And when you encounter those who resist your law, strike their necks until you have overcome them; then bind them with chains so that they may later ransom themselves from us, until the war or its campaign is finished. And if God willed, He would take vengeance upon them Himself, but He wishes to test you by means of one another. And those who are killed in the way of God, their works are not in vain, for they shall be guided and shall prosper with God, and shall enter the paradise destined for them. O you who believe, if you defend God, He will defend you and make your steps firm, etc.

God is made out to be the author of slaughter—He who took nature under His protection! He does indeed permit and sometimes command the sword to be drawn against the wicked; but against those who live peacefully, who possess the laws of God and keep them, and who have done no harm, violence should in no way rage. Now, we have seen frequently in this book that the law of the heathens is good if one does good, and the laws of Moses and Christ are equally so; therefore, none of them deserved to be killed justly. But it is no wonder that the "God of Muhammad," the author of evil, has cast a fire into the middle of the world even unto the ruin of nature, and commanded that war be waged against innocent peoples for the reason that they refused to believe what even a doting and delirious old woman could hardly agree to. Indeed, why wonder that the same God promises paradise and prosperity to unspeakable murderers? For his paradise is very much like that God: certainly entirely alien to the God of nature. In these paradises, he says, they shall live,

> under which flow rivers of clearest water, rivers of milk whose taste never changes, and rivers of sweetest wine for those who drink, and rivers of purified honey; and they have therein every kind of fruit, and mercy from their Lord.

Now, if you add to these the cushions on which they may recline, and the <term>glaucopides</term> <note>original: "glaucopides"; literally "gray-eyed" or "owl-eyed" women, referring to the Houris described in the Quran</note> women, and the young boys serving with golden cups, and the silken garments, necklaces, and whatever else is written in other places, who could wish for a greater happiness for <term>Sardanapalus</term> <note>A legendary Assyrian king known for his extreme decadence and luxury.</note> or <term>Heliogabalus</term> <note>A Roman emperor infamous for his religious eccentricity and self-indulgence.</note>? All these things are perfectly consistent with one another: the God, the creature, the prophet, the soldier, the paradise, the hell—finally, the law itself is everywhere consistent with itself. But since there are two powers in nature—one commanding, powerful in bringing forth and preserving all good things, yet indulgent toward evil as long as there is room for repentance; the other which tends toward and aspires to the ruin and hatred of nature—it is easy to judge from which of the two this law proceeded. We can even guess from this passage that those who had believed him from the beginning fell away, as seen in these words:

> And those who believed say: "A prophecy was never sent to him." And when a decisive prophecy is sent in which the mention of slaughter is made, you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one fainting at death; and it would be better for them to comply and say, "it is well." And when the command is urgent, if they believed God, it would be better for them, etc.

He held God to be favorable only as one whom he could appoint as a servant and approver of his own desires according to his lust. Even in good and necessary things, the God who pities human nature is not accustomed to act at first glance unless he is greatly moved by prayers. Thus, through many conjectures, that "God"—the Prince of Darkness and author of human destruction—reveals himself, coating pestilential and lost things with the color and pretense of good things. He does this lest, by openly using his schemes without disguise, he should immediately betray himself and, like a cornered rat, perish by his own evidence. He could not persuade anyone against nature that it is just to kill brothers, destroy parents, remove friends, swoop down upon the fortunes of all, oppress the poor, exalt tyrants, and make a path for wickedness by the sword; but [under the guise] of religion...

# DE ORBIS CONCORDIA #
### ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD ###

...and under the pretext of the divine name, the foulest deeds were made the most holy. The devil was not able to resist the power of Christ, so instead, under the guise of preserving divine honor—while pretending to give much and great things to God—he takes everything away. For there was, is, and shall be one and the same honor for God and Christ; yet this honor cannot truly be known or returned to God now except through Christ, the Son of God. Thus, he denies not only Christ himself but also the Father: a point I have previously demonstrated with many arguments. This is the cunning of Satan. Under the pretext of religion, it is now permitted for Muhammad and his followers to be armed to the destruction of nature; and while he promises a reformation of all religions, he utterly overthrows them all, as far as he is able. 

For he who confuses the false with the true, and calls the whole mixture "the truth," sins more gravely than he who asserts, holds, or approves what is false as true. The latter does not deceive others; he only harms himself—unless perhaps he sins by example. But he who persuades others of falsehood under the pretext of truth drags both himself and everyone else headlong into ruin. Hence, although this law <note>The Quran</note> seems to confess one God, it is for that very reason worse than the laws of all the idolaters. Their laws undermine nothing but themselves; this law makes God the author and approver of every crime that can fall within human sense and action. But this "good and murderous" prophecy armed the soldiers against Muhammad’s fellow citizens, seeking to test those who were willing to fall into danger in the name of the law. 

The following chapter, or prophecy, is therefore called <term>phatha</term> <note>original: "phatha"; referring to *Al-Fath*, Surah 48, meaning "The Victory" or "The Opening"</note>, that is, the "gate" or "victory," because it suggests that one may enter into persuasion through war. In it, he recounts the crimes committed by him in the Valley of Mecca, where he put the citizens to flight: 

> And it is He who withheld your hands from them and their hands from you in the valley of Mecca, after He had given you victory over them, and God sees what you do. They are those who are <term>Chaphiri</term> <note>original: "Chaphiri"; from the Arabic *Kafir*, meaning "unbelievers" or "infidels"</note>, and they opposed you in the Forbidden Temple; the victim is bound so that its slaughter may be completed; and were it not for the faithful men, etc. 

Because of the victory already won, he encourages his followers to kill their fellow citizens, parents, relatives, and friends in the manner of a "bound victim." And a little later: *The testimony of Muhammad is sufficient, and those who are with him are stronger than their adversaries.*

While other laws may be good, it is apparently "testimony enough" that Muhammad is stronger. What else could a robber say? It is enough for any subverter of the world if he and his followers are the stronger party, for this is his "right." No one is unaware that almost all empires were either occupied or increased by tyranny; but to use the authority of Providence as a pretext for crime—no one before him dared that. Those who crept into the title of divinity achieved it by means of some miracle cleverly devised by their ancestors, or earned it through their works. Legislators fixed the name of divinity to their laws without any blood; others were elevated by the glory of their parents. Muhammad alone dared to ascribe the ruin of the world to God as its author.

->51. Eltur.<-
<note>Postel refers to Surah 52, *At-Tur* (The Mount)</note>

He ascribes the authority of his law to Mount Sinai and to "scraped parchment," that is, he says it belongs to Moses and Abraham. The commentators say that the Quran was actually written on the skin of the ram that Abraham sacrificed, and is therefore the "Law of Abraham." I say nothing of the Paradises described in this prophecy, since they are similar everywhere. Here there are meats of all kinds, wines that do not intoxicate, young boys serving while dressed in many-colored garments, and many things that lead to total satiation. What bothers me, however, is that I do not read where such a vast quantity of food is to be excreted. For that part would seem quite necessary in such a paradise. Many other things also seem to be lacking there.

52. I have already shown how appropriate he deemed these things to be to the divine nature in that ascension to heaven. God is considered finite according to Muhammad—which is to say, he is nothing—since he <note>Muhammad</note> approached Him at a specific, fixed distance. For whatever has a beginning also has an end. I say nothing of the stars by which he swears here, which he claims are fixed with golden chains so that they might drive away demons who attempt to approach paradise. I do not speak of the brute animals inhabiting heaven; there is nothing surprising in this since they are to be resurrected. I say nothing of the angel whose head is a hundred thousand times larger than the world, by which he surpasses his "finite" God. Meanwhile, he seems to mock the divine nature with three goddesses. These are Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat <note>original: "alleta, alhozaí, elmenauta"</note>: whom interpreters identify as Diana, Venus, and Minerva. Al-Lat and Al-Uzza were worshipped by the Meccans and by Muhammad himself before he became a "Messiah" through the Jewish faction. When men are turned away from the true worship of God, they are drawn into destruction, leading to their own ruin and the ruin of others.

In Chapter 53 <note>Postel refers to Surah 54, Al-Qamar, "The Moon"</note>, the moon is split in the presence of Bugellinus <note>Possibly a Latinized name for a witness or a corruption of a name in Postel's source</note> at his request, as I noted before. Since no one else reports this, I do not believe it. For the moon, serving the world, does not enter the sleeves of prophets <note>Postel is mocking a popular medieval legend that the split moon passed through Muhammad's sleeves</note>. The following chapter <note>Surah 55, Ar-Rahman</note> imitates the 135th Psalm of David <note>Modern Psalm 136</note>, because it intersperses various statements with a certain repetition in the manner of a true prophet, so that it might seem related to him. In it are the women of paradise, with whom they lie but do not defile, and men and demons <term>jinn</term> created from a flame of fire. There are also pomegranates and fruits in that paradise, and many other things. The same paradise, along with a similar hell, is depicted in the nearby Chapter 55 <note>Surah 56, Al-Waqi'a</note>.

At the end of "The Iron" <note>original: "elhedid"</note>, Chapter 56 <note>Surah 57</note>, he even gives testimony to Christ, saying that his followers are pious, merciful, and religious. I wonder, therefore, why he wished to introduce a law different from the Gospel; or why the Muslims do not now rise up against him, since their own prophet confesses the Gospel law to be good.

One thing remains for us to note out of many lies: when, in Chapter 60 <note>Actually Surah 61:6, As-Saff</note>, he ascribes these words to Christ:

> And when Jesus the son of Mary said: O children of Israel, I am sent to you from God, to confirm what you have in your hands of the law, and I announce to you a prophet after me, whose name is Ahmad. And when he came to them with miracles, they said: this is plain incantation. And who is more unjust than he who forges a lie against God?

I would like the Muslims to be asked to show in what place in the Gospel it is written that "Ahmad" or Muhammad was to come after Christ. There exist copies of the Gospel in the Indian language, in Armenian, in the Jacobite, in two Chaldean <note>Syriac</note> versions, and there are even the words in Hebrew from the hostile Jews; the Greeks, Georgians, Serbians, Dalmatians, and Latins all have the Gospels in their own characters and languages. I say nothing of the innumerable vulgar tongues in which the same books are available. These nations are widely separated from one another. Let them also consult the Nestorians, Armenians, and Jacobites: if they find such a thing, <term>porrigimus herbam</term> <note>A Latin idiom meaning "we yield the victory" or "we surrender"</note>. How could it be that this was in the Gospel, yet no one anywhere possessed it? It is an impudent lie, Muhammad, used so that you might retain your soldiers and keep them obedient to you. Christ gave no support to your lie. When he spoke of you, he designated you as the Antichrist, not a prophet—unless you call a "false prophet" a prophet. He promised that after him he would send the <term>Paraclete</term> <note>The Comforter or Holy Spirit</note> to his disciples, which he manifested ten days later. After the greatest of prophets, after the Son of God, conceived of a virgin by the Holy Spirit, speaking in his cradle and swaddling clothes, exhibiting every kind of miracle, and taken up to God in body and soul into heaven—who is also to be the future judge of the living and the dead—no one greater could be promised or come, except a false one and an impostor. For you would strive in vain to restrain with a stake or hedges that animal which the defense of a citadel cannot hold. What is not confined by the greatest forces, you will struggle in vain to retain with a weaker power.

## ON GOD AND THE ULTIMATE END
->errors.<-
### CHAPTER XIV.

Now, if I wished to touch upon the absurdities of the *Sunnah* and the *Tafsir* <note>original: "Suneh & Hafsiar"; Postel refers to the *Sunnah* (traditions) and *Tafsir* (exegesis or commentaries), though "Hafsiar" may specifically refer to a particular commentator known to him</note>, this work would grow tenfold. It will be enough, therefore, to reveal in a few words what both the Prophet himself and the authors explaining his dogmas feel about the First and Ultimate Cause, which is God and Paradise. We can inquire no better into the quality of Muhammad's God than by observing how He visibly showed Himself to him in the highest heaven. We have already seen the memory of the night and the "two bow-shots" <note>A reference to Quran 53:9, describing Muhammad’s proximity to God during the *Miraj* or Night Journey</note> by which he was distant from God. 

The interpreters say that when he was in the seventh heaven, after he had commended himself to Christ, Gabriel did not dare to proceed further and left him to complete the journey alone. Then, through swirling places, through waters and innumerable snows, he traveled so far that he was entirely exhausted by the journey and stopped, until he heard a certain voice saying to him: "Muhammad, approach and greet your Creator." But when he approached at the sound of the voice, he saw such a light that it broke the sharpness of his eyes; nevertheless, he approached near to God within two bow-shots. God Himself, having seventy thousand veils of light before His face, did not offer a sight of His face to Muhammad, but touching his shadow with His hand, He affected him with such coldness that he could hardly stand. Indeed, He told him many secrets, which are truly so numerous in their writers' works that two hundred pack-mules could not carry a single copy of each book. 

But meanwhile, before we depart from that truly "cold God," it is necessary to know the distance from the earth to heaven, so that we may strive toward it. Listen, reader, to the oracles and the prophetic manner of citation. Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Qurtubi <note>original: "Hebdullahius Muhamedes Cartibius"</note> in the *Tadhkira* <note>original: "Tezchere elimam," referring to the *Al-Tadhkira fi Ahwal al-Mawta wa-Umur al-Akhira* (The Reminder of the States of the Dead and the Matters of the Hereafter) by the 13th-century scholar Al-Qurtubi</note>, which is a compendium of their faith, writes thus:

Ibn Wahb <note>original: "Aben uaheb"</note> reports, and Akhbar ibn Abi Bakr <note>original: "Achber bi rachman"</note> son of Ziad, son of Anham says, that he heard Hatebetum son of Hebdulzabi (may God have mercy on him) who related regarding this matter of the levels, that Gabriel <note>original: "Zagel"</note> came to the Prophet (may the prayer and peace of God be upon him) and said: "O Prophet of God, how many levels are there from here to Paradise?" He said: "One hundred levels, between any two of which the distance is as great as from the earth to heaven." The first of those levels—its space, its construction, its gate or entrance, its foundation, and its height—is made of silver. The space, building, entrance, foundation, and height of the second is made of gold. The parts of the third are of hyacinth, carbuncle, and pearls; and after that, up to ninety-seven levels, no one knows what they are except God alone. Al-Tirmidhi <note>original: "Thermindus"</note> also [says], etc. 

This is a "sensible theology" <note>Postel uses "sensible" in the philosophical sense: a theology based on physical, sensory perception rather than spiritual or intellectual truths</note> which requires no refutation, because it does not deserve belief. Among the Muslims <note>original: "Mussulmanos"</note>, God is devoid of quality, yet infinite, incomprehensible, and yet localized, finite, and susceptible to physical accidents. I shall say nothing of the heavens being wrapped within each other made of gold and silver—dense bodies; that there are snows and cold above the heaven where there is no matter; or that there is the most solid matter in a place where, by antonomasia <note>A rhetorical term for using a title or description instead of a proper name; here Postel means these materials are the very definition of "matter"</note> (unless you except diamond), it could be given the name of matter. For in all of nature, nothing is denser than gold among known things. But Muhammad’s God is delighted by these same things...

ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD.

...[God] and his prophet. We have already seen much regarding God as the final cause, and as the immediate or mediate happiness and goal of all things. For Muhammad’s paradise has frequently presented itself. Indeed, he does not grasp God in essence and contemplation as the source of happiness. He wants to drink, eat, and all that follows from those things; otherwise, he believes paradise is in vain unless it has an abundance of milk, wine, honey, meat, bread, fruit, banquets, luxury, women, catamites <term>catamites: young men or boys; Postel uses this term to attack the perceived carnal nature of the Islamic afterlife</term>, golden, silver, and silk garments, cushions, meadows, greenery, and whatever else are the instruments of luxury. 

Truly, he does not only want God to have authority in those paradises, but he says in the sixth paradise—for he claims there are various kinds—which his followers will possess after death, near the seventh in which Christ dwells, there is a fountain called Al-Kawthar <note>original: "Alcausaram"</note>. Its diameter is a journey of seventy thousand days; its water is whiter than snow and sweeter than honey, from which all who inhabit that paradise shall drink. After the day of judgment, Muhammad will go to hell and take the bad Muslims <note>original: "Muffulmanos"</note>, who are damned with black and filthy faces, and carry them to that fountain and wash them there, and they shall become most white and like the others. Thus, God will have no right over the bad Muslims, nor will hell serve any purpose. In this way, Muhammad will be far greater than God, because he will absolve those whom God has condemned. But meanwhile, those who are in paradise will drink the washing of his filth—of the bowels, the private parts, and the feet—because that same water will receive the filth and yet the blessed will drink it. O foolishness, O madness, O blasphemies! For a hundred years I could not finish transcribing the paradises of Muhammad. 

Truly, as long as I am in paradise with God, I must not omit the tree that is there, equal in size to paradise itself, with golden and silver leaves, upon which is written the name of the prophet and the name of God in these words: "There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the messenger of God" <note>original: "La alla illa alla Muhamed rassul alla"</note>. From this so great a tree, the Muhammadan persuasion takes its beginning. For they utter those words with the index finger raised when they give their names to Muhammad. But it is a wonder if that tree is equal to paradise, where men live, where there is a fountain so great, where there are rivers, hearths, ovens, weavers, goldsmiths, cushion-makers, and other citizens and craftsmen who prepare everything for those who arrive. Let these wretched fables perish. We must see if he speaks better of the angels than of God. For in this place, I do not wish to bring up more often that God—impious, unjust, an impostor, and a commander and approver of perjury, adultery, pederasty, brutality, slaughter, homicide, theft, and such things—whom I have already examined more than enough.

### CHAPTER XV. ON THE NATURE OF ANGELS.

This nature, just like the divine nature, is in Muhammad’s view corporeal, visible, tactile, and similar to us except for its size and wings. We have seen that angels are subject to wounds; otherwise, they would come as prophets and heralds in place of men, but they fear being killed. In the third heaven with Abraham, an angel was of such proportion that the space they have between their eyes is the width of a journey of seventy thousand days. Indeed, the more the heavens increase in number, the larger the angels are; so that in the seventh, where Christ is, there appear those who have seventy thousand heads, and in each head as many tongues, and from each tongue as many voices speaking praise to God. Some look out perpetually, never sleeping; others always lie prostrate, never rising from the ground; others are bowed, others standing, others with a bended knee. Some cry out with such a strained voice that they put their fingers in their ears lest they go deaf. From this, the ceremonies of praying were taken. For the individual *salawat* <note>original: "tzalauat"; refers to the formal Islamic prayers or "Salat"</note>, that is, the prayers, are performed partly by standing, partly by bending the knees, or by prostrating and kissing the ground.

Those ceremonies are called *rak'at* <term>rak'at: a unit of Islamic prayer consisting of a prescribed sequence of movements and recitations</term>, which is to say, a double bowing and prostration. Indeed, to these two prostrations and the bowings to the right and left, individual prayers correspond, such as those we saw at the beginning. Truly, those angels whose worship is observed here also possess a certain limitation, even though the head of one of them is seventy thousand times larger than the world. For when the Judgment is complete and the time for the banquet has come, God will send Gabriel to bring the keys of the holy paradise. Gabriel will go to another angel, who shall pull seventy thousand keys from his own mouth, each of which is seventy thousand days' journey in length. When Gabriel is unable to lift a key, he will go to God and say: "I cannot bring the key of paradise." To him God will say: "Turn yourself, and invoke my name and the name of Muhammad; then you shall carry it easily." He turns, invokes them, brings the key, it is opened, they enter, and they sit at a diamond table seventy thousand days in length. 

Yet, although they are so great and should be equal in wisdom, they are the ones who suggest to God that he should create a murderer <note>referring to the creation of man, whom the angels feared would shed blood</note>; they are mortal; and some are even condemned and afflicted with punishments in this life, such as Harut and Marut <note>original: "Arot & Marot"; two angels mentioned in the Quran who were tested and fell into sin at Babylon</note>. In this way, the lawgiver Muhammad, the "partner of God," explained the blessed spirits and the most holy intelligences: if the angels do not invoke him alongside God, they can do nothing. And lest anyone think anything here is a fiction, these are articles of faith among the followers of Muhammad, contained in the books of the *Siyar* <note>original: "Hassiar"; likely referring to the Sira, or biographies of the Prophet</note>, the *Sunnah* <note>original: "Suneh"; the body of traditional social and legal custom</note>, and the *Iman* <note>original: "Imamin"; the articles of faith</note>. It is a wonder that, since in the entire Quran he so often forbids men from making any person a "partner" with God, his interpreters would have him acknowledged and invoked as a partner by the angels themselves, especially since men, compelled by the necessities of matter, ought not to make any partner with God. It was necessary for liars to be mindful and to speak consistently with themselves, lest the deception betray itself.

### ON DEMONS. CHAPTER XVI.

He is no less consistent with himself when depicting their foul nature. For he says that nature was created from fire and from flame, and he repeats this ten times; but while he says that nature was disobedient to God, he establishes that same nature as wiser than God. For since nothing but the eternal ought to be worshiped by man or angel, God could not have been anything but the wicked author of idolatry by commanding the devil—created from the highest element <note>fire</note>—to so lower himself as to adore man, who was made from a drossy and muddy nature. Thus, the devil did better by not obeying than God did by commanding; and yet he is condemned for that reason. 

But he <note>Muhammad</note> does not want to admit that the devil was condemned because he sought the honors of divine power and thought to cast God down from his heaven; for that would make him irreconcilable, and he would not become a listener to the Quran, its preacher, and finally a Muslim <note>original: "Mussulman"</note>. For just as he wanted all idolaters and any others to be saved through the law of the Quran, so too he wanted to save the demons, who had sinned less. But it is a wonder how these things agree: the demons become Muslims and preach to their own people; and yet, in the book of history, it is said that when Muhammad was born, the Great Demon—Lucifer, of course—was cast into the sea by the angels, from which he barely emerged after forty days. Ascending Mount Quba <note>original: "Coba"</note> and summoning the demons with a horrific cry, he said to those asking the cause: "I rouse you with such a horrific sound because Muhammad, the son of Abdullah <note>original: "Hebdallæ"</note>, is born, whom God has sent with a radiant sword that penetrates all things, unto our ruin." And shortly after: "Because of this prophet, God has condemned me and made me the accursed Satan." To him his attendants respond: "Why are you moved, Satan? Do you not know that Adam had been created with seven virtues, of which only one remains? Do you fear that we, who prevailed against Christ, will not be able to resist this prophet?" These things are from the *Siyar*. Since the dev-

...[if the dev]il was damned through Muhammad, and if even as a small child Muhammad drove him away, how did it happen that he did not fear him when he was armed and protected by a bodyguard, but instead voluntarily converted to his belief and was saved? How is it that he made him forget the prophecies he once believed? You see that God is not the author of the devil's damnation, but Muhammad; nor was there a devil before Muhammad. Certainly Satan opposed the Gospel of Christ through Muhammad, and he could not oppose the Gospel before he became a Muslim. His associates could do what one man alone could not. Satan was not converted to the law of Muhammad, but Muhammad followed the law of the demon of darkness, of ignorance, and of the overturning of nature. He spoke prophetically only in this: that he said the demons have followers of his religion. I say nothing of the underworld and the tree of *Zaqqum* <term>Zaqqum: in Islamic tradition, a cursed tree in hell with bitter fruit shaped like the heads of devils</term>, whose branches are the heads of demons, for the additions would be countless. It is enough for us that the demon is corporeal, fears the sword, is converted to the faith of the *Quran*, will eventually die, and finally will be resurrected with the beasts. Regarding the silver and golden heaven, and the stars hanging from it by golden chains—which drive away the demons so they do not seek paradise—what need is there to speak? Yet it truly bothers me: why do the stars fear that demons might enter paradise, since the gates are always locked? Even the prophet himself, arriving with Gabriel, could not enter until they were opened; he must be worse than the demons, otherwise the doors would have opened for him of their own accord, as they do for the demons, who can only be driven away by stars hanging from chains. When I spoke of the levels, I spoke of the matter of heaven. Now you have understood the mountains, precipices, cold, and snow even in the highest heaven.

## WHAT HE ADMITTED AGAINST NATURE,
### CHAPTER XVII.

Throughout the entire law, it has been sufficiently clear that he overturned the order of things and the natural inclination of all, when he wished to persuade men that whatever crimes he allowed were from God and lawful. He wanted the "grace" granted to him (as he said) by God for perjury, adultery, fornication, effeminacy, and the killing of parents, citizens, and friends, to be lawful for everyone, so that he could not be condemned for that which he granted to all by law. What can be thought of as more shameful than "brutal" intercourse <note>likely referring to bestiality or unnatural sexual acts</note> or pederasty? Or what could be given that more completely turns into the ruin of nature? Who could have generated a greater plague among men than to pit them against each other under the pretext of piety, so that the most faithful is the strongest and the victor? What republic will ever be blessed if a citizen, in the name of religious persuasion, could justly be armed against his fellow citizens and parents? Those forces ought to have been turned against enemies. There were many famous cities in *Arabia* given to idolatry: it was necessary to compel or plunder and overturn those, not his own. He would have converted his own people sufficiently if he had dictated the law to his other neighbors. But it was not religion, but faction that persuaded him. *Abu Bakr*, *Umar*, *Ali*, *Zayd*, *Amru* <note>original: "Vbecharus, Homarus, Halys, Zeidus, Achmarus"</note>, and the other graceful and factious citizens of *Mecca* could not have supplied the prophet with strength and the heads of factions elsewhere; the prophet did not seek vengeance elsewhere. Those who knew him for what he was had offended him by describing him; they had to be destroyed. That was the "true religion": so that today in the whole earth there is nothing more inhuman than a Muslim modeling himself after the prophet's example. For since men can hardly be kept to their duty by the strictest laws, what do we think will happen when they are armed with laws against nature? "Whatever pleases is permitted"; whatever the prophet did was holy. Therefore, similar things are permitted to others. All these things take up arms against nature, they run counter to reason and public peace, and in truth they are so wicked that they seem to be wickedness itself.

## HOW THEY OPPOSE REASON. CHAPTER XVIII.

If it is permitted to judge the nature of things by similar things and their effects, who could ever persuade themselves that a man is unlike all others and divine, when everyone knows and sees that he lacks no part of vice? What prophet was ever burdened by such a foul filth of vices, and carried around such supreme impurity in both soul and body? Who among them did not confirm their words by at least a single miracle, or a true prophecy, or a singular innocence of life? Since, therefore, none of the ancients seem similar to this man, and he is in every way equal to the most wicked scoundrels, who would think he should be held among the prophets? Even if such a man spoke the most divine words or performed miracles, I would never believe him. For it is in vain that humanity, charity, innocence, friendship, chastity, sobriety, integrity, and the other better gifts of both mind and body are held as virtues, unless they find a place in the best of men. Hence, we do not hesitate to assert that he was an evil man, who not only lacked these virtues but was most uncontrollably driven and burdened by their opposites. Indeed, in Muhammad there was not just a mere lack of those virtues, but in him reigned—instead of humanity—cruelty, with which he raged against his own blood; instead of charity, the rejection of his own family so that he might give a place to harlots coming from everywhere; instead of innocence, the injustice with which he crushed everyone; instead of friendship, the hypocrisy from which he slaughtered his dearest friends while they slept; instead of chastity, that deceptiveness <note>original: "falacitas"</note> by which he mingled with fifteen wives, handmaids, beasts (for what he approved in others, he seems to have done himself), and male concubines; instead of sobriety, the greatest luxury, which he permitted even during his "Lent" <note>Postel uses "quadragesima" (the Christian 40-day Lent) to refer to the month of Ramadan to make it familiar to his readers.</note>; instead of integrity, the imposture with which he deceived everyone. And he, if it please the gods, was an intimate of God! In vain has God given to man the natural knowledge and desire for virtue if such a wicked life is "good." Either the opinions regarding the good and the virtuous are empty, or no one more wretched than Muhammad was ever born. For reason forbids that a guilty man, driven by a demon, a liar, an impostor, a deceiver, an ungodly man, and one ignorant of divine things, should be a friend to divinity.

## HOW MUCH UNHAPPINESS REPUBLICS SUFFER UNDER THIS LAW. CHAPTER XIX.

It is necessary that any Republic that receives this doctrine be oppressed by perpetual disturbances and losses. For it sins while it obeys this law, due to the lack, the abundance, or the fear of certain things. For what purpose did God, in His supreme goodness, wish the use of wine to exist in nature? Was it not so that we might use it moderately to the praise of His name? Now, through both private and public lack of wine, a most excellent part of nature perishes. Therefore, those skilled in the law laugh heartily at this precept if wine presents itself; the courtiers, soldiers, and merchants laugh, and they gorge themselves on it all the more passionately because it is so rarely permitted. For "we strive for the forbidden, and we desire what is denied" <note>A quote from the Roman poet Ovid (Amores 3.4.17): *Nitimur in vetitum semper, cupimusque negata*.</note>. The prohibition of wine is a useless prescription and most damaging to the Republic, whether you look at private affairs or the public treasury. What shall I say of the prohibitions in which the *Quran* <term>Alphurcan: Postel's transliteration of 'al-Furqan,' a name for the Quran meaning 'the Criterion'</term> agrees with the Jews? What sin is there in an animal torn by a dog, a wolf, or a bear? Do not many animals perish for the poor, whose bodies are otherwise useful? I am silent about the rest. What evil does a pig have in itself? I know Moses had prohibited it; he granted this from an ancient ritual to the children of Israel because in Egypt many were subject to leprosy, a disease from which this animal is frequently believed to suffer. They suffer from it among us as well; let them be inspected before the butcher's stall, and the meat will not harm the body it nourishes, and the lard <note>original: "axungiæ"</note> is most suitable for many uses. Nor are they more harmful in hot regions, as some say; for in all of India, under the equator, in the Moluccas, among the Chinese <note>original: "Quinas"</note>, and in Paria <note>Paria: a region in modern-day Venezuela, representing the Americas.</note>...

-># ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD<-

Nothing is more healthy or common than that animal <note>Referring to the pig, which was mentioned in the preceding text</note>: and so it is forbidden in vain. What shall I say of hunting being prohibited for four months, during which not only is utility lost, but even the poor farmers are harassed by wild boars, roe deer, stags, wolves, and lions, to whom at that time everything must be permitted. I have seen such a great abundance of wild boars in many places in Anatolia <note>original: "Natoliæ"</note> that for many miles they leave no crops undamaged. If a Christian catches one, he is beaten and crushed by a Muslim <note>original: "Muffulmano"</note>. He prefers the animal to rot and perish without use, rather than be converted to the uses for which God had given it. I say nothing of the superstitious slaughter, whereby some, in the Jewish fashion, never taste anything that was not slaughtered before their eyes, as if the soul remained in the small pieces. These things are drawn from pagan rites.

Having dismissed these lighter matters, if we proceed to estimate how many inconveniences the Muslims suffer from the abundance of ceremonies, wives, children—or rather slaves—and wandering robbers, and what calamities they feel and experience, truly the society and approval of this wicked law will seem not only useless, but adverse to peace, equity, and humanity. 

And to begin with the ritual washings <term>ablutionibus; specifically the Wudu or Ghusl</term>, if anyone remains in the ceremonies of the law, I ask, what else can he do but be washed and occupied all day long? At cock-crow, midday, evening, late, and at the first watch, everyone must be washed before they begin to pray. And if water is lacking, they are to be defiled with dust <term>original: "puluere infici," referring to the practice of Tayammum, or dry ablution with sand</term>; I do not see what could be more superstitious or more inconvenient than this. If water takes away sin, then there is no need for God; if God takes it away, there is no need for water. But if both water and God are required, then the dust is useless. For it is contradictory to wash the face, hands, arms, feet, shins, legs, and private parts, and then be defiled with dust. If these things were established for the sake of bodily cleanliness, then you wrongly use dust, which ruins it. 

But the Muslims will object with the baptism of Christians. There is no similarity. Once, into the death of Jesus Christ, we are not merely washed or scrubbed with waters purified by the blessing of the Word of God, but we are only dipped: not believing that the power of washing away sins is in the water, but by the power of the divine word and faith, when such things are done, we hope for and receive the remission of sins from God. What you do has nothing in common with us. Those things are from the Jews and the Anabaptists <note>original: "Catabaptiftis"</note>. 

Let us consider the necessities of nature—flatulence, bowel movements, urination, sexual intercourse, seminal emission—add the sins committed between the ritual washings and the prayers <term>salauat; the daily prayers or Salah</term>; who (if he wishes to be held a just observer of the law) would spend his whole day and life in anything else but in the waters, like a heron, duck, or goose, if he wished to be washed afterwards as the law commands? I leave the difficulty of winter to be considered: these are follies and ravings, which are so judged by wise men, while they utterly despise them. 

I pass over the fact that all are bound by the same laws, nor is any distinction made in that law, although those performing sacred rites have far more and more frequent duties to perform than others. Muhammad <note>original: "Muhamedes"</note> understood no distinction of orders at all, nor did he establish or care for them, even though he had overturned the state of affairs. 

What shall I say of that pilgrimage [or sacred period] of four months? No hunting is permitted then: to such an extent that many spare lice, bedbugs, and fleas. I do not touch upon the troubles of circumcision, when a boy in the vigor of youth, in the fourteenth year of his life, with the sharpest sensation, suffers his foreskin to be removed. The Jews are much wiser, who, even if they are condemned for not believing in Christ if they have heard of him, nevertheless circumcise on the eighth day as prescribed by divine law. For that fresh flesh is healed more easily than that of an adult. Moreover, a small child gives his name to the profession by the silent faith of his parents. But there was no need to become like those who, after they had established a prophet, fell away from him. 

Now if I add with what terrors the ignorant are agitated when they come to death, when they think of the two angels beating bodies in the tomb <note>A reference to the Islamic belief in the angels Munkar and Nakir, who question the dead</note>, of the soul which clothes the body like a shirt,

the body, and raises it up; belief in this is evidenced by the fact that graves are made very wide, so that corpses are able to move about and sit upright. <note>Postel refers to the Islamic belief in the "Punishment of the Grave," where the deceased is questioned by angels while sitting up.</note> Who would not laugh at such things? You hear nothing else before the judges than *talca*, *dulum*, *tzebin*, and the rest <note>These are Postel’s phonetic renderings of Arabic legal terms: *talca* for *talaq* (divorce), *dulum* for *zulm* (injustice or wrongdoing), and *tzebin* likely referring to *thaman* or *mahr* (the price or dowry).</note>: namely, repudiations, injuries, and dowries. No true faith can exist there, where there is the hope that the union will not be lasting. Friendships ought to be eternal and, as much as possible, most similar to God, who is their origin.

Suppose it were useful for divorce to be frequent because of frequent inconveniences; yet what mortal has ever been able to ensure that a flock of women sharing the same legal rights could live together in harmony? Even if you beat some of them to death, you could not impose such a rule upon them, especially if it concerns marital rights. What do we think will happen when they not only have rivals, but see handmaids and female slaves sought from everywhere and preferred over them? What peace, love, or concord can exist in those houses? Therefore, that law is in more frequent use among tyrants and the powerful, who station those women in various places. The poor, by a silent consent and by their actions condemning the law, are usually content with one wife; the prudent, sober, and continent are much more so. No one who has not seen it can believe how tyrannically and imperiously women—who are half of human nature—are treated.

Let us now consider what happens as a result of the power of this law. Let us assume a marriage is fertile on both sides. Both can procreate from the age of 14 to 50 (assuming the power of the man and woman is equal); a woman can give birth every year. I myself have known many who have given birth to 30 or 35 children. But taking away half the time—since from 15 to 50 is 35 years—let there be 18 years, and as many children from one wife. Multiply 18 by four [wives], and in 18 years there will be 72 children. If an arbitrary number from handmaids is added to these, a private citizen could generate not 72, but 100 or more children or slaves for the State. Consider from where he might be able to nourish such a flock <note>original: "gregem"</note>: so that it is no wonder there is no nation in the whole world more greedy than the Muslim <note>original: "Mussulmana"</note> nation. 

If, moreover, such a great multitude lacks their own mothers (for anyone can have sought that number from various women), and stepmothers are added, what do we think will happen? Since one stepmother can hardly bear to look upon a single stepson, will she not busy herself with removing all those who are not her own? If she does not attack them, she will certainly never care for them. A handmaid, unless the master is present, will care even less, since he can manumit her as a free woman with a small gift or sell her at his whim. Thus, the burden of such a great family must necessarily fall back upon the wretched father of the household. 

But nature has taught how fit men are for ruling a domestic family; she made them with a stronger body and a more perceptive mind for this reason: so that they might bring home the fruits of external labors and cares, while the diligent mother of the household looks after the common family and the children. I do not say how grievously this law sins against nature, since it even removes paternal love from one's own children. For although it is well known that all men are held by a desire for offspring, nevertheless, if very many children are born, the affection cannot appear equal toward all, even if they were born of one irrevocable and most beloved mother. But if they are born of handmaids and little-loved women, the father does not even care to see them. The handmaids are cast out to beggary, the offspring are exposed, and they are raised as beggars. And if someone with greater humanity takes care to raise the offspring of a handmaid at home (unless he otherwise entirely lacks legitimate children, or is very powerful), it is done so perfunctorily that his life and death are esteemed just the same. Thus, the bastards of poor and unjust men are accustomed to...

### ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

...nothing is more healthy or more common than that animal <note>Postel is likely referring to the pig, defending its consumption against the Islamic and Jewish prohibition mentioned on the previous page.</note>: therefore it is forbidden in vain. What shall I say about the prohibition of hunting for four months, during which not only is utility lost, but poor farmers are also harassed by wild boars, wild goats, deer, wolves, and lions, to whom everything must be permitted at that time? I have seen such a great abundance of wild boars in many places in **Anatolia** <note>Modern-day Turkey.</note> that for many miles they leave no crops undamaged. If a Christian captures one, he is beaten and crushed by a Muslim. He prefers it to rot and perish without use, rather than be converted to the uses for which God had given it. I say nothing of the superstitious slaughtering, such that some, in the Jewish fashion, never taste what has not been slaughtered before their eyes, as if the soul remained in the pieces. These things are drawn from pagan rites.

Leaving these lighter matters aside, if we proceed to estimate how many inconveniences the Muslims suffer from the abundance of ceremonies, wives, children—or rather slaves—and wandering bandits, and what calamities they feel and experience, truly the society and approval of such a wicked law will be seen not only as useless, but adverse to peace, equity, and humanity. And to begin with the ablutions <note>Ritual washings, known in Islam as *Wudu*.</note>: if anyone remains in the ceremonies of the law, what else, I ask, can he do all day but be washed and occupied? At cock-crow, noon, evening, late, and at the first watch, everyone must be washed before he begins to pray; and if water is lacking, he must be stained with dust <note>This refers to *Tayammum*, the ritual purification using sand or dust when water is unavailable.</note>. I do not see what could be more superstitious or more inconvenient than this. If water takes away sin, then God is no longer necessary; if God takes it away, water is not necessary. But if both water and God do so, then the dust is useless. For it is contradictory to wash the face, hands, arms, feet, shins, legs, and private parts, and then be stained with dust. If it were established for the sake of bodily cleanliness, then you apply the dust poorly, as it defiles. 

But the Muslims will object to the **baptism** of Christians. It is nothing like it. Once, into the death of Jesus Christ, we are not just washed or rinsed, but dipped in waters purified by the blessing of the word of God. We do not believe there is a power to wash away sins in the water itself, but through the power of the divine word and faith, when such things are done, we hope for and receive the remission of sins from God. What you do has nothing in common with us. Those things are from the Jews and the Anabaptists <note>Postel often links Islamic practices to those of groups he considers heretical or "legalistic," like the Anabaptists or practitioners of Jewish Law.</note>. Let us estimate the necessities of nature: the passing of gas, bowel movements, urination, sexual intercourse, nocturnal emissions—add the sins committed between ablutions and prayers <note>original: *salauat*, likely referring to the *Salat* or formal prayers.</note>—who (if he wishes to be considered a just observer of the law) could do anything else than spend his whole day and life in the water like a heron, a duck, or a goose, if he wished to be washed afterward as the law commands? 

I leave the difficulty of winter to be considered; these are follies and ravings, which are judged as such by wise men, as they utterly despise them. I am silent on the fact that all are held to the same laws, nor is there a distinction in that law, although those performing sacred rites ought to undergo far more and more frequent rituals than others. **Muhammad** understood no distinction of orders at all, just as he neither instituted nor cared for any, even though he had overturned the state of affairs. What shall I say of that four-month pilgrimage? <note>Referring to the *Hajj* and the sacred months.</note> No hunting is permitted then: to the extent that many spare even lice, bedbugs, and fleas. 

I do not touch upon the troubles of **circumcision**, when a boy in the vigor of youth, in the fourteenth year of his life, suffers his foreskin to be removed while his senses are most acute. The Jews are much wiser, who, even if they are condemned for not believing in Christ (if they have heard of him), nevertheless circumcise on the eighth day as prescribed by divine law. For that fresh flesh is healed more easily than that of an adult. To this is added that the little boy gives his name to the profession through the silent faith of his parents. But there was no need for them to become like those who, after they had established a prophet, fell away from him. Now, if I add with what terrors the ignorant are agitated when they come to death, when they think of the two angels beating the bodies in the tomb <note>Refers to the Islamic belief in Munkar and Nakir, angels who test the faith of the deceased in the grave.</note>, and of the soul which, in the manner of a shirt, clothes

...either to be wasted away, or to spend their childhood and youth in a state of lethargy, and very rarely do they reach maturity. If it happens that they do reach it, this occurs not through the benefit of their upbringing, but by their own diligence. For while they are barely born, or are just beginning to speak and walk, all domestic duties are thrust upon them as if they were slaves; yet they overcome through endurance and eventually emerge. But who would doubt that almost all Muslims <note>original: "Mussulmanos"</note> are of such a character and are valued at such a price, since all their women are esteemed no more than slaves and handmaidens? And if they are valued more highly, it is for the sake of the dowry or the family, not for the person or for love.

These are the "illustrious" effects of the Quran <note>original: "Alcorani"</note>. Yet that "prudent" lawmaker [Muhammad] provided for this vast and nearly destitute multitude. For he established an order of those who, having abandoned their own possessions, fight "in the way of God" <note>original: "militant in uia Dei"</note>, and he urged more than once that alms should be distributed to them. Indeed, such is the dregs of the common people of that sect, wherever Muhammad <note>original: "Mahumedes"</note> is heard of, that it is never safe to travel even two miles—especially if the journey must be made in Africa, Egypt, Arabia, Syria, and Asia Minor (which they call Anatolia <note>original: "Natoliam"</note>).

Therefore, it is scarcely ever safe to travel there alone, nor in a group of ten, or twenty, or even a hundred men, unless they are similar to those desperate people. A <term>caravan</term> <note>original: "Carouana"; a large group of travelers or merchants journeying together for safety</note> is necessary—that is, a cohort of several hundred or thousand men—which even then can barely protect itself from those paupers. Truly, these people are so thin that many living in Mecca <note>original: "Mechae"</note> drag out a wretched existence on scraps and the rinds of cucumbers and fruits. Some, especially in the deserts of Arabia and Syria, have reached such power that, having chosen a leader for themselves, they are formidable even to the Prince of the Turks <note>original: "Turchorum"; the Ottoman Sultan</note> himself, who is forced to buy off their harassments with payments.

Consider how true that philosophical axiom is: *Once an absurdity has been admitted, countless similar things follow.* Once a wicked scoundrel was accepted as a prophet, a most wicked law was approved. Once his decrees were received, marriages that are illicit and repugnant to nature and friendship were introduced. From these was born a mass of needy orphans, driven to desperation by their poverty; while they pretend to be preserving their law, they bring ruin and disgrace upon the entire state.

Indeed, this "plague" creeping through the fields asks for alms in such a way that if you do not give, it snatches; if you are met alone, it robs you and punishes you with terrible beatings. It even has various sects: some go naked, others semi-naked; some with heads bare, others covered. They are also of various colors: some wear clothing made of patches of every color, others have torn bodies and wide wounds—sustained (as they say) in the name of the prophet—provided that you pay them some coins.

But the "holiest" of all are those who, from the whirling of the body in a circle, lose their minds and collapse <note>A reference to the practice of Whirling Dervishes</note>. More "holy" still are those who refuse to move from their spot despite the injuries of the weather. The "greatest" are those who, pretending to have no reason, couple with female donkeys or any animal, and if none is available, they expose themselves openly. Some are devoted to specific clothes, some to worship, others to foods, regions, or places; so that no place is free of this "plague," which has sometimes proceeded to such audacity that they have even attempted to secretly attack and kill princes on several occasions.

The wretched common people have grown callous to their injuries and harassments, and in many places, having abandoned agriculture, they have either fled or joined them, preferring to live wretchedly by plunder rather than be defrauded of their daily labors. Because of this plague, Asia Minor, Syria, Mesopotamia, the Arabias, and Egypt—once the wealthiest and most cultivated provinces—are now almost sterile. Where there once were ten very wealthy cities, with their villages and villas, now there is scarcely a single fort or small village. When matters have been afflicted by war from the Muslim <note>original: "Muſſulmano"</note>, the wretched people have never been allowed to rebuild cities, cultivate fields in peace, or pay just taxes to the treasury—because everyone plunders, and no one protects. ...if they are caught; but if they remain hidden, no suspicion of wrongdoing falls upon these religious men. Some are powerful in illusions and sorcery, much like the fortune-telling women among us; they bring blight upon the crops and the livestock.
