Let the soul be persuaded in Christ, and let him appear clearly to all, depicted entirely in his own colors. For the sake of satisfaction, however, we shall not direct the cause of falsehood toward the true aim, but we shall say to the Prophet <note>Postel refers to Muhammad as "the prophet" here in a rhetorical sense to address his claims</note> that the Jews, out of hatred for Christ, urged many things contrary to the Gospel—as they indeed did—and among other things, it is clear they wished to strip away his divinity (which is evident from the universal judgment and the lives of Christ's disciples). And therefore he <note>Muhammad</note> believed them, since they were his first instructors and followers. Furthermore, those words which are in the **Quran** <note>original: "Alcorano"</note> concerning the Trinity, the divinity of Christ, and his death, are not *muhchemat* <note>original: "muhchemat"; a term in Islamic scholarship referring to clear, non-ambiguous verses</note>, that is, decisive and true. 

Certainly the true reason Christ's divinity was removed in the **Quran** was so that there would be no shared glory between **Muhammad** and **Christ**, or **Moses**. For had he subscribed to either, the glory would fall back upon them, and his acquired wealth would perish. Now therefore, having spoken of virtue and all men, and having made frequent inductions against those vices with which the false prophet teemed, as I have already said, **Muhammad** will betray himself by his [lack of] signs, and by the same labor, **Christ** and the apostles shall be exalted. And so, that there may be an abundance of evidence with which we may persuade men that **Christ’s** followers provided testimony of His divinity both in words and deeds, I have decided to append, for the sake of example, a brief summary of the lives of certain apostles and several other saints.

### BRIEF LIVES OF CERTAIN DISCIPLES OF JESUS
### CHRIST. PETER.

No one ought to precede him who was first called to the apostolic office. Therefore, in the first place, **Peter**, who was also called **Bar-Jonah**, **Cephas**, and **Simon** <note>original: "Simhon"</note>, must be described. Born in the city of **Bethsaida** <note>original: "Betsaieda"</note> situated by the **Lake of Tiberias** (which the Sacred Scriptures call the sea), **Peter** followed **Christ** for three years. He shared this miracle with Him: that while **Christ** provided proof of His divinity during the **Transfiguration**, **Peter** walked upon the seas or the lake with dry feet without a boat, just as his teacher **Christ** had done before. But because **Jesus** was present with him, that miracle might be attributed to Him more readily than those things which happened after the death of **Jesus Christ**, although all things were done in His name. 

A miracle occurred on the 50th day from the resurrection, the tenth from the ascension, when all the disciples were gathered together: the **Holy Spirit** followed in the form of a **fiery tongue**, conferring upon all that grace which they were able to give—either with or without a sign—by the laying on of hands to all who approached the faith. By that gift, they attained knowledge of all languages, than which nothing in all of nature is more wondrous. Indeed, they performed such innumerable miracles wherever on earth they traveled that they could not be contained in writing. With the whole city of **Jerusalem** <note>original: "Ierosolymitana"</note> present at the gate of the **Temple**, a man lame from his mother's womb was healed by **Peter** in the name of **Jesus Christ**. From that time, **Ananias** and his wife **Sapphira**, because they had dared to lie to God before the apostle, were struck dead by the mere word and nod of **Peter**. 

When the company was scattered into various parts, **Peter** was divinely freed from prison by an angel and led outside the city, even while he himself did not fully believe it, until he recognized that he was outside the city. While staying at **Lydda**, he restored the paralytic **Aeneas** to health. In **Joppa**, he raised a girl named **Tabitha** <note>original: "Thabithã"</note> from the dead to life. In every single city, he performed miracles. But never in such great abundance as in **Antioch**. For as many sick people as could be found from the city and the neighborhood, **Peter** healed them all, gathered in one place, in the name of **Jesus Christ**. Indeed, there was such a multitude that ten thousand believers came to the true faith on that day. And thus it happened that **Antioch** first received a place for the church, its see, and the name "**Christian**." A certain **Theophilus**, a leading man of the city, gave his own house as a see for the bishop. I do not wish here

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

Since I aim for brevity, I will mention only a few of the many conflicts between Simon Peter and Simon the Samaritan <note>Commonly known as Simon Magus, a practitioner of magic mentioned in the Book of Acts who became a recurring antagonist in early Christian legend.</note>. It is enough to know that in a single encounter, Peter took three thousand men away from Simon (who was the leader of the Sadducees after Dositheus <note>Dositheus of Samaria was a gnostic teacher; Postel here links Simon Magus to the Sadducee sect through him.</note>) and drew them from magical illusions to the true faith. Indeed, Peter refuted Simon so thoroughly that there was no place left for him in all of Syria, as the people whom he had previously deceived began to hunt him down. This plague, leaving Syria, sought out Rome to find new supporters. Once his seat was established in Antioch, Peter followed him to Rome, both for the sake of preaching the truth and for tearing down what was false. 

For his sustenance, Peter used only bread with olives, and occasionally vegetables, drinking only water; his clothing consisted of a small cloak and a tunic. These were the "baggage" of the prince of the apostles: these were his pomp, his triumphs, and his chariots. Yet under that outward poverty was a power that could command nature itself. 

In Rome, Simon the Samaritan played with men's minds using such illusions that they even erected a statue to him, inscribed **To Simon the Holy God** <note>original: "Symoni Deo sancto." This refers to a famous historical confusion; early Christian writers mistook a statue of the Sabine deity Semo Sancus for one dedicated to Simon Magus.</note>, which remained near the Tiber for a long time. Among the conflicts held in Rome with Simon (for they were many and varied), I will bring forward only the two most famous. Because the apostles eluded all his tricks and showed that the arts—with which he held great sway over that most curious monster and lover of novelties, Nero—were vain, dangerous to men, and useless, a pact was made between Peter and Simon before a great crowd: whoever could not raise a dead man to life should be put to death. 

By chance, a certain young man had died shortly before. First, Simon approached and whispered incantations; the lifeless corpse seemed to move its head. At this, the furious mob, incited by the magician, was already rushing at the holy apostles until Peter, having with difficulty obtained silence, said: "If the dead man truly lives, let him rise, walk, and speak. If he cannot do this, know that these are the illusions of evil demons. Let Simon step away from the bed, and you will see that nothing moves at all." 

When Simon stepped away and the dead man lay still, Peter approached and spoke thus: "Young man, in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, the crucified, rise and walk." Immediately he rose, walked, and spoke; he lived for a very long time afterward and provided a testimony for the apostles.

The second conflict was Simon's last, and the catastrophe of his life. Claiming he was offended by the "Galileans" (for that is what he called our people out of envy), he affirmed to Nero that he wished to leave the city he had undertaken to protect. He named a day on which the multitude should gather at the Capitol, for he intended to fly from there into heaven. On the appointed day, the people were there, the Emperor was there, and the apostles were there. Simon, circling his temples with a laurel crown like a victor, climbed the Capitol and from there began to be carried high into the air by the work of demons. But when Peter and Paul prayed, he was abandoned by the demons and fell to the earth half-dead. Carried away to Aricia by his followers because of the disgrace, he resigned his unhappy soul to the demon the following day. 

This was the end of Simon’s life, which became the cause of the apostles' deaths. For Nero, seizing the opportunity against them, did not stop until they were destined for execution. Thus Paul ended his life with his neck severed by a sword; Peter closed his days on a cross after the manner of his teacher, but with his head turned toward the ground. This is the end of those who taught the truth and lived most innocently. This is the sign of the presence of Jesus Christ—of his divinity, death, and resurrection—when such remarkable miracles are performed in his name. These things and those that follow are drawn from Luke, Clement, Linus, Cletus, Hegesippus, Tertullian, Leo I, the Genoese <note>Referring to Jacobus de Voragine, the Bishop of Genoa and author of the *Golden Legend*, a famous medieval collection of saints' lives.</note>, Gennadius, and others.

...of the dignity of Peter, I have decided to place Andrew in the second position. Having been sent by the holy assembly <note>The Council of the Apostles in Jerusalem.</note> to preach the Gospel to the Scythians <note>A group of nomadic peoples living in the regions north of the Black Sea.</note> (not the Asiatic ones, but the European ones), when they did not receive the word, he sought out the regions of Greece and arrived in Epirus and the Peloponnese. Thus, he won many for Christ within the borders of Achaia <note>A province in southern Greece.</note>. Indeed, he became famous for these miracles: When a certain young man had joined him, the youth's mother, stirred by the madness of a demon, lusted after her own son. When the son would not comply, she accused him of an attempt against his mother’s modesty. The young man was summoned and stood before the judge, calling upon Andrew as his advocate. The judge, having heard the woman’s case, sentenced the boy to death while the boy remained silent out of shame; Andrew, meanwhile, was sent to prison. For the wretched woman added this to the gravity of the case: that her son had attempted this act from the moment he had joined himself to Andrew. 

After the judge’s unjust sentence and a rebuke of the woman, Andrew was thrust into prison. As he prayed for the liberation of the youth, a lightning bolt from heaven and an earthquake from the ground arose together and consumed the wretched woman. This threw those who were present to the ground and filled everyone with such terror that they begged the apostle that they might not perish. In Nicaea, in Asia, he raised a young man who had been killed by dogs and restored him to health. Once raised, he came to Christ, as the judge of the woman and his family had done previously. Forty men were coming to him by ship for the sake of faith and baptism. A demon broke the ship and drowned them, leaving no survivors. Hearing of the miserable fate of the corpses cast upon the shore, Andrew invoked the name of Christ and recalled them all to life, training them in the sacred institutions. Finally, most famous for many other miracles, for the innocence of his life, and for his doctrine, he was fastened to a decussate cross <note>original: "cruci in decussem," an X-shaped cross, now commonly known as a Saint Andrew’s Cross.</note> by Aegeas, the proconsul of Achaia. He was seen to embrace this cross with a most ardent vow, that he might follow Christ.

### P A U L

It can hardly be judged whether we owe more to Paul for the integrity of his life, his tireless labors, and his miracles, or for his most holy writings. Certainly, a greater fruit comes to the Church daily from his writings, which breathe that divine spirit, than from his miracles, in which our "new Christians" <note>Postel likely refers here to contemporary skeptics or certain Protestant reformers who were critical of the miraculous legends found in hagiographies.</note> lose their faith. It is established from the *Acts of the Apostles* that by his imprecation, Bar-Jesus <note>original: "Bariehum," also known as Elymas.</note> the magician and false prophet was struck with blindness. This happened in Paphos, a city of Cyprus. At Lystra in Asia Minor, a lame man was healed. At Philippi, he expelled a demon from a girl from whom her masters made a great profit by her fortune-telling. In Troas, he restored to life a young man who had been killed by a fall from the windows of a roof while Paul himself was preaching. At Ephesus, he obtained by prayer that the Holy Spirit should glide into twelve men in a visible form. 

But what is more miraculous than his calling and transformation? In Sicily <note>While the New Testament places this event on Melita (Malta), Postel here follows a tradition identifying the island as Sicily.</note>, after being cast out in a shipwreck (though the men who were in his company were saved by the grace of God), he was not harmed at all by a biting viper. Through prayer, he freed a man sick with dysentery; as many as were present from the whole island who were sick were healed. Now, if anyone considers how many countless deeds he performed in Corinth and Athens, where he spent so much time, no one would believe it; he cured all kinds of diseases and raised the dead to life there, as witnessed by Dionysius his disciple, whom the Greeks call "the Great" for his distinguished learning, and "the Areopagite" <note>A judge of the Areopagus court in Athens who was converted by Paul's speech.</note> because of his office, though we use only the second name. While acting in Rome and frequently conferring with Peter, he was an aid in uncovering the deceptions of Simon. From the imperial household, he restored to life a young man very familiar to Nero, named Proclus, and brought him to Christ. Finally, he was punished by beheading by order of Nero, and with him and Peter, a countless crowd of martyrs.

As much for his intimacy with Christ as for his distinguished knowledge of divine matters, John claims a place for himself among the first. For nothing is purer than his flesh, nothing more divine than his soul (besides God), and nothing more sublime than his writings. Before Domitian regarding reli...

# ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD

...accused of [his] religion, and cast into a cauldron of boiling oil, and after he emerged from there unharmed, he was exiled to the island of Patmos, one of the Cyclades: where he lived until the death of Domitian. After Domitian's acts were rescinded by the senate, John returned to Ephesus. There he raised Drusiana <note>A woman of Ephesus whom John is traditionally said to have raised from the dead.</note> from the grave. He restored gems that had been crushed by the philosopher Crato for the sake of empty display, and he turned stones and branches into gold and gems. He raised a young man who had recently been married from the dead, destroyed a statue of Diana with a prayer, and drank poison offered by Aristodemus without harm. By the touch of his garment, the dead were raised by Aristodemus. Finally, most famous for his miracles, in the 99th year of his life, descending into his tomb on the appointed day, he disappeared covered in heavenly light. Nor was anything found in his tomb except manna.

### MATTHEW.

Matthew confirmed his preaching in Ethiopia with very many miracles, of which these are the notable ones. When the sorcerers Zaroes and Arphaxad were leading the people astray and playing tricks with illusions, he exposed their arts so that they were overcome with shame. By the sign of the cross alone and by invoking the name of Christ, he crushed and drove away dragons. He restored the son of the king of Ethiopia to life. Indeed, a fire sent by a furious prince into the holy house dedicated to virgins was extinguished by his prayer so that a divine incense crept from there into the palace; from which the prince alone barely escaped unharmed. Having been pierced through with a sword, however, he ended his life.

### PHILIP.

Philip brought those Scythians <note>Nomadic peoples of the Eurasian steppe.</note> who belong to Asia to Christ; he healed those who had been weakened by the foul breath of a serpent emerging from the shrine of Mars, having defeated the serpent; and he restored to life three high-ranking men who were even dragging the apostle to his death, but had been killed by the serpent. Finally, as an old man, he was crucified in the presence of his two daughters in Hierapolis of Phrygia. From the Acts <note>The Acts of the Apostles in the New Testament.</note> it is clear how the Spirit snatched him away for the baptism of the eunuch of Candace <note>The Queen of the Ethiopians; see Acts 8:26-40.</note>. To whom later Matthew confirmed the words of the Savior at home. Philip was the first minister of that religion which they still observe today in Ethiopic India, under that prince whom we call Prester John <note>original: "Prestoianun"; a legendary Christian king of the East.</note>. So also they report today.

### THOMAS.

Thomas, preaching in India, ordered as many as were seized by diseases in that region where he stayed to be led or carried to one very large place: and in the presence of an innumerable crowd of people, having poured out a prayer, with light coming from heaven, he healed everyone in the name of Jesus Christ. He restored the sight of the eyes, lost for a long time, to a high-ranking woman named Syntice. Finally, when Carisius, the prince of the region, forced him to fall down before idols, as he knelt and prayed, the idol was smashed to pieces by the demon dwelling within it. For which reason, having been beaten with a sword by the high priest of the false sacred rites, he ended his life. Even now in India on this side of the Ganges, there are the temples of Pulicat <note>original: "Paleacheti"</note> and Tenasserim <note>original: "Tarnaſſeri"</note>, near Narsinga <note>The Vijayanagara Empire of southern India.</note>.

<margin>Bartholomew.</margin> Preaching the word of God to Further India, Bartholomew confirmed the Gospel with many signs. He overturned all the temples, shattered the statues, raised the dead, and healed very many of the sick. Having been flayed alive, and afterwards having his head cut off, he died. His body, thrown into the sea by the heathens in a leaden coffin, arrived by divine power at the shores of Sicily, and manifested itself through a revelation. And it remained—until the Muslims plundered the city and island of Lipari nine hundred years ago—in the Church of Lipari. And from there his bones, which had previously been scattered by the Moors, were brought to Benevento, also selected by revelation. Who could follow all [the stories]? There are those who performed two hundred or more miracles. What is more miraculous than Dionysius <note>Saint Denis, the first bishop of Paris.</note> after his death? Who carried his severed head for two thousand paces? All of Paris <note>original: "Lutetia"</note> was a witness, as was the tyrant Fescennius, etc.

# WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK IV

...I was. The same also happened to Lucian of Beauvais <note>Saint Lucian of Beauvais, a 3rd-century martyr said to have carried his own head after decapitation.</note>. The followers of Muhammad also approve of the history of the **Seven Sleepers** <note>A famous legend of a group of youths who hid in a cave to escape Roman persecution and woke up centuries later; the story appears in both Christian tradition and the Quran.</note>. That story must be brought forward. Nor should we omit the deeds done in **Antioch** by the Apostles, which I mentioned above. **Mauritius** <note>Saint Maurilius, 4th-century Bishop of Angers.</note> raised **Renatus** <note>Saint René of Angers, who legend says was raised from the dead by Maurilius after being dead for seven years.</note> who had already been lying in the tomb for seven years, and after him, Renatus ruled the Bishopric of Angers most long and holily. 

Truly, no one could explain the great restraint and innocence of life found in all the followers of Christ. They considered immense weights of offered gold as nothing more than dung. Chastity, humility, charity, patience, fasting, nakedness, and other peculiar virtues belonged to them all. Whatever the world considers supreme, they did not even deign to look upon. This is the holy and certain **transformation** <note>original: "μεταμόρφωσις"</note> of Jesus Christ. These men had surpassed human capacity. It was possible for unlearned, poor, and weak men to overturn the power of both types of law <note>Divine and human law.</note> throughout the whole world. For he who moves religion must also disturb the civil state. For the <term>Commonwealth</term> <note>original: "Respub." (Respublica)</note> never allows the sacred rites of the gods to be overturned without the civil power being forced into the accepted religion by the greatest strength, whether divine or human. 

Yet, since the followers of Christ were unarmed and set out to tear down the wealthiest beliefs in the world, overturning all temples, altars, and statues of false gods by the word or sign of the cross alone, what great crowds were not stirred up by the innumerable multitude of priests and pontiffs, who boasted that they held the reins of empires? Even the best princes were forced to obey those pestilential impostors, lest they provoke the people to rebellion. Therefore, it is no wonder that there were countless thousands of witnesses to the truth of Jesus Christ. But what is more marvelous is that the more they were afflicted, the greater the multitude that approached present death; this fights against the very nature of other men. Therefore, God was, is, and shall be, in whose name those things were done. 

Now, by contrast, those most famous for their crimes should come forward: the **Caliphs**, who for the sake of greed, pride, ambition, and lust oppressed so many thousands of men and slew one another, so that nothing more clearly hostile to nature was ever born. Also to be refuted and attributed to the demon are those miracles that occur among the Muslims. For even among the idolaters, many things used to happen by the author of the demon; yet none of them knew or worshipped the true God. The demon sent diseases so that he might seem to cure them while the idol was being worshipped. This is the very thing that **witches** <note>original: "striges"</note>, magicians, and sorcerers still do today, by the same author. 

Indeed, as for the divinations found in sacred rites (unless you ask for them to be revealed to you by God through a holy man), they must be judged as having been frequent within false beliefs. For this reason, there were prophets not only for the impostor-gods Apollo and Mercury, but for every single god and goddess, who daily reported either ambiguous dreams or true ones by the impulse of the demon. Yet those laws were not good because of this, but rather were the most false by far. False miracles and divinations must be refuted by certain examples. I will bring forward one or two by way of example, which are commonly recited in the dominion of the **Turks**. 

Once, when a nation of those abandoned men (whom they call religious and holy) had conspired to kill a prince, and the leader of that faction wished to wash away the discovered crime before the prince but could not clear himself of the charges, he said he was ready to undergo a trial of his integrity in the midst of a fire unless the prince believed him. A pyre was lit; he remained in it for a long time unharmed (as they say), and certain parents of his showed off his **sandals** <note>original: "foleas", likely "soleas"</note> untouched by the fire to create faith in the matter. These are trifles: that only a few parents knew what was allegedly done in the middle of the city by the judgment of the prince, and that such a celebrated deed was not handed down in public records. Was there not a most just cause for a prince anxious for his own life to punish those men who frequently...

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

...they rise up most violently against him; these are the tricks of the Devil, devised to mock the foolish minds of the people. What shall I say of the illusions of the famous **Gothuel Mirsini** <note>This likely refers to a local saint or legendary figure in Turkish folk-Islam (possibly *Gök-el*, "Heavenly Hand") whom Postel encountered or heard of during his Eastern travels.</note>, who is held most holy among those who have lost something? The eyes of men are so played with that, passing through one place a hundred times, they do not see what—by making a "vow of eating" with those pilgrims mentioned above <note>original: "comedendi uoto". Postel refers to a folk practice where people made vows to share a meal with spiritual figures or dervishes to find lost items.</note>—is immediately offered to the eyes of all. If the saints indicate anything, they do not torment for so long, nor do they sell their works for the sake of eating. They do not bewitch the eyes. Furthermore, the saints are poorly prepared for fleeting and failing things; unless it concerns the life or safety of a person, they are almost never and very rarely present when called. **Nephesougli** <note>original: "Nepheſougli". This is Postel's transliteration of the Turkish *Nefesoğlu*, meaning "Son of the Breath," referring to people believed to be descended from spirits or dervishes with magical powers.</note>, that is, the **sons of the incubus** <note>Postel interprets these figures through a European lens as the offspring of demons.</note> (so they are called, for I have heard that there is such a rumor), are to be exhibited and thought of as the food of demons. Thus, by the collision of truth and falsehood, the truth will reveal itself without any envy and will be persuasive. Therefore, after demonstrating the excellence of both Christ and his followers through the benefits bestowed by God upon man and the corrupt nature of humanity itself, we must proceed to the proof of his divinity, frequently repeating the points above. 

**First**, that he could not be a mere man who performed miracles in his own name, and not by invoking God. **Second**, that the greatest of prophets could not have told a lie; and Christ said in many places that he was God, a word in which it was impossible for him to lie. **Third**, that he who rose of his own accord, with no one praying for him, necessarily carried God joined to his humanity. **Fourth**, that the judgment belongs to God alone. And yet, even they <note>Referring to Muslims.</note> confess that Christ will be the judge of all with a most just judgment; wherefore it is necessary for them to believe that he is God and all-knowing. **Fifth**, because he was conceived by the **Holy Spirit**, he cannot lose his female origin <note>He remains truly human through Mary.</note>; but since the Holy Spirit is God, it is necessary to confess that Christ is God. For although he is not from the Holy Spirit by descent <note>original: "ex traduce", a biological term for inheritance.</note>, but rather by guidance, yet it cannot be that he did not always have divinity with him. **Sixth**, from the integrity of the Apostles and saints. For if his disciples preferred to die rather than bow to an idol or be gifted with great honors, it is far more to be believed that they would have abhorred a lie. But in all places, they called Christ "God." Therefore, he is God. **Seventh**, he in whose name all miracles have been performed cannot but be God. But by invoking the name of Christ, all kinds of miracles have been produced by the Apostles and saints, and continue to be produced. **Eighth**, the transformation of his own people and their total dissimilarity from the world proves that their author was God. Now, if they admit the Gospel at all, how many arguments for his divinity will present themselves, which could not be performed by a prophet? He has the testimony from the Evangelists that he is from eternity. A voice from heaven, sent by the Father when he was baptized, taught: **"This is my beloved son."** The Transfiguration confirmed it, as did the prediction of his death and resurrection, the Ascension, and the sending of the Holy Spirit—all of which can belong to no mere creature.

As a final touch <note>original: "Pro colophone"</note>, there should be added (to the fact that they confess from the **Sunnah** <note>original: "Suneh", the traditional customs and practices of Islam.</note> that Christ will be the judge of all) even an article of their faith which I have taken from the **Tadhkirah of the Imam** <note>original: "Tezchere elimam". Postel is likely citing Al-Qurtubi's *Tadhkirah*, a famous work on the soul and the end times.</note>, where they have it thus: **"That in the judgment, Christ will drag Gog and Magog from their places, and they shall die; then Christ and the true believers shall remain; and nothing shall be worshipped on earth except God; and he shall travel, and those who share in his happiness shall travel with him: and they are his disciples."** This tradition—even though it is false <note>Postel considers the specific Islamic details false, even if they point to a core truth.</note>—will greatly confirm our own, since "one flock and one shepherd" can only be made by God and Christ. Indeed, it places the happiness of paradise on earth, along with the **Nicolaitans** <note>An early Christian sect mentioned in the Book of Revelation, often accused of living sensually.</note> and other heretics. But it is just as permissible to take testimony from a falsehood as long as it is believed, as it is to wrest a sword from an enemy in order to finish him off.

<header>GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK IV.</header>

# AN ARGUMENT FROM THE ORDER
## of things, and the duty of man.

After the knowledge of God and man, we must teach concerning the order of things and the duty of man: how the universe consists of the **super-celestial** <note>The realm of God and angels</note>, **celestial** <note>The stars and planets</note>, and **elemental** masses, and what things and creatures are found within them. Four kinds of things in the lower regions are evident to our senses. For some things merely *exist*, *live*, *feel*, and *understand*, such as man; brutes <note>animals</note> are devoid of intellect; plants lack sensation; while stones, metals, and the elements lack life. 

Just as the intellect is added to the first three—namely, existence, life, and sensation—to reach the highest perfection and give completion to all, so too for the highest perfection of man (which already consisted of a **triad** <note>original: "ternario"</note> of body, soul, and intellect), it was necessary for divinity to be added, and for the first creature to be joined to the highest and first Intelligence. For just as man is the fourth level up from the lowest things, so God is the fourth level up from the angels. The possibility of this thing is in God; the will of God is to desire all things for the best; and it is necessary for the salvation of man. Therefore, **Christ** was, is, and shall be God for eternity. See the arguments in the first book. 

In this life, man is born for three causes. First, for the sake of God: that he may worship, acknowledge, and love Him, and seek Him through the obedience of good works, mixed with pure goodwill, humility, and faith. Second, he exists for his own sake: that he may strive to prove himself most worthy of his Father through purity and innocence. Third—which proceeds from both—that through his service and whatever skill he possesses, he may show toward his brother (the other man) that he was not born into this life in vain. 

Although this goal is set before everyone, no one hits the mark <note>original: "collímat nemo", an archery metaphor</note> because of our **depraved nature** <note>The concept of Original Sin</note>. Therefore, there was a need for a Physician and a repairer of this life, who could heal men so affected and restore them to their original life. God does not do this by simple inspiration alone; an angel could not restore it, and much less could a man. There was a need, therefore, for a "God-man" composed as one <note>original: "homíne Deo unà composíto"</note>, who might mend our nature—such as the whole world has seen in the true followers of Christ. For they referred all things to the goal of divine honor, their own innocence, and charity; a thing which has happened to no one estranged from Christ. These and similar points sufficiently reveal the divinity in Christ. From here, we must gradually come to the rejection of the **nefarious law** <note>Postel refers here to Islamic law or the Quran</note>.

### HOW A FALSE
### persuasion is to be refuted.

Since the highest truth, wisdom, and the rest of the soul's gifts and virtues are from God, and since He is never the author of evil, there can be no falsehood, ignorance, or any vice in Him or from Him. But in the **Quran** <note>original: "Alcorano"</note> there are nine thousand lies and falsehoods; whence it is clear that it is from the devil. Any law that commands one to take up arms against nature—which God desires to be preserved—is not from God. Such is the Quran. To this point we must refer those things which, throughout the second book, were seen to fight against divine goodness, nature, art, and public peace. 

And meanwhile, while the old bond is being dissolved, this must always be kept on the lips: that **princes must be obeyed**. For when an old law is abolished and a new one introduced, we must see to it that no sedition arises. Christians are armed with **patience**, until, once things are entirely settled and a Christian magistracy is introduced, it is permitted to pursue one's rights legally. For in this we are most proven: if we suffer patiently. The restoration ought to be similar to the origin. The examples of Christ and his followers must be brought forward; there should be frequent talk of the uncertainty of fortuitous things; that by the same use, origin, and catastrophe <note>the final end or conclusion of a life</note>, princes and commoners are equal—differing in this one thing: that they consume at lunch or dinner...

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD
## Book IV (Continued)

...they rise up most urgently <note>original: "instantissime," completing the word from the previous page</note> against him: these are the tricks of the Devil, devised to mock the minds of foolish people. What shall I say of the illusions of **Gothuel Mirsini**, a most famous man and held as most holy among those who have lost anything? There, the eyes of men are so deceived that, though they pass through one place a hundred times, they do not see what immediately reveals itself to everyone’s eyes once a "vow of eating" <note>likely a ritual meal or offering</note> is made with those pilgrims whom I mentioned above. If they point out anything holy, they do not prolong the matter, lest they lose their opportunity to sell their services for the sake of eating. They do not bewitch the eyes. Moreover, the saints are little concerned with fleeting and decaying things; unless it concerns a person’s life or safety, they are hardly ever, and then only very rarely, present when called. *Nephesongli* <term>Nephesongli: Likely a corruption of a Turkish or Persian term relating to "spirit children"</term>, that is, **sons of incubi** (*if any such exist, for I have heard of them only by rumor*), are to be hissed away and considered like the offspring of demons. Thus, by the collision of truth and falsehood, the truth will reveal and urge itself forward without any envy.

Therefore, after demonstrating the benefits bestowed by God upon man, the corrupt nature of humanity, and the excellence of both Christ and his followers, one must proceed to the proof of his divinity, frequently repeating the earlier points. 

**First**, that he could not be a mere man who performed miracles in his own name, without calling upon God. 

**Second**, that the greatest of prophets could not tell a lie; yet Christ in many places called himself **God**, and in that word it was impossible for him to lie. 

**Third**, he who rose of his own accord, with no one praying for him, must necessarily have carried Divinity joined to his humanity. 

**Fourth**, only God can be the Judge. And yet even they <note>referring to Muslims</note> confess that Christ will be the judge of all with a most most just judgment; from which they ought to believe that he is God and all-knowing. 

**Fifth**, he who is conceived by the Holy Spirit cannot lose the origin of that seed; but since the Holy Spirit is God, it is necessary to confess that Christ is God. For although he is not from the Holy Spirit by way of descent <note>original: "traduce," a biological transmission</note>, but as if by guidance, yet it cannot be that he did not always have divinity with him. 

**Sixth**, from the integrity of the apostles and saints. For if his disciples preferred to die rather than bow down to an idol or be gifted with great honors, it is far more to be believed that they would have shrunk from a lie. Yet in all places they called Christ **God**. Therefore, he is God. 

**Seventh**, he in whose name all miracles were performed cannot be anything other than God. But by invoking the name of Christ, all kinds of miracles were and are performed by the apostles and saints. 

**Eighth**, the transformation of his followers and their dissimilarity to worldly people proves that their author was God. 

Now, if they admit the Gospel at all, how many arguments for his divinity will present themselves, which could not be performed by a mere prophet? He has testimony from the Evangelists that he exists from eternity. A voice from heaven taught this when he was baptized, sent from the Father: **"This is my beloved son."** It was confirmed by the Transfiguration, the prediction of his death and resurrection, the Ascension, and the sending of the Holy Spirit—all of which can belong to no mere creature.

As a closing summary <note>original: "colophone"</note>, there should be added (to the fact that they confess from the *Suneh* <term>Suneh: The Sunnah, the body of traditional social and legal custom and practice of the Islamic community</term> that Christ will be the judge of all) an article of their own faith which I have taken from the *Tezchere elimam* <term>Tezchere elimam: Tadhkirat al-A'imma (Memorial of the Imams), a Persian or Arabic work of religious traditions</term>, where they have it as follows: 

> "That in the Judgment, Christ will drag **Gog and Magog** <note>Biblical and Quranic figures representing chaos/evil</note> from their places and they shall die; then Christ and the true believers shall survive; and no one shall be worshiped on earth except God; and he shall travel as a pilgrim, and those who share in his happiness shall travel as pilgrims with him: and these are his disciples." 

This tradition especially (even though it is false) will confirm our own, since "one fold and one shepherd" <note>John 10:16</note> can only be brought about by God and Christ. However, it places the happiness of paradise on earth, as do the **Nicolaitans** <note>An early Christian sect mentioned in Revelation, often accused of heresy and sensuality</note> and other heretics. *Truly, one is permitted to take testimony from a false source as long as faith is given to it, just as one might wrest a sword from an enemy to finish him off.*

# GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK IV. EVIDENCE FROM THE ORDER
->of things, and the duty of man.<-

After the knowledge of God and man, they must be taught about the order of things and the duty of man: how the universe consists of the super-celestial, celestial, and elementary realms, and what things and creatures exist within them. Four types of things in the lower realms are evident to our senses. For some things merely exist; others live; others feel; and others understand, such as man. Beasts are devoid of intellect; plants lack sensation; and stones, metals, and elements lack life. 

Just as intellect is added to the first three—namely essence, life, and sense—to reach the highest perfection, giving completion to all; so also for the highest perfection of man (which already consisted of a triad: body, soul, and intellect), it was necessary for divinity to be added, and for the first creature <note>Postel refers here to the human nature of Christ</note> to be joined to the highest primary intelligence. For just as man is the fourth degree from the lowest things <note>The hierarchy being: 1. Element, 2. Plant, 3. Beast, 4. Man</note>, so God is the fourth degree from the angels. The possibility of this is in God; the will of God is for all things to be at their best; and it is necessary for the salvation of man. Therefore, Christ was, is, and shall be God forever. See the arguments in the first book. 

Man is born in this life for three causes. First, for the sake of God: that he may worship, acknowledge, and love Him, and seek Him through the obedience of good works, with pure goodwill mixed with humility and faith. Second, he is born for his own sake: that he may strive to prove himself most worthy of the Father through purity and innocence. Third, which proceeds from both the first and second: that he may show toward his brother—another man—through kindness and whatever skill he can, that he was not born in this life in vain. 

Toward this goal, although it is set before everyone, nevertheless no one aims correctly due to our depraved nature. Therefore, there was a need for a physician and a reformer of this life who would heal men thus afflicted and restore them to their original life. God does not do this through simple inspiration; an angel could not restore it, and much less a man. Therefore, there was a need for a "God-man" joined together, who would reform nature—the kind of reformation the whole world saw in the true followers of Christ. For they directed all things toward the goal of divine honor, personal innocence, and charity; a feat achieved by no one estranged from Christ. These and similar points sufficiently reveal the divinity in Christ. From here, one must gradually move toward the rejection of the wicked law <note>Postel refers to the Quran and Islamic law</note>.

## HOW A FALSE
### persuasion is to be refuted.

Since the highest truth, wisdom, and the other gifts and virtues of the soul are from God, and since He is never the author of evil, falsehood, ignorance, or any vice cannot be in Him or come from Him. But in the Quran <note>original: "Alcorano"</note> there are nine thousand lies and falsehoods; from this, it is clear that it is from the devil. That law which commands one to take up arms against nature, which God desires to be preserved, is not from God. Such is the Quran. 

To this point one must refer those arguments which, throughout the entire second book, were shown to fight against divine goodness, nature, art, and public peace. And meanwhile, while the old bond is being dissolved, it must always be kept on the lips that princes should be obeyed. For when an old law is abolished and a new one introduced, care must be taken lest any sedition arise. Christians are armed with patience until, once matters are entirely settled and a Christian magistrate is introduced, it is permitted to pursue one's rights legally. For in this we are most tested: if we endure patiently. 

The restoration ought to be similar to the origin. The examples of Christ and his followers must be brought forward; there should be frequent talk about the uncertainty of fortuitous things; and that princes and commoners are of equal use, origin, and final outcome <note>original: "catastrophe," used here in the sense of the final scene of a play or the end of life</note>. They can differ in this one thing only: what they consume at lunch or dinner...

princes—wealth which would be enough for countless middle-class people—should instead nourish infinite numbers of the poor. Let the great ones be covered in silk, purple, and fine linen: while hardly a cloth remains for the poor man. He is the happiest of all before God who has the fewest things, because he owes the fewest things <note>Postel is arguing that the Christian ideal of poverty and charity is a powerful tool for conversion</note>. There are many passages from the **Quran** <note>original: "Alcorano"</note> already persuasive toward this opinion. But those things which are good should be transferred into the **Gospel**: so that it clearly appears that if any good is seen in that law <note>The Islamic Law</note>, it is much better and presented in a better order in the Old and New Testaments. Thus, while they leave the nursery of false persuasion, they will feel they have lost nothing.

But once our own people are persuaded and others are dissuaded, the greatest difficulty arises from the variety of ceremonial rites. The **Muslim** <note>original: "Muhamedica"</note> people burn with no greater hatred toward us than because of our use of images. Therefore, for a time, the images of the saints should be removed, or they should be allowed their own temples <note>i.e., icon-free spaces for prayer</note>. Indeed, it would seem far better to abolish them entirely than for new converts and students of the faith <note>original: "neophyti & catechumeni"</note> to take offense at the various types of worship. Liturgies preserved in the calendar could be equally preserved and celebrated daily in the absence of an image, which has no power of its own. 

If, however, they do not want to put aside their own worship immediately, they should be tolerated rather than removed, until through the persistence of preaching the Gospel they arrive at the sincerity of doctrine and worship. Those who have taken multiple wives should be permitted to keep them, but once those wives have died or been divorced, they should be allowed to have only one. As for the sheep slaughtered at Passover <note>Postel likely refers here to the Islamic *Eid al-Adha* or *Kurban*, which he correlates to the Passover rite</note>, if someone does not want to omit that rite immediately, let the meat be eaten with the poor after invoking the name of Christ. If they do not want to be bound to all the rites of all the sacraments and prayers, they should not be pressured at first. Thus they should not be driven from their own customs against their will, except for those things which clearly sin against Christ. 

The more serious crimes with which that nation is burdened—and to which that nefarious law made a way and gave assent—must be driven out with dire imprecations and proscribed by law. Thus it will happen that by the persistence of preaching and social interaction, any prince may draw the people to true piety without any public unrest. To make this easier, he ought to abolish all privileges favoring the false law, and promulgate by edict that anyone may freely debate it privately or publicly. It should be permitted to prefer philosophical opinions over it; and meanwhile, so that whoever wishes may read the Gospel, let all the **Alfaquis** <note>Islamic legal scholars</note> and **Imams** have copies. Thus a good part of the people will recoil from foolish blasphemies of their own accord. This is the method of dealing with **Muslims** <note>original: "Mussulmanis"</note>.

### THE PAGANS TO THE TRUTH
->method of drawing.<-

Idolaters and those imbued with any false opinions about God are to be approached using common principles (as handed down in the third book). That nothing is more excellent than God, and everything is owed to Him. One must grant something to human weakness. One must not immediately resist their false opinions about God, but a certain "turning a blind eye" should be used until the people are attentive, and they should be persuaded by these logical steps:

That man is more excellent the more he is subject to and familiar with a greater power. And even if lower things seem to have some power, nevertheless all are subject to the highest God and the father of all. If the sun is believed to be God, it must be shown that he is a servant, and necessarily obeys God. Because the sun has no will, nor can it rest; since it is compelled, it has no free choice. That which has no liberty, serves; that which serves, cannot be a god. For gods must be by far the most free, most happy, and intelligent beings. From this it follows that statues, cloth, forests, and all other things are not to be held as gods. It must be shown that their material is similar to common things, in which there is no holiness. Furthermore, so that the matter can be settled with religious judgments, they should be warned that if they do not want to abolish at first sight their ancient...

worship, while preserving their wealth, offerings, and sacred rites, they might gradually attribute everything to the God of heaven, the highest of the gods. The just judgment of God must be placed before their eyes. [They must believe] that it was not some inferior power that created the universe, but God, the Highest: to whom man must give an account for the actions of his whole life. For God cannot exist unless He is just. While consulting the weakness of the people—if it cannot be done otherwise from the beginning—the power of the credited deity should be restricted to certain conditions of things: all other things should be attributed to the highest God, who is also able to do those things which they believe the inferior power can do. Thus, once the highest God is introduced, every form of idol will immediately be exploded. 

To make this easier, they should be questioned about their own rites and gods, and a refutation should be introduced from their own words. For it cannot be that those things believed and said about any inferior power are not unworthy of God. Since whatever is believed to be the highest and God must necessarily be the most powerful, the wisest, the most beneficial, blessed in Himself, and subject to no corruption or injury: it is impossible for anything else to befit Him. Thus, inferior things will betray themselves when compared with that power. 

From the enumeration of God’s benefits and a certain order, when the evangelist <note>The "Evangelista" here refers to the missionary or preacher spreading the Gospel</note> begins to speak, the common people will easily find rest. However, the prince and primary power must be persuaded by reasons—the art by which the minds of the people may be retained for them, once true persuasion and faith are admitted. The benefits received from the <term>treasury</term> <note>original: "fisco"; referring to the state's administration and public funds</note> should be recalled to the memory of the people—namely, the institution and preservation of justice, the defense of the province, the restoration of roads, the founding, growth, and preservation of cities, and the legal, sacred, and military orders—so that they may always be willing to rest satisfied with their princes. It should be promised that after they worship the true God and choose to live according to His prescriptions, they will be most happy. 

Histories of Christian affairs should be brought forward, so that they may be enticed from these false opinions to the true ones. For thus it will happen that while those whom truth does not draw by itself are led by a false opinion, they may finally, by acquiescing, become most like the good. For the counsel of Paul is to be imitated in the beginnings of persuasion. For he says: *Provided that whether by pretext or by truth Christ is announced; and in this I rejoice, and will continue to rejoice.* <note>Philippians 1:18. Postel is suggesting that even if people join the faith for the "wrong" reasons—like civic stability—the end result is still good</note>. Although the true aim of a Christian is to value nothing earthly—splendor, fame, or glory—nonetheless, it should be said that these things are greatest among Christians, and in such abundance that everyone has more than enough; this indeed does not conflict with their vow. More hopes of temporal happiness (by which most men are strongly held) can draw one to the persuasion of truth; these people will later, through holy fellowship, begin to despise the false and empty vow along with the good. 

Once faith in the highest God has been received and confirmed, faith in the Trinity will also necessarily follow. For no one can understand a Creator without understanding Him as most powerful, most wise, and most benevolent. Therefore, power, wisdom, and will must be admitted in God. Finally, the demonstration must be completed with other arguments, so that the evangelist may immediately come to the two generations of Jesus Christ—both the eternal and the temporal. In all these things, the most holy precepts of the Gospel must be taught, and how much peace they bring to those who observe them, so that a paradise may seem to be present among true Christians. Once these are persuaded, external testimonies of Gospel history should be brought forward, by which it is established that Christ was God.

### EXTERNAL TESTIMONIES REGARDING
### *The divinity and greatness of Christ.*

ALthough to men inspired by God and immediately embracing the truth, nothing could be given with greater faith than the Gospel, in which a soul conscious of good finds rest and happiness; nonetheless, because there are many more who are wicked...

...both the untrustworthy and the good and faithful, for even though some seem beyond hope, they must not be neglected. For this reason, when people are being led toward the truth of the Gospel—than which nothing is greater—certain individuals are accustomed to return to the testimonies of external authors who differ from us. The faith they do not initially receive from the Gospel, they seek from the authors of human literature; and from there, not infrequently looking into themselves, they recognize their errors and grasp the truth from the original sources themselves. Therefore, external signs must be brought forward to lead people toward faith in sacred things. Nothing offers itself as more famous than that account of the **Magi**, who came from the regions of the East, if you look toward Judea (for every position in the world is defined in relation to something else), but from the western part of Persia, traveling toward **Jerusalem**, so that in the primary city of the whole region they might inquire about the King, whom they had come to adore. There were three of them, as we learn from the Gospels themselves—men of primary authority and **sages**, which is what the word <term>Magus</term> <note>original: "Magus"; Postel explains this Persian term as meaning a "wise man" or "philosopher," rather than a "magician" in the modern sense</note> signifies. Having seen a star in their own region—not fixed in the heavens like the others, but wandering in the region of the air near the earth—they turned their eyes toward it more attentively. While they were looking to see what it might mean (for they were a nation most attentive to observing the celestial bodies), there appeared in it—as they themselves used to tell, and as has been faithfully handed down through the generations—the form of a boy with a body all of fire. This figure said to them that a boy had been born in Judea who would rule over the Jews and the world, and that they must travel there and adore him. They placed their faith in these words, and having quickly ordered their **camels** and **dromedaries**, they passed through the deserts of Arabia and the land of the **Midianites**, entering Jerusalem on the 13th day to seek news of the boy from the wise men.

When our interpreters say that the journey was a miraculous one of thirteen days from the [far] East into Judea, they are mistaken. For they are confused by the word "East," thinking it has only one simple meaning, whereas it is multifaceted. For the "East" is relative to something else; no position of the East is so fixed that the same place might not also be the South or the West in different comparisons. For at every point in the sky where the sun acts, it always creates an East, a Noon, and a West. Many understand "from the East" to mean from a distance of 90 degrees, or a quarter of the heavens. But since dromedary camels, although they can travel 60 miles in a natural day, could not have come from such a distance to Jerusalem in fewer than ninety days. Therefore, they came from the region of the Magi, which is called **Persia** and is adjacent to the Persian Sea; it is distant from central Syria (the land of the Phoenicians) by 13 degrees of longitude, sharing the same latitude. In that latitude, a degree of longitude contains about 55 miles. This journey fits perfectly with the moderate pace of dromedaries. For the fastest daily run is 60 miles, as I said; the slowest is 45, and the average is 54. If there were 13 degrees of distance, they would have had to cover 60 miles each day. The entire journey would have been 690 miles. However, in thirteen days, allowing for some care for the animals, they arrived by a moderate pace of 515 miles. <note>Postel is using complex geographical calculations to prove that the "13 days" mentioned in tradition is scientifically plausible if the Magi came from Persia rather than the furthest reaches of the Orient.</note>

They had to pass through the region of the **Midianites** so that the prophecies might be fulfilled. For **Isaiah** says in chapter 60: *A multitude of camels shall cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all those from Sheba shall come, bringing gold and incense, and announcing the praise of the Lord.* These words describe the reality. For **Midian** is the eastern part of desert Arabia; **Ephah** marks a part of "Happy Arabia" <note>original: "Arabia felix"; a classical geographical term for the fertile southern part of the Arabian Peninsula</note>; and the region of **Sheba** refers to all the Arabias, and especially the South. Therefore, their dominion extended to the Persian Gulf. Furthermore, **David** calls them kings, saying of God: *Kings shall offer gifts to you* (Psalm 68). And likewise: *The kings of the sea and the islands shall offer gifts, the kings of the Arabs and of Sheba shall bring presents.* They were indeed kings of the islands and of the Persian Sea, and truly worthy of the name by their reputation alone; thus Christ approved their rule as if it were the only legitimate one...

...revolved. For they were such as the most fortunate republics have experienced, and such as **Plato** desired for his own republic, which he wrote would then truly be blessed: **either when the prince shall practice philosophy, or the king shall be a philosopher.** <note>Postel is referencing Plato’s *Republic* (473d), arguing that the Magi represented this ideal union of intellectual wisdom and political power.</note> For among others, the world is usually shaken no less than it is ruled. All the literature of every nation testifies that the **Magi of the Persians** possessed remarkable wisdom. It is handed down in writing that these men were kings and presided over the highest affairs of state. That region which was ruled by the Magi selected twelve primary men of wisdom to be in charge of the highest matters. From that number, they would select by vote three who would hold the reins of the kingdom for each year; these men would **watch the heavens** <note>original: "de cœlo seruarent"; referring to the Magi's role as astronomers and omen-readers.</note> and, if any urgent matter arose, they could attend to it immediately. These three elected for that year were the highest philosophers, true kings, and most worthy of the name.

Coming from such a distant region, when they had asked the leaders of the Jews the location of the newborn boy, they greeted him in the **City of David** [Bethlehem]. To the infant, who was surrounded by the extreme nakedness of all things, they offered gifts worthy of emperors. After these things were accomplished, they departed to complete the administration of their own magistracy. They died as happy men and as **Christians** in that same region. For this reason, 300 years later, **Helena**, the mother of the Emperor Constantine, while she was searching for the Holy Cross, took care to have their bodies brought to her, and they were carried to Constantinople. From there, through the holy **Eustorgius**, the Bishop of Milan, they were translated to his see; and from there they were brought to **Cologne** by the Emperor Henry, <note>Postel refers to the tradition of the "Three Kings." While historical records usually credit Frederick Barbarossa with moving the relics to Cologne in 1164, Postel attributes it to an "Emperor Henry."</note> where they are famous for the power of their miracles.

Now to the deeper history. When **King Herod**, a foreigner, had killed all those of royal blood—possessing the empire through crime and the death of its lords (for he had been a servant of the **Maccabean** princes)—and being most greedy to retain his part, he heard from the Magi about the "King of the Jews." Then, with feigned benevolence, he asked them to report back to him about the boy. When he heard that they had not done so, but had departed, he ordered that all children from two years old and under within the borders of the City of David (which is called **Bethlehem**) be removed and killed, lest the boy escape. This crime was not only known within the narrow borders of Judea, but was immediately reported to **Augustus Caesar** in Rome.

**Macrobius**, a man entirely foreign to our faith, will be a rich witness for us in this matter. For he writes thus in his *Jests of Augustus*: **"When Augustus had heard that among the boys under two years old whom Herod, the King of the Jews, ordered to be killed in Syria, Herod’s own son was also slain, he said: 'It is better to be Herod’s pig than his son.'"** <note>original: "Melius est Herodis porcu esse q̃ filiu." This is a famous pun attributed to Augustus. In Greek, the words for "pig" (*hys*) and "son" (*huios*) sound similar. Augustus was mocking Herod for following Jewish law by not eating pork, yet violating basic humanity by killing his own family.</note> This was written by Macrobius, an otherwise impious man. Listen, you impious ones, who place more trust in the authors of human learning than in the Gospel! Macrobius subscribes to the Evangelist. It is established that it was done.

Indeed, what great madness could have seized a man otherwise so greedy for splendor and glory, that he would take upon himself the stain of such a monstrous crime and accept such a mark upon his reputation? What could that most innocent age have done to offend him so much that he would kill his own son along with the others? Certainly, he had received word from the Magi that the **King of the Jews** and the **Emperor of the World** had been born. Otherwise, he would never have committed that crime. The splendor of empire alone dissolves and ruins all things, both divine and human. It was necessary, by the grace of that occasion, that the man should have come to such a state of madness that he turned the sword into his own bowels. **Josephus** concurs when he says: **"Whomever he knew to be of royal blood, or those from whom someone might reach the hope of the kingdom, he ordered them all to be killed."** He removed and killed the entire Senate, saving only one who had predicted his rule. So great was the man's cruelty in that regard that the number of the slain seemed innumerable. The histories of the Romans support the Gospel. It was a firm conviction among the Jews, as **Suetonius** says, that a ruler of the world would be born among them at that time. This was so widely published among foreign nations that, at that time, the power of the Jews was formidable to the Romans. Therefore, they broke that province with so many wars, and with their own...

...handed over to be ruled by a Roman governor given to the people on account of seditions. That rumor was not false. For then He was born, who **came unto His own, and His own received Him not.** <note>A reference to John 1:11, used here to frame Christ’s arrival in the Roman-occupied world.</note> Numerous literary monuments provide evidence for the miracles that occurred in 그 year. **Three suns** were seen for a long time, which finally merged into one: something that is not read to have happened at any other time. For **sundogs** <note>original: "παρήλιοι" (parhelioi); an atmospheric phenomenon where multiple suns appear due to ice crystals in the clouds.</note>, which occur frequently and represent two or three suns, never merge, but disappear as the impression on the cloud vanishes. These were certainly proofs of the Divinity visiting men more closely, signifying the **One and Triune God**.

The Romans did not know that the most majestic temple they had recently built—founded because of the long-lasting peace they enjoyed under **Augustus**—was struck by lightning from heaven because a **virgin had given birth**. For in that year, which was the 42nd of Augustus’s reign, the **Temple of Peace**, which was believed to be eternal in opinion and called so by its title, was struck by a lightning bolt. Indeed, when that temple was built, the Romans, no less needy than they were desirous of long-lasting peace, consulted the oracle of **Apollo** as to how long such a magnificent temple dedicated to Peace would last. The response given by a demon was that it would last **until a virgin gives birth**. They, thinking it would be an eternal work, inscribed the title over the doors: *The Eternal Temple of Peace*. Finally, in the 12th year from that time when Christ was born, the immense mass collapsed to its foundations. After the Christians living in Rome heard of this many years later, they established a temple there to the **Divine Virgin**, which they now call **Santa Maria Nuova**. <note>Now known as the Basilica of Santa Francesca Romana near the Roman Forum.</note> How could it happen that a work so recent, so sound, and so large could collapse in such a way, with no earthquake shaking the City? Certainly, a peace other than a human one had come into the world: the Author of Peace, God, had lowered Himself among men, so that He might confer upon all the inhabitants of the world who believe in Him that peace which we are unable to achieve in this life by any human skill without Him. For **peace is not merely a rest from war.** There is a need for **pacified minds** (as the best philosophers have urged) before there can be any true rest in a man. It is not within human skill for anyone to achieve it without the knowledge of the wisdom of God.

What shall I say of the **Augustan Basilica**, which later brought the name of the "Praetorium" <note>A term for a general's tent or a governor's palace, here referring to a space converted for Christian worship.</note> to sacred rites? Certainly, without the sight of a miracle, a prince alienated from the true religion would not have made a sacred place and a basilica in the middle of his houses. Yet there is a place dedicated to the Virgin in the **Golden Heaven** <note>Postel refers to the *Ara Coeli* (Altar of Heaven), located on the Capitoline Hill.</note>, where the temple constructed today still stands. **Orosius**, a diligent historian, says that in a clear sky at the third hour, Augustus saw the sun surrounded by a golden color. While he was held in admiration of this thing, he consulted the **Sibyl** <note>The Tiburtine Sibyl, who in medieval legend showed Augustus a vision of the Virgin and Child.</note> as to what this sign meant for him. She said that very soon one would be born who was to be worshiped by him and the whole world. Therefore, he should take the greatest care not to accept the divine honors offered to him by the Roman people, but should worship Him who was to be born. On this account, he wanted the place in which he had seen that vision to be sacred to the **unknown deity**, until it was dedicated by our people, who know the true God, as a temple to the **Virgin Mother**, and called "in the Golden Heaven." In imitation of this, basilicas have been constructed under the same title in many places in Italy.

What shall I say of the **fountain** from which a spring of oil gushed forth at Rome for an entire day when Christ was born? I could bring forward innumerable miracles from our own authors, but they would not command the faith of our apostates. **Pagan doctrine is needed for pagans.** They prefer to believe **Lucian** rather than the Evangelists. If we come to those signs which occurred at the death of the humanity of Christ, what a great abundance of external witnesses will support our Evangelists! That **marvelous eclipse**, which lasted for three hours, and which was preserved for a very long time in the archives of the Romans, noted in the diaries of the Persians, written of by **Phlegon**, and observed by **Dionysius the Areopagite** and **Apollophanes**, since it was contrary to nature...

Both by the span of time and the opposition of the stars, it could not fail to signify that its Author also suffered an eclipse <note>original: "deliquium"; literally a failure or a fainting, here used to mean a solar eclipse.</note> of the body. That this was against the laws of nature is shown by the opposition of the heavenly bodies. For it was the 14th day of the moon <note>This refers to the full moon of Passover. A solar eclipse naturally occurs only during a new moon, when the moon is between the Earth and the Sun.</note>, at which time the moon itself can be deprived of the sun's light because the earth is positioned diametrically between them—but the sun certainly cannot. For an eclipse of the sun can only happen during a conjunction <note>original: "synodo"; the meeting of the sun and moon in the sky.</note>. Furthermore, the duration of three hours was also against nature, since the natural limit for half-durations <note>A technical term in Renaissance astronomy regarding the phases of an eclipse.</note> never usually exceeds ten-twelfths of an hour. It was fitting that the Author of all things should suffer according to his humanity, since the most glorious parts of the heavens failed at his death.

Who does not know that there was a universal earthquake, greater than any recorded in the memory of literature? For its violence was noted both in Asia and in Rome; whereas otherwise, other earthquakes are never universal, and indeed they scarcely extend to the visible horizon on earth, or about two hundred miles. If they do exceed this, they only disturb specific regions or provinces. For since it is a natural occurrence, it is necessary that the other parts of the earth remain fixed and steady to offer resistance when one part is shaken. For without resistance and a fixed point, motion cannot occur, even in animals; how much less in so vast a mass as the earth? **Pliny** <note>Pliny the Elder, in his *Natural History*.</note> noted that this happened in the times of **Tiberius**.

In the times of that same prince, what did those shrieks of demons mean—those messengers of this very event who moved so swiftly? This same agitation of demons was felt even at the ends of the world. Surely at the death of even the greatest man or prophet, nothing similar ever happened. Let the passing of the holiest men be estimated; let the deaths of the most famous men be weighed. Let **Osiris**, **Cambyses**, **Xerxes**, **Alexander**, and **Augustus** step forward into the center: what greater figures has the world seen among men? They had the greatest supporters and flatterers, who would even "make an elephant out of a mouse." Yet when they departed from life, absolutely no similar prodigy occurred.

Unless these things had happened at the death of Christ, how could it have been possible that the **Apostles** and **Evangelists**—the lowliest class of men, destitute of human protection—would have dared to propose such things to a world so eagle-eyed and such a diligent observer of all famous events? If even the slightest suspicion of a lie had fallen upon them, the Gospel would never have found a place. Our records were attacked by **Porphyry**, **Celsus**, and **Julian** <note>These were famous pagan critics of early Christianity.</note>. All of them testify to these crimes <note>original: "facinora"; used here in a heavy sense to describe the "suffering" or "violent disruptions" of nature.</note> of a wandering and laboring nature. Unless these events had been thoroughly proven by the monuments of all nations, these critics would not have passed them over, since they were eager to pluck at even the tiny accents <note>original: "apiculos"; literally the small strokes or points in writing, meaning the smallest details.</note> (or anything even more minute) in our writings with a mind for contradiction.

I do not even bring forward the opinion of **Josephus** concerning Jesus Christ and his miraculous works. I pass over the letter of **Abgar**. I do not repeat what **Pilate** wrote about him to Tiberius. I omit the judgment of **Philo** regarding our **Therapeutae** <note>A Jewish sect described by Philo of Alexandria, whom early Christians like Postel often identified as the first monks or Christians.</note>. All know from the letters of **Pliny the Younger** of the innocence of our people, and with what worship they performed sacred rites to Christ. The letter of **Marcus Aurelius** survives, concerning the water obtained by divine means through a Christian soldier. **Suetonius** called our people "malefactors" for this reason: because the priests of the idols interpreted the miracles performed in the name of Christ in a sinister way. **Tacitus** is in the same error.

In the same fault are the **Jews**, who in their **Talmudic** traditions, even now do not cease to attack Christ. Some call him a sorcerer and a worker of evil; others say he performed miracles using the name <term>יהוה</term> <note>The Tetragrammaton, the holy four-letter name of God. Postel is referencing a medieval Jewish legend that Jesus stole the secret name of God from the Temple to perform miracles.</note> which he had taken from the sacred stone of the Temple and hidden from the gatekeepers—lions that were a thousand years old. All agree on this point: that he surpassed human faculty. His divinity is truly confirmed by the prediction of the overthrow of Jewish affairs. For, as we have seen from Jewish records, because of the killing of Christ, six million men were slain in two Roman expeditions; and from the death of Jesus Christ, Jews everywhere on earth are oppressed by slavery and serve, being entirely destitute of liberty.

The Emperor **Julian the Apostate** provided the greatest confirmation of the divinity of Christ when he turned away from the truth in Jerusalem. For when, in his hatred for the "Galileans" (as he [scornfully...]

...he was accustomed to criticize with sarcasm and mockery) <note>This sentence begins mid-thought, referring to the Emperor Julian, known as "the Apostate."</note> he wished to bring back the nation of the Jews to Jerusalem to cause envy and reproach—for that people was then suppliant and interceding with that impious man by means of gifts. He gathered a vast number of them so that, before the others could arrive from elsewhere, they might restore the Temple in the place where it had been three times constructed and destroyed. It is marvelous to tell and wonderful in the doing: when the foundations were being dug out more deeply, and while the leading men and their craftsmen were about to lay the foundations of the work, globes of flames erupted from the bowels of the earth. These consumed many of them not once but twice, and they ceased from the undertaken work, having even been touched by fire from heaven.
