# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD
## BOOK IV

...[sacrifices] converged into Judea; for the time predicted by the prophets had reached its limit, the time in which the Messiah was to come. But because Christ was not a tyrant, and because he was (as I have said, and as is clear from his life) most like unto God even according to the flesh; because he claimed no worldly power for himself, but spent all his efforts on the comfort of the afflicted and the miserable; because he trampled on worldly honors and publicly rebuked the vices of the wicked magistrates and priests—not only did they not follow him as their leader, but their leaders even punished him with death. 

Truly, that the Jews had converged from the whole world into Syria in the hope of some bloody Messiah, who would finish off the rest of mankind by overturning the world and prepare for them a vast dominion over all things, is proven by that incredible multitude of people who perished under **Titus** and **Hadrian**. For shortly before, under the **Maccabees** <note>The Hasmonean dynasty that ruled Judea in the 2nd and 1st centuries BCE.</note>—who immediately preceded **Herod** the foreigner, under whom Christ came—the greatest Jewish forces could scarcely reach ten thousand men, as their affairs were frequently worn down. Yet, as they were constantly in motion, within sixty years they had converged into such a great multitude that eleven hundred thousand <note>1,100,000</note> were shut up in Jerusalem during the siege by Titus. 

Furthermore, according to the report of **Hegesippus** <note>A 2nd-century Christian chronicler who wrote about the history of the Church and the Jewish wars.</note>, a man of the Jewish race, twenty hundred thousand <note>2,000,000</note> people in total were lost in that war. Then, fifty years later, under the second **Bar Kokhba** <note>original: "Barchoziba." Simon bar Kokhba led the second major Jewish revolt against Rome (132–136 CE). His name "Bar Koziba" means "Son of a Lie," a title given to him by those who considered him a false messiah.</note>, forty hundred thousand <note>4,000,000</note> people were killed when **Betar** <note>original: "Betora." The last standing fortress of the Bar Kokhba revolt.</note> was overturned, according to your own authors. They add that in the territories of **Alexandria**, 700,000 <note>original: "70 myriadas"</note> were killed by the same. Some say that forty million <note>original: "quater mille myriades"</note> were finished off in Betar or thereabouts, from which there was such a great rush of blood flowing from that slaughter that huge stones were swept away by the torrents of blood, from there toward the sea, and from there toward the **Lake of Gennesaret** <note>The Sea of Galilee.</note>.

Mention is made of the first Bar Kokhba by **Rabbi Moses the Egyptian** <note>Maimonides, also known as the Rambam.</note>, whom they call **Ben Maimon** <note>original: "Ben mannon."</note>, in the *Laws of Kings* <note>original: "sententijs regum"</note>, where he speaks of **Rabbi Akiva** <note>original: "Alziba."</note>, the supporter of the Bar Kokhbas and an author of the **Talmud**. Further, in the book of *The Sanhedrin* <note>original: "συνεδρῶν [synedrōn]"</note>, which they call *Sanedem*, in the chapter *Helek*, and in *Ekhah Rabbati* <note>The Midrashic commentary on the Book of Lamentations.</note>, that is, the commentaries on the Lamentations of Jeremiah, where it is said: *Her enemies have become the head, etc.* <note>Lamentations 1:5.</note> Truly, in the book *Megillah* <note>A tractate of the Talmud concerning the festival of Purim.</note> there is much on these matters. Concerning the second Bar Kokhba, however, there is information in many places, but most especially in *Bereshit Rabbah* <note>The Midrashic commentary on the Book of Genesis.</note>. Let **Rabbi Johanan** be read there upon that verse: *The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau, etc.* <note>Genesis 27:22.</note> Likewise in the book *Ekhah Rabbati*, and in the tractate *Gittin* <note>original: "Maschet haghittim." A Talmudic tractate on divorce and legal documents.</note>, in the chapter *Hammazikhin*. 

But meanwhile, that which they themselves pass down concerning their second Bar Kokhba must not be omitted. For it strongly confirms what I brought forward earlier; they record that such a great multitude converged from everywhere in Judea in the hope of a future Messiah, that four hundred thousand devoted men joined him—each having cut off one of his fingers and uprooted a cedar tree as a test of recruitment. Relying on this multitude, he broke out into these words:

->Lord of the world, do not support us, nor help us, nor give us courage. Have you not rejected us? Do not go out with our armies.<-

However, after **Hadrian** had besieged the city for three months and captured it, a certain soldier brought the severed head of Bar Kokhba to the Emperor, and the Emperor commanded him to see that the trunk of the body be brought to him. The soldier returned immediately and found a serpent of unusual size wrapped around the headless body. When Hadrian heard this, he said: "In truth, unless their God had killed this man, no mortal could have overcome him." These things are in *Ekhah Rabbati* and *Bereshit Rabbah*. 

Certainly, the Jews had been forced together from the whole world, not so that they might reign or obey bloody Messiahs, but so that the entire nation might truly pay the penalties for the crime committed against **Jesus Christ**, and so that the survivors might serve a perpetual and harsh servitude among all nations, along with the dire memory of that slaughter. It was necessary, O Jews, for the prophecies to be fulfilled in you.

## ON THE REJECTION OF THE JEWS.

In the first place, I will set down those passages by which the rejection of the Israelite race is made evident; secondly, I will resolve their objections; then, what kind of Messiah and what kind of condition of things they are to have under him; and lastly, I will gather the gospel prophecy from the prophets: so that it may be clear whether our Christ is such as the prophets described. That the whole nation is not to be gathered, but only the remnants, is clear from these places. Isaiah 10, after speaking of Assyria, also adds a note regarding a second punishment: *The light of Israel shall be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame; and his thorns and briars shall be kindled and devoured in one day.* <note>Isaiah 10:17</note> Shortly after: *And the remnant of the trees of his forest shall be so few in number that a child could write them down.* These things must have been spoken concerning a certain false prince and regarding a total slaughter. For from the Babylonian captivity, many thousands of captives survived. Therefore, these things were said not of that captivity, but of the slaughter of lost men under a lost prince, whom they considered to be the "light," as was the case with both leaders named Bachoziba <note>original: "Bachoziba." Postel refers to Simon bar Kokhba, leader of the Jewish revolt (132–136 CE). His name was originally Bar Kosiba, but supporters called him Bar Kokhba, "Son of the Star." After the defeat, critics called him Bar Koziba, "Son of a Lie."</note>. For those who survived the slaughter at Jerusalem and Bethar could indeed have been written down by a child. It follows: *And it shall come to pass in that day, the remnant of Israel, and those who have escaped from the house of Jacob, shall no longer lean upon him who struck them, but shall lean upon the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.* <note>Isaiah 10:20</note> All these things are consistent. For before the factions arose under **Titus** and **Hadrian**, they leaned upon the Romans—who eventually struck them—until after the slaughter took place in Bethar <note>original: "Betora." The fortress where the Bar Kokhba revolt ended in 135 CE.</note>, when many were converted to the faith of Christ. *The remnant,* says the prophet, *shall return—the remnant, I say, of Jacob, to the mighty God. For though your people Israel be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them shall return,* etc. He does not say the whole multitude, but that its remnants are to be saved; for the ones to be saved were few—the Apostles and disciples of Christ and a great number in our primitive church. Thus, the much greater part was to perish by slaughter, the smaller part to be saved, and the rest to be kept in stubbornness as a perpetual mockery for all nations. 

Truly, the Spirit said through Jeremiah that the remnants would be so small relative to the whole that nothing would seem to remain. He says in chapter 11: *Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts* (because they had rejected and killed Christ), *Behold, I will visit them: the young men shall die by the sword, their sons and their daughters shall die by famine, and there shall be no remnant of them.* Although Jeremiah is speaking of Anathoth <note>Jeremiah's home village.</note>, nevertheless, under that name, he speaks of the whole race of Israel. Indeed, there was no long-lasting siege by the Assyrians at that time, so they did not suffer from famine then in Jerusalem; therefore, this must be referred to the second destructions <note>The Roman destructions of 70 CE and 135 CE.</note>. 

In Ezekiel 9, is it not clearly evident that those who were not marked with the sign **T** <note>The letter "Tau." In the ancient Hebrew script, this letter was shaped like a cross (+ or x). Postel and other Renaissance scholars saw this as a prophecy of the Cross of Christ.</note>—that is, the Holy Cross—were to be entirely taken away and exterminated? Is it not so that when **Titus** came to the siege of Jerusalem, a voice was heard in heaven, repeating this several times: *Let us depart from here, let us depart from here*? And the Jews were so blinded that none could leave; but all the Christians left, who were marked with the sign Tau. So says the prophet: *And he cried in my ears with a loud voice, saying: The overseers of the city have approached, and each was endowed with a weapon in his hand; and behold, six men came from the way of the upper gate, which faces the north, each having instruments of destruction in his hand.* And a little later: *And the Lord said to the man clothed in white garments* (for Christ took punishment from you using the Romans as an instrument) *who was in the midst of the others: Go through the city, and mark a Tau upon the foreheads of the men who are grieved by the abominations. And he said to the others: Go through the city, following him, and strike. Let not your eye spare, nor have mercy.*

Entire provinces of the Gentiles have come to the Lord Jesus Christ; yet the unfaithful Jews were unwilling to receive him, except for a very few half-forced remnants.

For it is most proven in many places that the people of Israel are called a "fornicating woman," who has committed fornication in her inventions with stone and wood. Therefore, the prophet says three children—a son, a daughter, and a son—were born from fornication. The first condition is in the name of the first son, concerning the crimes which were the cause of the overturning and the Babylonian captivity, along with the captivity itself, for which God had mercy. The second condition, placed in the name of the daughter, signifies those consumed in the destruction by Titus and Hadrian; and therefore she is called **Without Mercy**. <note>In Hebrew, *Lo-Ruhamah*.</note> The third son is called **Not My People**, <note>In Hebrew, *Lo-Ammi*.</note> by which the present condition of the Jews is signified. **Gomer daughter of Diblaim** <note>The wife God commanded Hosea to marry.</note> was a certain famous and infamous prostitute of that time, in my judgment, whom he took as a type of a nefarious people; just as if someone, because of crimes, had called the Romans "Flora," or the Athenians "Lais" or "Phryne." <note>Postel compares the biblical Gomer to famous courtesans of Roman and Greek antiquity to illustrate the metaphor.</note> He says: "Go, take for yourself a wife of fornications, and make for yourself children of fornications, because the land commits fornication assidue, being alienated from the Lord." And he went and took Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son, and the Lord said to him: "Call his name **Seed of God**, or **Jezreel**, for in a little while I will visit the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and I will cause the kingdom of the house of Israel to cease. And on that day I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel." And she conceived again and bore a daughter, and He said to him: "Call her name **Without Mercy**, for I will no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, but I will utterly forget them." And do...

He uses the names of Hosea’s children as an allegorical timeline for the Jewish people's rejection by God after the time of Christ.</summary>

-># ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD<-

### BOOK II

<page-num>368</page-num>

...I will have mercy on the house of Judah, and I will save them in the Lord their God. And I will not save them by the bow, nor by the sword, nor by war, nor by horses, nor by horsemen. And she weaned her who was called "Without Mercy." And she conceived and bore a son, and he said: Call his name "Not My People," for you are not my people, and I will not be yours. And the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea which is without measure, and shall be innumerable; and it shall be in the place where it was said to them, "You are not my people," it shall be said to them, "Sons of the living God." And the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together, and they shall appoint for themselves one head, and shall come up from the land, for great is the day of the seed of God. <note>Postel is quoting Hosea 1:7–11. He interprets these verses as a prophecy of the Jews being replaced by Christians.</note> Pay attention to these individual points, O Jews; pay attention, I beseech you by the mercy of God, for your salvation is at stake. Each detail must be examined diligently, and it will appear as if the prophet has woven a history of future events. 

The prostitute synagogue named **Gomer** is clear enough. <note>In the Book of Hosea, Gomer is the unfaithful wife of the prophet, symbolizing Israel's perceived unfaithfulness to God.</note> For although God did all good things for her, and expected her to produce grapes, she produced only wild grapes for Him; He cultivated her like a vineyard, but she produced fruit like a wild field. He held her in the place of a wife, yet she scarcely held God the Father in the place of anything but an adulterer and a rival. Truly, His son—whom the ox and the ass recognized in the manger <note>A reference to Isaiah 1:3, traditionally associated with the Nativity of Jesus.</note>—His own people did not recognize, but killed most cruelly as an enemy. 

As for why the first is called the "seed of God," the reason is that there were still many good people before the captivity and before Christ, and because the "seed" of Jesus Christ was preserved in them, as **Isaiah** says: *Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us a seed* <note>original: "nisi Dominus exercituum reliquisset nobis semen"</note>—that is, the future Messiah—*we would have been like Sodoma and Gomorrah.* And for that reason He did not exterminate them, but the Lord caused the kingdom of Judah to rest for seventy years under the power of the Assyrians, which happened shortly thereafter, and the strength of Israel was broken in the **Valley of Jezreel**. <note>original: "ualle Iefrahel"</note> For because of the displayed wealth of the House of the Lord, punishment came from a foreign king, and it was accelerated, beginning with the Lord's first servants. 

The daughter is called "Without Mercy" <note>Hosea's daughter, Lo-Ruhamah.</note> because after Jesus Christ was killed, everyone was slaughtered to the point of extermination—regardless of age, sex, rank, or order—so that God was clearly moved by no mercy toward that wicked nation. Otherwise, He is accustomed to mitigate the fury even of barbarians, lest they rage against the innocent. Thus the Lord willed to sharpen the anger of **Titus**, **Trajan**, and **Hadrian** <note>Roman Emperors who oversaw the suppression of Jewish revolts in 70 AD, 115–117 AD, and 132–136 AD respectively.</note> so that the Jews might pay the penalty for killing His son and for selling the Just One and their brother. 

Indeed, when the Lord permits wars to be launched against nations estranged from God, He employs some mercy, ensuring they are kept in servitude or that the tender age of children is spared. But nothing similar happened in the destruction of Jerusalem or **Bether**; <note>original: "Bitterensi"; Betar or Bether was the final stronghold of the Bar Kokhba revolt in 135 AD.</note> they perished to a man during the Passover. Six million people <note>original: "sexageties centena hominũ milia"</note> were counted and recorded—a number which God has scarcely permitted to be killed among wicked and idol-worshipping nations over many centuries. 

Truly, Jerusalem committed so great a sin that the whole world could not have committed a greater one; therefore she was turned backward. And so, He will no longer add to His mercy for you, but will bury you in eternal oblivion. It follows: *But I will have mercy on the house of Judah, and I will save them in the Lord their God, and I will not save them by the bow, and sword, etc.* The Lord speaks here—the Lord, I say, the Father and God of heaven and earth. And yet He will save the "True Judah" in the Lord their God—that is, in Christ Jesus the Messiah, who is both man and God. 

Thus it appears that "Judah" is the name used here for the **Christians** who truly confess God. They have come into great power and have been saved without war, without the bow, without the sword, without horses or horsemen. Instead, through the highest patience, innocence, piety, charity, and humility—and through deaths and torments—they have come to the highest glory and the majesty of all things. **Israel** "saw" God, but only saw Him; **Judah** saw Him and *confessed* Him. <note>Postel is playing on the medieval etymologies of the names: "Israel" was often interpreted as "the man who sees God," while "Judah" (Yehuda) relates to "confession" or "praise."</note> Not only in this place is "Israel" used for the rejection of the Jews, but the same sentiment is found in **Isaiah 49**, which says: *And now, says the Lord, who formed me from the womb to be a servant to Himself, that...*

He argues that the brutal Roman destructions of Jerusalem and Betar under Titus and Hadrian were divine punishments for the crucifixion of Christ, marking the end of God's mercy for the biological nation of Israel.</summary>

->## BOOK IV OF GUILLAUME POSTEL<-

...I will bring back Jacob to him, and Israel shall not be gathered. And I have been glorified in the eyes of the Lord, and my God has become my strength. <note>original: "reducam Iacob ad eum, & Israēl non congregabitur..." Postel is quoting Isaiah 49:5.</note> In this place, the Messiah speaks according to his humanity concerning the Father, who glorified him and was his strength, and placed him for the salvation of Judah and of all nations; and yet "Israel shall not be gathered," for there is a change from the preceding sentiment. For God had said: "You are my servant Israel, because in you I will be glorified." And I, says the Messiah, have labored in vain; without cause and uselessly I have consumed my strength; therefore my judgment is with the Lord, and my work is with my God. For Christ came unto his own, and his own did not receive him; and he did not merely labor in vain among them—for Israel was so far from believing in him that they even killed him with a most cruel death—wherefore he says his judgment and his work in Israel are "with God," that is, before the judgment of God the Father, by which he shall judge all men, he would not have his judgment and work accepted in Israel. 

And so, as if the prophet were retracting what he had said about him being a servant who was not to be, he said that "Israel shall not be gathered." As for what is written in the <term>Ticcun Sopherim</term> <note>These are "Corrections of the Scribes," traditional Masoretic notes on the Hebrew text.</note>—that is, the corrections of the scribes, or rather their corruptions and depravations—it is written as a <term>Keri and Ketiv</term> <note>A traditional Jewish scribal system noting a difference between the "written" word (Ketiv) and the "read" word (Keri).</note> that the word "not" <note>original Hebrew: "lo" (לא)</note> is written with an *aleph*, but read as "to him" <note>original Hebrew: "lo" (לו)</note> with a *vav*. This contradicts the sense of the prophet. For he had called him a servant before, and in the second place he wished to change the sentiment; for this reason he says, "and now." It is as if he were saying: "Then, indeed, when I first called you, you were my servant; but now, after the Messiah has labored between you and your people, I say certainly in vain that Israel shall not be gathered." 

Nevertheless, Christ called certain remnants and the dregs of the poor from among them, and made them most blessed, and in this they were like God, for they needed nothing and benefited everyone. But let us see if we read "to him" <note>Hebrew: לו (lo)</note> instead of "not" <note>Hebrew: לא (lo)</note>, what meaning results: it would surely have to be read, "and Israel shall be gathered to itself." See what a sentiment results from the corrupted scripture! If Israel is gathered "to itself," then it is not gathered to the Messiah. For he who acts for himself—that is, for his own benefit—does not act for a leader or a prince. Thus, the corrupters of the scriptures fall into <term>Scylla</term> while wishing to avoid <term>Charybdis</term> <note>A classical idiom meaning to fall into one danger while trying to escape another.</note>. For it makes absolutely no difference whether you say, "upon the coming of such a prince, that people will not be gathered by him," or if you say, "they will be gathered to themselves and not to him," for the subjection of that people will always be foreign to him. 

Indeed, the word *lo* <note>meaning "to him"</note> is spoken of the third person. But in this place Christ speaks for himself: thus it should have been said *li*, which means "to me," so that the sense would fit: "but Israel shall be gathered to me." Certainly, if it had ever been written *lo* with a *vav*, as they claim, they would have made another <term>Keri and Ketiv</term>, and from *lo* <note>לא (not)</note> they would have made *li* <note>לי (to me)</note>, since there is a far greater affinity between the letters *yod* and *vav* than between *aleph* and *vav*, which have nothing in common in their shape. How rightly Jeremiah said of those lost scribes: "How do you say, 'We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us'? Truly the lying pen of the scribes has worked a lie." <note>Jeremiah 8:8.</note> For those Scribes who existed after Jesus Christ, whenever they saw things that clearly convicted them and could be corrupted during transcription, they attempted to invert them all; and this is but one instance out of many. 

There is also another, most clearly betraying the cunning and wickedness of the scribes in Psalm 22, where it is written of Christ things which so perfectly match the fastening of his feet and hands that if the prophet had seen it present before him, he could not have described it more clearly. The place genuinely has it thus: <note>original Hebrew: כרו ידי ורגli / caru iadai ueraglai</note> "They pierced my hands and my feet." The scribes changed "they pierced" <note>Hebrew: כרו (kaaru)</note> into "like a lion" <note>Hebrew: כארי (kaari)</note>. But it helps to look deeper into the passage and weigh what precedes or follows it. Thus the prophet speaks of Christ when he was driven to the cross by a wicked nation: "I am poured out like water, and all my bones are scattered; my heart has become like melting wax in..."

...in the midst of me.
> My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue has cleaved to my jaws, and you have brought me down into the dust of death. For dogs have surrounded me; the council of the wicked has besieged me. They have pierced my hands and my feet; I might count all my bones. But they looked and stared upon me; they divided my garments among themselves, and upon my vesture they cast lots. <note>Postel is quoting Psalm 22:15-18 (Psalm 21 in the Vulgate). This passage is traditionally viewed by Christians as a direct prophecy of the Crucifixion.</note>

How perfectly this prophecy matches, word for word, the death and torments of the blessed Jesus Christ, I will not say now; it will be revealed in its proper place. It is agreed between both parties—however they may twist and corrupt it—that the Psalm is spoken by a person placed in great affliction, who complains in one continuous tone about his sufferings. Therefore, let even the most stiff-necked of the Jews judge how fittingly it would be said of a man weighed down by every affliction: "like a lion my hands and my feet." <note>original: "sicut leo manus meas..." Postel is critiquing the Hebrew Masoretic text which reads *ka’ari* ("like a lion") instead of the version found in the Septuagint and Vulgate, which suggests *karu* ("they pierced").</note> Or, in a direct sense, what affinity does a most fierce lion have with the hands and feet of a man so crushed by blows and torments that his bones, separated from their joints, can be numbered? What fierce spirit or anything else "lion-like" can square with such hands? Judge, you blind ones; judge whether these things can stand. And finally, detesting the wickedness of your rabbis, come to your senses. 

But the grace of the scribes' wickedness must be confirmed; one or two more passages must be added. Since they were most wicked in offering sacrifices, yet so they might not seem to provoke God, they corrupted the passage by which they were rebuked by the prophet. For where it was in the first chapter of Malachi:
> And you have polluted it, in that you say, "The table of the Lord is contaminated, and that which is placed upon it is contemptible to eat." And you said, "To what end is this labor?" and you have troubled me <note>The Hebrew word is *oti* (me).</note>, or thought me light, or puffed at me.

It was written thus of old. In this place, because they were treated badly—even while the business of sacrifice was flourishing—and were rebuked for mocking God, the scribes placed "it" <note>The Hebrew word *oto* (it/him).</note> in place of "me," <note>Postel is identifying another of the *Tikkun Sopherim* (Corrections of the Scribes), where a pronoun was allegedly changed to avoid describing God in a derogatory way.</note> as if by putting a <term>vau</term> <note>The Hebrew letter ו (Vav), often used as a suffix meaning "him" or "it".</note> in place of a <term>yod</term> <note>The Hebrew letter י (Yod), often used as a suffix meaning "me".</note> in the scriptures, there would no longer be any injury against God. This is noted by Rabbi Solomon <note>Rabbi Shlomo Itzhaki, known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval commentator.</note>, and he says it is one of the 15 words corrected and changed by the scribes. But now there are not fifteen, but five hundred; if they had dared to mark these in the letter as they do in the margin, nothing would have remained whole in the Bibles long ago. Likewise in the fourth chapter of Hosea, which pertains to your reprobation:
> My people are cut down because they had no knowledge; because you have rejected knowledge, I will reject you, so that you shall not perform the office of priesthood for me; and you have forgotten the law of your God, and I too will forget your children. According to their multitude, so they sinned against me; I will change my glory into ignominy. <note>Hosea 4:6-7.</note>

Beyond the fact that I must note the corrupted passage, I should not omit that they were more wicked as they became more numerous. For it says: "According to their multitude they sinned against me." This was evident under <term>Barcoziba</term> <note>Simon bar Kokhba, who led a major revolt against Rome (132–136 AD) and was hailed as a Messiah by some, including Rabbi Akiva. Postel views him as a "son of lies" (Bar Coziba).</note>. For in the whole world, in a place as narrow as Judea was before it was cut off forty years ago, four million people were never seen, much less killed. A little before that wickedness, in the times of Trajan, the Jews practiced such cruelty against the people of Cyrene that they were not satisfied with killing 220,000, but they girded themselves with the intestines of the slain, covered their heads with their skin, and even ate their hearts and flesh according to their lust, until 260,000 of them were killed. <note>Postel is recounting Roman historical accounts (like those of Cassius Dio) regarding the Kitos War, used here to demonstrate "wickedness."</note> God had already rejected the priesthood. 

But the corrupted passage reads thus: where formerly it was <term>kebodi</term> <note>Hebrew: כבודי (my glory).</note>, that is, "my glory," they put there <term>kebodam</term> <note>Hebrew: כבודם (their glory).</note>, that is, "their glory," so that they might change the sentence written by God, which they feel in fact. For there "Glory" (*Kabod*) is used for the people of the Israelites, as in many places. Thus the prophet asserted it would happen that He would change His glory—that is, He would love another people for His glory, having abandoned them. Lest God should do this, they thought they could do it by canceling His decree. O men destitute of sense, who even think they can deceive God! In the same sense they changed...

They changed <note>original: "mutauerunt"</note> the text in the second chapter of Jeremiah, using the same word and the same action. Similarly, they corrupted the eighth chapter of Ezekiel <note>original: "Iechechelis 8"</note> in this way: "Surely you have seen, O son of man. Is it a light thing to the house of Judah that they should commit these abominations which they commit here? For they have filled the land with iniquity and have turned to provoke me to anger; and behold, they apply the stench to their noses." It was once written, as the *Bereshit Rabbah* <note>A collection of ancient Jewish interpretations (Midrash) on the Book of Genesis. Postel cites it to prove that the text originally referred to God's nostrils, not the people's.</note> notes, "to *my* nostrils." Therefore, I will also act in fury; my eye shall not spare, nor will I have mercy; and though they cry to my ears with a loud voice, I will not hear them. The corrupted passage is obvious. For they were truly applying the stench of all their vices to the nostrils of the Lord, but they thought they could remove this by merely changing a word, and so they "applied the stench to their own noses." If that stench refers to sins, as it surely does, it cannot help but rise up to the nostrils of the Lord (if He were to have limbs)—that is, against and before His majesty. Thus, the meaning remains exactly the same, whether you like it or not, O scribes. For whoever sins in any way, at the very least, commits a grave offense against himself and God. If he harms a brother, he brings reproach to God, wickedness to himself, and injury to man. If the text spoke of a stench that could be pleasing to man but displeasing to God, or to both, why was such a great punishment inflicted upon you for it? Since the times of Simon the Just <note>A High Priest during the Second Temple period, legendary for his holiness.</note> and the holy ones, you have had no priest; from the time of the Maccabees, no king; and from the time of Christ, no prophecy. And yet, you have never ceased to cry out to the Lord, always praying and fasting, yet never ceasing to be afflicted for these full fifteen hundred years. Surely God is truthful. He promised you that He would not hear your prayers; the prophets foretold the present condition of your affairs. Meanwhile, by miserably deceiving you, the Rabbis refer all types of captivities back to Babylon, not noticing that God heard you from that place and brought you back. But the word of God must be entirely fulfilled, which He foretold in almost innumerable places: that at some time He would not hear you, would not gather you, would even reject you and not listen to your prayers. His word remains forever; He is truthful. If you believe His words, you must believe them to be true. The Israelites were to be driven away until the final judgment, for then they will be gathered with all the individual nations to be judged. For your Messiah was not going to permit you to suffer those calamities forever in this life. It is necessary, therefore, that while He reigns among other nations, you must suffer those evils which the truthful God willed to be foretold concerning you. For two times were promised to you: the time of the Law and the time of the glorious Messiah. Under the Law, it was impossible for you to be so rejected by God that He would never hear you. For otherwise, your Law would be evil, and from an evil author, if it were the cause of your misfortunes. You should have suffered much less under the law of the Messiah if you had believed in Him, because the law of Christ was to be of far greater perfection than the Mosaic law; otherwise, it would have been superfluous. But you keep the Law, as you say, and the law of the Messiah is not yet known to you, and yet you are to be forsaken by God. Thus it remains that you suffer these evils because of the killing of Jesus Christ and the neglect of His law, against which your *Nizzahon* <note>referring to *Sefer Nizzahon* (The Book of Victory), a famous Jewish polemical work against Christianity.</note> and certain others have dared to exercise a venomous tongue; you subscribe to these out of obstinacy rather than truth, because they applaud your vices. You shall have no other Messiah, O Jews, than the Antichrist, who will fight directly—just as you desire—against the law of Jesus Christ. This captivity of yours has already lasted since Christ was killed, as I said: from which your calamity took its origin, not to be ended before the Day of Judgment, except for a few years before that day in which you will join yourselves to the "Son of Perdition" <note>A biblical title for the Antichrist.</note>. Unless God had been most hostile to you, for all these miseries that have fallen upon you from every side, He would not have added such a famous argument of His wrath under Julian the Apostate <note>The Roman Emperor (reigned 361–363) who attempted to rebuild the Jewish Temple in Jerusalem to spite the Christians; the project failed due to fires and earthquakes, which Christians interpreted as divine intervention.</note>. For when your ancestors—to whom...

->ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD<-

<header>ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD</header>

<page-num>372</page-num>

Out of hatred for us [Christians], he <note>Referring to the Emperor Julian "the Apostate" (reigned 361–363 AD), who attempted to reverse the Christianization of the Roman Empire.</note> wished to please them, and so he granted them the opportunity to rebuild the Jerusalem Temple so that he might restore your nation. Mortar was tempered, stones were gathered, and materials were prepared in every way. Trenches were even excavated to lay the foundations. Suddenly, on the day before the first stone was to be laid, such a great earthquake arose that it overthrew not only the site of the temple but the greater part of Aelia <note>original: "Heliæ." Aelia Capitolina was the name given to Jerusalem by Emperor Hadrian.</note>, and especially all the porticoes, in which an innumerable multitude of the Jewish people, who had come from everywhere, perished. On the following day, a ball of fire came out from the workmen's hut during the daylight hours, which repeatedly wandered through the whole city and, returning again and again to the site, consumed as many Jews as it met. Many sought safety in flight, acting as messengers of such a great disaster. So that it would be clear to them that these things happened by the will of Christ and not by chance, all their clothes were imprinted with the sign of the cross in such a way that they could not be removed by any skill. When they saw all these things, almost all the Jews in the whole of Syria became Christians. This is written not only in our histories but also in the pagan histories. Your rabbis would not wish to reveal these things to you, lest you come to your senses.

I return for a short while to certain <term>corrections</term> <note>original: "ticun," referring to the *Tiqqune Sopherim* or "Corrections of the Scribes."</note>. What would the scribes not have dared to invert? Rabbi Akiva <note>original: "Atriba." Rabbi Akiva was a leading 2nd-century Jewish scholar.</note>, the "Light of Israel" as you believe—the greatest of your ten ancestors who were put to death by various tortures under Hadrian, and in whose memory you celebrate the fast of atonement on the tenth day of Tishrei <note>Yom Kippur.</note>—inverted the scriptures and read them in favor of Bar Kokhba <note>original: "Barcozibarum." Simon bar Kokhba led the Jewish revolt against Rome in 132–136 AD.</note>. Regarding what is written in Numbers 24, "A star shall rise out of Jacob," which is a passage concerning the coming of the Messiah, he asserted that it was written wrongly. Where it said *kokhav* <note>original: "cochab," the Hebrew word for star.</note>, he said it should be replaced with *kozav* <note>original: "cozab," meaning "lie." Akiva initially hailed Bar Kokhba as the Messiah (the "Son of the Star"), but after the revolt's failure, his name was often punned as Bar Koziba ("Son of the Lie").</note>; that is, "a lie" in place of "a star." You have this written in the book of *Ta'anit* <note>original: "Taamith," a tractate of the Talmud.</note>, in the chapter that begins "Three Chapters," and in the *Lamentations Rabbah* <note>original: "Echabati."</note>. That Messiah was worthy of your misfortune, both in deed and in name, because you have always preferred the false to the true.

But I wonder less that the scribes and doctors permitted themselves this in the Law of God, since they wished the same to be permitted even to servants. It is written in the Talmud, in the book *Yevamot* <note>original: "Iebamoth," a tractate on levirate marriage.</note>, in the chapter on heretics, that Rabbi Yochanan <note>original: "Iohanam."</note> said in the name of Rabbi Simeon: "It is good that you take away one letter from the Law, so that the name of heaven may be sanctified in public"—that is, it is good to overthrow the Law of God and its meaning to please men. Thus in Hosea 9, where it was written, "And my flesh from them," they wrote, "and when I depart from them," etc. Innumerable things have been corrupted and changed so that posterity might not recognize the truth.

But I return to the exposition of the first chapter of Hosea, from which I had digressed to the <term>corrections of the scribes</term> <note>original: "ticun sophrin."</note>. We have already noted two places where Israel shall not be gathered. There followed: "And she weaned her who is 'Without Mercy'" <note>Referring to the daughter of Hosea, *Lo-Ruhamah*.</note>. What is this "weaning"? It is a slaughter. For they were despoiled of the benefit of nature and the most excellent gift of God, which is life—as I said, around the 140th year from the birth of Christ—to the number of 1,860,000 <note>Postel lists "sexies decies centena 860,000," suggesting a massive death toll from the Bar Kokhba revolt.</note> Jewish people. Scarcely a tenth part survived, which embraced a holy life under the law of Christ; one may see the holiness of these people in the writings of your own countryman, Philo. 

The son born in the third place from the fornicating Jewish nation was called "Not My People" <note>Hosea's son, *Lo-Ammi*.</note>, because neither the Jews who have been born since the time of the destruction are the people of God, nor is God their God, even though they always occupy themselves with fasts and ceremonies. God is no more their God than he is the God of the gentiles and idolaters, because for as long as the law of Jesus Christ has endured—namely, for fifteen hundred years—they have been estranged from God, nor do they have a Republic, a miracle, or a prophet. With those people outlawed, the prophet now places the true Israel in the position of the false one. These are the Christians, innumerable throughout the whole world, who, where previously they were "not the people of God"—that is, outside the Holy Land—there they are called the people of God. They are the true seed of Abraham, surpassing the sand of the sea. With them, on the day of judgment, all the elect from the Jews and all nations shall be joined, and they shall ascend into heaven with Christ as their leader, and there shall be "one fold and one shepherd." <header>GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK IV.</header>

That great day of the seed of God. You have seen the tragedy of your unhappiness depicted to perfection <note>original: "ad unguem," literally 'to the fingernail'—a Latin idiom for precision or perfection</note>, and the sequence of events until the very end of the world. The false Israel will be alienated from God until the end of the world; the true Israel, following Christ and keeping His precepts, will live forever, without any concern for human affairs except insofar as they contribute to the glory of God, their own innocence, and the love of one's brother. Some trust in chariots, and others in horses, but we shall be glorified in the name of the Lord. <note>A reference to Psalm 20:7.</note> If the Messiah you expected was greater than Moses—as He certainly was (otherwise it would have been pointless for Him to have been promised by God for so long, unless He were better)—then He was going to give you a far more perfect state than you ever had before.

Yet, in terms of the kindness of the heavens or the earth, the abundance of resources, and every part of physical happiness, no nation was ever more fortunate than you were under the judges, David, and Solomon. For in the Books of Kings it is said that there was as great a supply of gold, silver, and gems as there was of dust or stones. If this is the highest good for you, then certainly Solomon was your Messiah, because under that king and his reign, nothing was ever more flourishing or abundant. Yet that same man, so wealthy, who had seen to it that riches from the whole world were brought into the Syrian world <note>Refers to the region of Greater Syria/Palestine, where Solomon's kingdom was centered</note>, wished to testify to you in a dedicated work <note>Refers to the Book of Ecclesiastes, traditionally attributed to Solomon</note> that in the abundance of wealth, gold, silver, provinces, power, and such things, beyond what is necessary for use, there is nothing other than vanity and affliction of spirit. He showed that fleeting mortals are tortured in vain so that they neglect heavenly things. Since these things are therefore empty, and cannot make a person blessed or satisfy them in every part, it remains that the blessedness promised by God cannot consist in them. For since God is the highest wisdom, He would not place the highest good in a most vain thing; wherefore it follows that the happiness promised to come under the Messiah was not subject to this luck and the vanity of corruptible things. The highest Giver must give something solid.

Therefore, the highest happiness in the whole world is of this kind: the contempt of all things for the love of God; to marvel at none of those things that the world considers supreme; as if having all things, yet possessing nothing; to be born for others, not for oneself; to rule over pleasure, to overthrow vices, and to avoid whatever fights against man's goal, and to follow what tends toward it. But Christ our God taught us all these things. From which it is clear that He and His prescriptions are the highest good in this life, and the way to the future one. Accept Him, therefore, O Israel, who has already been driven away from you by the fates; accept Christ. He is not angry with individuals; He wants the nation and the republic destroyed <note>Postel likely refers to the destruction of the Jewish state as a political entity, which he sees as a divine judgment</note>, but not the person. You have lived by His spirit, even though you have been without His religion. You will be victors, not as bloodthirsty men and destroyers of nature, most unlike God, but in all things as similar to Him as a man can achieve with God's blessing. The law is now different from when you entered the Holy Land. Then, a way had to be opened for religion by the sword; now, there is a need for the contempt of all things (except for God and one's brother). For he who restrains his appetite from things is far more perfect than he who is carried into lusts by all sorts of desires, often empty ones, which leave nothing to a man except torments and miseries.

The peasant who happens upon only the bread required by the laws of necessity is happier than a prince, or any glutton or gormandizer, who keeps himself and countless servants busy for the sake of a single throat; since they are equal in the condition of being born, using, and dying, except for the fact that he who has more squanders far more than he who has little. He has all things who has God as Father, who has himself desiring nothing, and who has every person as a brother. Both he who consumes little and he who does not fail to place every man in the position of a brother cannot be in want. But I wish to dwell a little longer on your rejection, so that you may completely set aside the false hope of a coming Messiah—in which your Rabbis falsely hold you—and turn to Jesus Christ before the day...

But the Jew will object: "If God hardens us, what can we do? We cannot resist." There is nothing in the prophets that is not filled with news of your dispersion. ...In your own traditions, in the <term>Seder Olam</term> <note>original: "Seden holam" — The "Order of the World," a 2nd-century CE Hebrew manual of chronology.</note> it is established (from the book <term>Yevamot</term>, <note>original: "Iebamot" — A tractate of the Talmud concerning levirate marriage.</note> in the chapter <margin>Chapter of the brothers' widows</margin> on brothers' widows) that the children of Israel entered and possessed the holy land twice, but that it is not permitted for them to return there a third time. Truly, if anyone wished to select all the passages regarding your rejection, it would be necessary to examine the whole of the sacred scripture, especially the prophetic books; one must come to the causes of such great evil, which have been declared so often. <margin>Isaiah Chapter 65</margin> **Isaiah Chapter 65**: 

> Because I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not hear, and you did evil in my eyes, and chose those things which I did not want: therefore thus says the Lord God, behold my servants shall eat and you shall be hungry, my servants shall drink and you shall be thirsty, my servants shall rejoice and you shall be confounded: behold my servants shall praise for joy of heart, and you shall cry for sorrow of heart, and shall howl for affliction of spirit, and you shall leave your name for a curse to my chosen ones, and the Lord God shall slay you, and call his servants by another name, and whoever blesses himself in that land shall bless himself in the true God, etc. 

All these things were spoken concerning the second calling, which was made by Jesus Christ. For if they were spoken of the calling made by Moses or the prophets, there was no other people of God under that law except Israel. For although God afflicted His people with various disasters and captivities, He never took up another nation in its place until the scribe and the leader failed from the thigh. <note>A reference to Genesis 49:10, a classic "proof text" used by Christians to argue that the Jewish right to rule ended when Christ arrived.</note> Therefore, it remains that this must necessarily be understood as being because they did not listen to Christ. For those who consented to His death paid the bitterest penalties; those who did not listen were dispersed. 

And then the name of **Christians** was made great and glorious because of their remarkable innocence, charity, and piety. But the name of **Jew** or **Israelite** became so shameful that even the pagans and those foreign to our religion can today hardly endure hearing the word "Jew" without resentment. 

The Christians, however, abound in a great plenty of things—not because of wealth, but because of sobriety and charity (I do not wish to have the lives of many individual Christians thrown back at me, since the Law itself is not at fault). If they abound, they abound for God; if they are in need, they are in need for God. For the whole aim of Christ is that God should be everything to us, that man should be content with necessities, thinking he possesses nothing, but rather tending toward the supreme good—God Himself—aiming with a direct gaze as if at a target. 

The Jews, with their Messiah, go about seeking empires, the slaughter of many men, famous victories, the most ample riches, the highest honors, and other vain things in which Satan plays with the present world. For them, their Messiah will not be enough unless he is a god. But in this place you ought to note carefully that we are called the **True Israel**, renamed as Christians, while your name has been exploded. I myself know what your condition is among the followers of Muhammad; certainly a dog is held in greater esteem than a Jew. Indeed, a Jew is exposed as prey to everyone. Thus is your name execrable and hateful. 

In this way, for fifteen hundred years now, God has been teaching you that His word is most true, and that you have changed the truth into a lie: that you not only failed to hear Christ, the true God and man, but you killed Him, and you chose the two **Bar-Kozibas** <note>original: "Barcozibas" — Referring to Simon bar Kokhba, the leader of the Jewish revolt against Rome (132–136 CE). Postel's mention of "two" likely refers to the father/son or general/imposter legends in medieval chronicles.</note>, those sons of lies, and made them your Messiahs. 

There is another reason: they thought the Messiah would be for the Jews alone, and that salvation was to be expected only from them. Therefore they object: "If the Messiah had come, Israel would have been gathered together." They see the whole world believing except for themselves, and yet they refuse to yield. He came first among them, but there—where He ought to have been received—He, the True One, was exposed to the impious and paid the penalty. That the death of Christ was the cause of the desolation, and that it preceded it, is testified through the Holy Spirit by Daniel, whom the rabbis place among the prophets in the book <term>Megillah</term>, <note>original: "Megilach" — A tractate of the Talmud concerning the festival of Purim.</note> in the chapter "The Megillah is Read." ...the street shall be restored, and the walls in a narrowness of times: and after sixty-two weeks Christ shall be slain, and not for himself, <note>original: "non sibi" — Postel interprets the Latin Vulgate's phrasing of Daniel 9:26 to mean the Messiah did not die for his own sins, but for the sins of others.</note> that is, not by his own fault, but by ours; not for his own sake, but for ours. And the people of the leader to come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary, and its end shall be devastation, and after the end of the war, a decreed or perpetual desolation. Moreover, he shall confirm a covenant with many for one week, and in the middle of that week the victim and the sacrifice shall fail, and because of the height of abominations everyone shall be astonished, and the desolation shall endure until the consummation and the end. Nothing can be brought forward more clearly than these words, which show the Messiah slain before the desolation. From the precept and edict for the rebuilding of the temple, which was published in the 30th year of the reign of **Artaxerxes Longimanus**, <note>Artaxerxes I, King of Persia (reigned 465–424 BCE), known as "Longimanus" or "Long-handed."</note> until the death of Christ, there are 62 ½ weeks. And from the death of Christ to the overturning of the second temple there are 7 ½ weeks. 

Or, as others calculate, from the 20th year of Longimanus to Alexander there are 132 years. From then to Christ, 322 years. If you add to these the 30 years of the life of Christ, there arise 484 years, or 69 weeks. In the middle of the seventieth week, Christ died, and then, with the true Victim arriving, the old one perished. However the matter stands, the 70 weeks of years are the 490 years of the duration of the second house <note>The Second Temple in Jerusalem.</note> and from the times of the captivity. Therefore, when Christ came, many hoped they might be able to see him about 50 years earlier. But he was unknown to all, because he sought nothing earthly, wished to possess nothing, and embraced no other sovereignty than that of blessed souls. For this reason, he was despised by everyone, because he did not savor earthly things. 

But the impious and treacherous rabbis prefer to call certain others "Messiahs" here in Daniel, rather than to acknowledge the true one. Yet the highest point of history is at stake because of this slain one, and the result is the eternal desolation of Jewish affairs: which ought not to be, unless the greatest offense against God—greater than any other—had been committed. If the tradition of the chapter **Helek** <note>original: "Helec" — Referring to the eleventh chapter of the Talmudic tractate Sanhedrin, which discusses the afterlife and the arrival of the Messiah.</note> is true, concerning the six thousand years—of which two thousand are without the law, two thousand are under the law, and two thousand are under the Messiah—how is it that fifteen hundred years have already slipped away from the Messiah himself? By this reasoning, barely five hundred years would remain for him; what could be more absurd? Indeed, with the Syrian state perishing, the law of Moses perished. Let them explain it as they will, the Messiah was certainly to be killed by them before the dispersion, as will be made clear in the Gospel prophecy. 

At one and the same time, a foreign king, <note>Herod the Great, who was of Idumean descent rather than Judean.</note> having killed all men of royal blood and removed all priests (except for a few who perceived he would reign), showed that what Jacob had said in his blessings concerning the future Messiah was fulfilled: namely, that he had come who was to be sent. Or, as <term>Kimchi</term> <note>David Kimchi (1160–1235), a prominent medieval Jewish biblical commentator and grammarian.</note> explains, "his son"—that is, the son of the virgin—when the scepter and the lawgiver had failed. For although the kingdom was taken away in the Babylonian captivity, nevertheless <term>Mechochechim</term>, <note>original: "Mechochechim" — From the Hebrew "Mechoqeqim," meaning lawgivers or governors.</note> that is, the legislators and wise interpreters of the law, were never lacking, nor were the prophets. For Jeremiah and Daniel were led there with many others. In addition, although the power of the scepter was removed for 70 years, the royal lineage was not slaughtered to the point of extinction as it was under Herod. At that time, the blessing upon the people in the name of **YHWH** <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter holy name of God in Hebrew.</note> ceased to be made. 

While **Simeon**, <note>Postel likely conflates Simeon the Just, a High Priest of the Second Temple period, with the Simeon of the Gospel of Luke who recognized the infant Jesus.</note> who had received Jesus himself as the Messiah at the purification, was administering the priesthood, the lot was still carried in the right hand. Upon his death, the eternal flame failed, and 49 years before the destruction of the temple, it was flickering. Simeon also predicted his own death, because every day a man clothed in white garments would enter the temple with him, visible only to him. But in the year he died, his companion entered with him clothed in a black garment. These things are in the **Talmud** in the book **Yoma**, in the chapter *The Lot and the Bowl*. <note>original: "טרף וקלש" — Transliterated as "Tarof ve-Kalush," referring to the methods of drawing lots in the Temple service described in Tractate Yoma.</note> The following are also there, word for word:

...the western lamp <note>original: "men uefpertinum" — Postel is continuing the sentence from the previous page, referring to the *ner ma'aravi* (Western Lamp) of the Temple Menorah. According to the Talmud, this lamp miraculously stayed lit, but began to fail forty years before the Temple's destruction.</note> was burning, and the gates of the temple were opening by themselves, until Rabban Yohanan the son of Zakkai <note>A primary Jewish sage of the late Second Temple era.</note> rebuked them, saying: "Temple, temple, why do you destroy yourself? For Zechariah prophesied of you in chapter 11, saying: *Open your doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may devour your cedars.* These things are from the Jerusalem Talmud. The prophecy of Zechariah is most clear. For the gates of the temple were constructed from the cedars of Lebanon, and the fire set by the soldiers of Vespasian and Titus 40 years after the death of Jesus Christ devoured those cedars and the other materials of the temple composed of the same wood. In innumerable places, as noted in *Genesis Rabbah*, <note>original: "Berefsit raba" — a classic midrashic collection of scriptural interpretations.</note> for forty years the council of the 71 judges sat outside the Chamber of Hewn Stone <note>original: "extra Gazit" — the *Lishkat HaGazit*, the official seat of the Sanhedrin within the Temple.</note> before the temple was destroyed. From there the judges, having been driven out, put sackcloth over their flesh and tore out their beards and hair, saying: "Woe to us, for the scepter of Judah has departed from us, and the Messiah, the son of David, has not yet come." <note>Postel cites this to show the rabbis recognized the timing of the Messiah’s arrival based on Genesis 49:10, even if they denied Jesus was He.</note>

Therefore, those judges, expelled from the Chamber of Hewn Stone where they handled capital cases, sat for 40 years in the "Shops," <note>original: "Hamith" — likely a variation of *Hanuth*, the market area where the Sanhedrin moved when they lost the power to impose the death penalty.</note> another place where they never again judged criminal cases. Let one read the tractate *Bava Batra*, <note>original: "Baba bathra"</note> the chapter "The Partners" <note>original: "Haſſutaphin"</note>; there, worthy of being read, will be found accounts of the removal of both judicial and royal power. How, after all the heads of the royal blood were killed, Herod preserved only Mariamne as his wife so that he might be called the heir of the royal House of the Hasmoneans <note>original: "Hafmonai"</note>—that is, the Maccabees, who were also called the *Heads of the Exile*, <note>original: "Raſſe galliot"</note> that is, the leaders of the captivity. However, when Mariamne, scorning the status of a slave, threw herself down by order of her husband, he saw to it that she was preserved at home for 7 years, pickled in spices and anointed, for the sake of retaining the royal inheritance. Indeed, after all the judges—whom they call by the honorable title of *Rabban*—were removed, he saved only one, whom the Talmud calls Bava ben Buta. <note>original: "Baba Ben bota"</note> Josephus, who agrees in reporting these things, calls him simply Bava. Although Bava had previously prophesied the kingdom for Herod, Herod nevertheless dug out his eyes while holding his children in prison. This lone survivor, Bava, could not choose fellow judges for himself from so great a senate, since they were not legitimately elected unless by five men from the fellowship. Furthermore, Herod chose others for the senate who would be dependent on him, even after the sacred books were removed. He appointed a foreigner, Ananelus, as High Priest, and changed both sacred and profane matters so that no traces of the ancient state of things might remain.

In the Babylonian Talmud, in the chapter "Seven Days," <note>original: "Sibeat Iamim" — referring to Tractate Yoma, which discusses the seven days of preparation for the High Priest.</note> it is read that 40 years before the overturning of the second temple, the ten miracles that used to happen in the temple failed. They can be read there. To this is added the saying of David: *We have not seen our signs, nor is there any prophet anymore.* <note>Postel cites Psalm 74:9.</note> Rabbi Moses the Preacher <note>original: "Moſes Hadarfan" — an 11th-century Jewish scholar from Narbonne.</note> explains that passage from the last chapter of Isaiah: *Before she travailed, she brought forth; and before her pain came, she was delivered of a man child. Who has heard such a thing? Who has seen such things?* He explains it this way: "Before he who would subjugate Israel into the final servitude was generated, the Redeemer was born." Do you see how everything agrees? Before Titus was born, the Messiah was born. Read concerning the Arab who, calling the Messiah prophetically "Menahem son of Hezekiah," <note>original: "Menahem filium Chiztriæ" — Menahem means "Comforter."</note> that is, "the Comforter, son of the strength of God," said he was born in Bethlehem of Judah. This tradition is in *Genesis Rabbah*, and even if spoken by a stranger, it is nonetheless consistent with the truth. Mention of it is also made in *Lamentations Rabbah*. <note>original: "Eca rabeti"</note> Truly, if Christ has not come, he is never to come, since he was to be born in Bethlehem, which is entirely destroyed. At least let Suetonius, a pagan <note>original: "ethnicus"</note> author, as much a stranger to you as to us, provide you with proof, writing thus: "An ancient and constant opinion," he says, "had spread throughout the whole Orient, that it was in the fates that at that time men proceeding from Judea would become masters of the world." <note>A famous quote from Suetonius' *Life of Vespasian*, often interpreted by Christians as a pagan recognition of the Messiah's coming.</note> The opinion was certain and constant at that time. He agrees with us and with your people regarding the time. However, he uses the insane interpretation of the Jews, seeking happiness and the highest good in these corruptible things after the manner of beasts...

-> # ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD # <-

...those who place their highest good in worldly things, judging from their own nature, believed the Son of God would be born to ruin the whole world so that one nation alone might enjoy luxuries and power. They were never able, or perhaps willing, to recognize his supreme humility and his kindness toward all; they could not accept one so humble once they had recognized him. And yet, as I taught from the beginning, even if Jesus Christ had been only a man, he would have appeared most like God by his works. Possessing absolutely nothing, he bestowed everything that was placed within him. For as I noted in the first book, regarding the merchants driven from the temple, if he had come to amass wealth, he could have acquired as much empire as he could travel through. Indeed, without any change, he could have been the arbiter of the whole world in a moment—just as he will be terrifying at his second coming to all those who despised him. Since they believed him to be the most excellent of mortals (even if they refuse to believe he is God), they should have judged his power not as similar to this or that tyrant or destroyer of the world, but as superior to all. What, then, does that dross of the world <note>original: "fex orbis" — a disparaging term for worldly wealth and material power</note> have to do with his dignity, in which a man no less than God might be occupied? Avarice has destroyed you, O Jews; stubbornness has destroyed you; the hatred of truth has destroyed you; the cunning of the rabbis <note>original: "rabinorum uafricies" — Postel frequently blames the Jewish leadership for what he perceives as a misinterpretation of the Messiah's role.</note> has destroyed you. One thing I dare to say: if God willed it, he could indeed bring the whole world under one empire in a single blink of an eye. However, he could not retain it for even an hour so long as the freedom of the will <term>libertas arbitrij: the theological concept of free will</term> remains. For since the heart of man is prone to evil from his youth, he cannot be restrained by any legal statutes—even in the presence of a prince and under threat of punishment—so that he obeys commands in all things. 

No clearer proof of this matter can be given than in yourselves. For when you saw the lightning, the flashes, the darkness, and the miracles of God's presence, and heard his voices, and could not bear the radiant face of your leader <note>Moses, whose face shone after descending from Mount Sinai (Exodus 34).</note>, you nevertheless dared to prefer a calf—procured at the great expense of your own gold—to God. Why should I mention the sedition of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram? <note>Biblical figures who led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron and were swallowed by the earth (Numbers 16).</note> The gaping maw of the earth remains even now as evidence of that punished crime. Nor was this vice found only among the wicked. Miriam sinned and was struck with leprosy; the Levites sinned. Unless God had stripped away your free will as if you were stones, he could not have bound you with a tighter rule than when he was present with Moses. What do you think you would have committed if you had been a hundred thousand paces away from that place, or if that divine food of manna had been lacking? 

Examples of human rashness are frequent. Hannibal, while living, lost as many lands as he had sought, even though he had joined the Spains, Italy, and part of the Gauls to Africa. Alexander the Macedonian was warned of the signs of rashness and human stubbornness by a most wise Indian. A dry ox-hide was brought before him; when Alexander pressed down on one edge, the other parts rose up; when he pressed in the middle, all the edges lifted. This taught by signs that only those things which are closest to power and correspond to it in proportion are truly subject; the rest are in constant motion. And although the great nobles do not immediately defect from a prince, they nevertheless crush their subjects with such extortions that a rebellion, if it does not come from the head, is stirred up by the plundered members.

What shall I say of that "Iron Scythian" <note>Postel refers to Tamerlane (Timur), the 14th-century Turco-Mongol conqueror known for his swift and brutal expansion across Asia.</note> who, a few years before our own century, subdued the most famous and fierce parts of Asia—Scythia, Iberia, Armenia, Persia, Media, Syria, and Asia Minor—in a very few years? Yet he met the same end for his empire as he did for his life. Let us look at the most celebrated power of the whole world: the Romans. As soon as they had obtained the greatest and most distant provinces, they began to labor under their own weight, nourishing both foreign and domestic fire, and having produced with great difficulty...

...to protect it, and losing it daily. But the Empire of the Messiah is eternal, and of his kingdom there shall be no end. Since this is most true, and the whole world must be submitted to him, it necessarily follows that his corporeal empire cannot be understood <note>Postel argues that if the Messiah's kingdom were merely physical and political, it could not be truly eternal or universal in a world of decay.</note>, but rather a jurisdiction over souls and piety throughout the whole world is owed to him. From a very rich king, Attalus <note>Attalus III, the last king of Pergamon (r. 138–133 BCE), who famously abdicated his interests in ruling to study botany and gardening, eventually bequeathing his kingdom to the Roman Republic.</note> became a simple countryman. Diocletian, though otherwise a most wicked man, preferred a private life to the empire. Tiberius used to say of the crown, if I remember correctly, whenever he received the ornaments of empire: "O crown, more unhappy than happy, you who carry so many cares within yourself alone!" Since the Messiah must be blessed in every respect and rule the whole universe forever until he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, he ought not to have been "blessed" with that brand of happiness which contains the greatest misery within itself. But you will object to me the shameful acts committed against Jesus by your people: for which I will provide an answer once I have brought forward the true cause of your present rejection and joined it to the previous arguments.

Amos <note>original: "Hamos"</note> in his second chapter speaks thus: "Thus says the Lord: For three crimes of Israel I will turn away, and for the fourth I will not turn away, because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for shoes." <note>Postel is quoting Amos 2:6.</note> The cause of this is the selling of Jesus Christ. Your more recent rabbis, as they pervert everything, explain this as the "accepting of persons" <term>acceptio personarum</term> <note>A legal term referring to judicial partiality or favoritism.</note> and the bias of judges in trials, as if that were the world's greatest crime. Others say it refers to the sale of Joseph by his brothers; but these sins, even joined together, would not be worthy of eternal exile and rejection, since the crime of the sold Joseph was expiated by the afflictions suffered in Egypt, as your more sensible interpreters agree. Indeed, while corruption in trials is a very great crime, much graver things can be committed. Therefore, homicides are punished far more severely everywhere among nations than thefts; and thefts, even when they seem to have a pretext (as among the powerful), although they are larger, are not thought to be the greatest crime because they are a sin against property <note>original: "in rem peccetur"</note>. Certainly, in the whole world, even among the wise, that disease of greed blinds judges, yet God does not adjudge perpetual punishments wherever these things happen—and they will happen constantly as long as the world lasts. God knows how to bait the powerful with the splendor of fleeting things so they may adorn themselves and their families with titles; He knows that a loss (though he who takes it away is most unjust) is sometimes usefully made, so that those whom the "love of having" had occupied might return to themselves. He knows how to give the greatest gains from those things we usually call "losses," since man's goal is not found in external things; both the prince and the peasant, or even the destitute man, can satisfy himself with what is necessary for use. That sin of Israel was far more grave, such that it deserved eternal exile. 

But our interpreter shall be the Emperor Hadrian, who explained this in a dialogue held with ten great men (as you call them). When, after Bar Kokhba <note>original: "Barcoziba," the leader of the Jewish revolt against Rome (132–136 CE).</note> was killed in Betar <note>original: "Bittera," the final fortress of the Bar Kokhba revolt.</note>, he had shut up ten men of great authority in Israel in prison, Caesar spoke thus to them: "Judge a just judgment in justice. If someone is found who has stolen a soul from his brother who is of the children of Israel, and has betrayed and sold him, what shall the penalty be?" They answered, saying, "That thief shall die." Caesar added and said: "And where are your fathers, who sold their brother? And you, therefore, receive the judgment of heaven upon..."

Others say it refers to the selling of Joseph by his brothers. Certainly, in the whole world, even among the prudent, that disease blinds judges; and yet God does not adjudge perpetual punishments wherever these things happen (and they will happen constantly as long as the world lasts). 

God knows that the splendor of fleeting things entices the great so that they may adorn themselves and their kin with brilliance and titles. He knows that a loss (even if he who takes it is most unjust) is sometimes made usefully, so that those who were occupied by the love of possessing might return to themselves. He knows that from those things which we are accustomed to call "losses," the greatest benefits are not infrequently given. Since a man's goal is not found in external things, both the prince and the peasant, or the destitute, can satisfy themselves through necessary use. That sin of Israel must have been far more serious to merit an eternal exile.

you. If they themselves were alive, I would bring their judgment before you. You, therefore, shall bear the iniquity of your fathers. Who could persuade himself that a wise and sensible man would want to avenge a crime already buried in almost eternal memory upon men who were innocent of that crime and possessed great authority? 

The crime he was avenging was recent, which the fathers of these men had truly committed. The living body of Joseph was sold so that he might live in Egypt; but Christ Jesus was sold so that he might die on the cross. These ten men <note>The "Ten Martyrs," a group of ten rabbis whose execution is a central theme in Jewish liturgical poetry (the *Eleh Ezkerah*).</note> assented to the death and sale of Jesus Christ, for by following the most cruel persecutions against Christians, they brought help and provided counsel to a false prophet born for the ruin of the nation. 

Although Aelius Hadrian was not a Christian, he was nevertheless not a stranger to Christ; he honored Christ's image in his private shrine along with Abraham and many others. Certainly, if the faction of the priests of idols had not been so great, he would have openly professed the Christian faith through baptism. He, therefore, was the genuine interpreter of the passage written in Amos <note>original: "Hamos." Referencing Amos 2:6: "they sold the righteous for silver."</note>. For although the sons of Israel sinned by selling their brother Joseph, they could not yet be held by a law that was hardly given until two hundred years later. And no law punishes past crimes unless it is admitted by the one who promulgated it. Do you not judge from these things and those said before that you have fallen into a reprobate sense? Thus, you prefer to stand by the opinions of four or five modern, nefarious scoundrels and neglect your ancient interpreters rather than embrace the truth. Read, you wretched people, read the prophets, weighing what you have committed against Christ. Ponder the 7th chapter of Ezekiel. Because of your perverse judgment against Christ, you suffer these things, as the prophet says there: "nor will he spare you." But I have pursued this argument of reprobation long enough. For I shall persist in it everywhere, since mention of it is never lacking.

## THE OBJECTIONS OF CERTAIN MODERN
->*Jews, and their solutions.*<-

I do not know what I should approach first in this place, or which objections I should encounter first, since the modern <note>original: "neotericorum," referring to contemporary Jewish commentators of the 16th century.</note> interpreters contain nothing in themselves but solid errors and inversions of the Holy Scripture. First, therefore, I will take up and explode those things which seem to run counter to this so lengthy captivity and reprobation. However, so that all things may be clear, the matters under discussion must be gathered into certain main headings, so that it may be seen whence the hallucination occurred in Israel. There are three conditions of things to be considered from the creation of the world until its end:
